title: Efton Chism III’s amazing one-handed TD catch might have saved the Patriots’ season
description: The NFL’s best catch this season came from a totally anonymous wide receiver.
fullText:
Drake Maye has been absolutely dreadful to start the 2026 season to follow a breakout second season that almost earned him league MVP. Maye and the New England Patriots badly needed a win over Buffalo Bills in Week 4 to build some positive momentum and avoid a 1-3 start. Maye played by far his best game of the season, and he gave the Patriots a chance to win by hooking up with wide receiver Efton Chism III for a clutch fourth quarter touchdown.

With the Bills leading by five points late in the fourth quarter, Maye rolled to his right and flung the ball to the end zone. Chism seemed to be held by Buffalo's defensive back when the ball was in the air, but that didn't stop him from extended his free arm to make an incredible one-handed catch to take the lead. New England picked off Josh Allen on the next possession, and the Patriots earned the win they were desperate to get.

Did Chism make the best catch of the year so far? I think so given the stakes. Apologies to Keon Coleman, who also made an amazing catch in this game, but this is at least the catch of the week. Watch Chism's grab here:

ARE YOU EFTON KIDDING ME!!!!!!!

📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/dRQyU4Vbca

Chism was an undrafted free agent in 2025 who only had five career catches coming into this week. Chism entered the game with two catches for -1 yard on the season. A receiver with this small of a footprint making arguably the best catch of the season, and one that delivered New England a victory at that, is a truly special moment.

Maye will get the credit for leading the Patriots to a bounce-back win against an elite team, but it doesn't happen without Chism making this ridiculous and amazing play for his QB. The NFL never ceases to surprise us.

title: “Novak Djokovic Could Be 68 & Still Beat Alexander Zverev” – Fans React To German’s Shock Loss To Serb At China Open
description: Fans have taken a dig at Alexander Zverev following his quarterfinal loss to Novak Djokovic at the China Open, with some questioning the German’s form. Zverev opened his China Open campaign with a win over Cameron Norrie before defeating Juncheng Shang in the round of 16.
fullText:
Fans have taken a dig at Alexander Zverev following his quarterfinal loss to Novak Djokovic at the China Open, with some questioning the German's form.

Zverev opened his China Open campaign with a win over Cameron Norrie before defeating Juncheng Shang in the round of 16. However, the top seed suffered a 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 loss to Djokovic on Sunday at the Capital Group Diamond Court. He took the opening set but was unable to maintain his advantage as Djokovic fought back to win the next two sets. The match lasted two hours and 35 minutes, with Djokovic advancing to the semifinals.

Following the defeat, some fans criticized Zverev's performances against the sport's biggest names and questioned his two Grand Slam victories this season. One fan on X wrote:

"Djokovic could be 68 and he'd still beat Zverev 🤣"

Taking a hit at his two Grand Slam wins, another user wrote:

"Zverev is truly the worst Grand Slam winner in history—he won 2 the easy way and can't even beat a 40-year-old player 💔😭😭😭😭" (Translated from Portuguese)

Another fan called Zverev "lucky" for winning the French Open and US Open:

Along similar lines, a few other fans chimed in:

The match also featured a bizarre moment involving a courtside advertising board early in the opening set. After Zverev missed a forehand, he requested a video review, claiming that the LED advertising display had changed during his service motion.

The review confirmed that the advertising board had changed, and chair umpire Adel Nour ruled that the point should be replayed. Djokovic was visibly frustrated by the decision and argued that Zverev should have stopped play immediately rather than continuing the point and then requesting a review after missing the shot.

During his pre-tournament press conference on Sept. 30, Alexander Zverev was asked about the battle for the No. 1 ranking and how much of a goal it was for him. The German acknowledged that reaching the top spot was an ambition but said his main focus was on controlling what he could on the court.

"I think it's a goal for anyone. I think in the beginning of the season everybody expected that battle to be between Carlos and Jannik, so I'm very pleased that I'm in that conversation. Of course, yeah, there's some of it in my head. Again, I think I've said it so many times this year, the only thing that I can control is play good tennis, play well on the court, try to feel well on the court, try to do everything I can to prepare myself to play good tennis," said Alexander Zverev.

"Everything else will fall into place. Yeah, in my control, out of my control. There's certain factors there, as well. So yeah, I'm just going to try to focus to win the matches that I can."

Alexander Zverev had a major opportunity to close the gap on Jannik Sinner after the Italian withdrew from the Shanghai Masters because of a lingering knee injury. However, his loss to Djokovic in Beijing means he will not maximize his points haul at the China Open. He can still challenge for the World No. 1 ranking in Shanghai, where Sinner's absence leaves the race open.

title: Cowboys' touchdown with 40 seconds left beats Texans 34-30
description: CeeDee Lamb's 17th reception from Dak Prescott was the game-winner.
fullText:
The Cowboys needed a win Sunday. The Texans needed a win Sunday.

Dallas beat Houston in a battle down I-45, as Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb tore up the Texans defense in the second half. The Cowboys improved to 2-2, while the Texans fell to 0-4.

The Cowboys had 121 yards in the first half and trailed the Texans 16-6. They had only two field goals and missed two others from 60-plus yards. The Cowboys finished with 399 yards in one of the most exciting second halves of any NFL game this season.

Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown, a 12-yarder to Lamb with 40 seconds left for the game-winner. Houston had no answer for Lamb, who caught 17 passes for 189 yards.

George Pickens had two big catches for 75 yards.

Cowboys running back Javonte Williams had 19 carries for 62 yards and three touchdowns.

KaVontae Turpin had kickoff returns of 48 and 32 in the second half.

The Texans gained 397 yards but couldn't keep up with the Cowboys in the second half. C.J. Stroud's Hail Mary fell incomplete on the final play.

Stroud went 21-of-31 for 347 yards and two touchdowns, with Nico Collins catching seven passes for 118 yards and both touchdowns. David Montgomery ran for only 24 yards on 10 carries as the Texans' problems in the run game continued.

title: Barcelona star Joao Cancelo scores another banger for Portugal vs Norway
description: What an effort!
fullText:
Joao Cancelo is making a habit of scoring spectacular goals and was at it again on Sunday night in the Nations League for Portugal against Norway.

The Barcelona defender struck a ferocious effort on 38 minutes to make it 1-1 after the visitors had gone ahead through Kristoffer Ajer.

A long throw from Portugal found Cancelo lurking on the edge of the area, with the Barcelona star connecting sweetly with the ball to arrow a fierce effort into the top corner.

João Cancelo is scoring worldies for Portugal just like he’s doing for Barcelona 🔥

We're getting used to these stunners now 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/Iz6khtL3Yg

The goal is Cancelo's second for Portugal during the current international break and comes just days after the full-back won La Liga's Goal of the Month award.

The Barcelona defender claimed the prize for his spectacular effort against Racing in September that came as part of a 7-2 victory.

Sunday's match is Cancelo's last with Portugal before he returns to Barcelona to begin preparations for the resumption of the Liga season and a clash with Getafe.

title: NY Giants' walk-off interception for TD seals wild win over Cardinals
description: Deonte Banks' interception for TD as time expires seals NY Giants win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.
fullText:
EAST RUTHERFORD - The New York Giants are still searching for an identity, and with everything that has happened over the first month of the season, that's likely going to continue for the foreseeable future.

One thing's for certain: they going to scrap. They're going to fight.

And under John Harbaugh, the Giants (3-1) are showing they might just be becoming winners again.

Deonte Banks picked off Jacoby Brissett and returned it 98 yards for the ultimate Pick 6, ending Sunday's game in thrilling fashion and sealing a 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium.

Jameis Winston threw for three touchdowns, including the first 100-yard receiving game for Malik Nabers since Week 2 of last season, and the Giants' defense responded with an interception in their own end zone - and at the goal line - with the game on the line. Winston has won back-to-back starts for the first time since 2021.

And with the Philadelphia Eagles' loss on Sunday, the Giants stand alone in first place of the NFC East.

Last week, the Tennessee Titans were driving for the potential game-winning touchdown when Jevon Holland intercepted Cam Ward in the end zone, setting off a celebration inside MetLife. This time, Brissett and the Cardinals took possession with 2:06 left on their own 33.

Like Tennessee, Arizona needed a touchdown, and got an 18-yard defensive penalty to put them at the 4-yard line.

In the shadow of their own end zone, needing to defend those four yards, the Giants managed to force three incompletions by Brissett, including pass breakups by Dru Phillips and Banks.

That set up one final play with 11 seconds left, and Brissett looked to his left to Michael Wilson. Banks was in great coverage at the goal line, he jumped the route and took off the opposite way for what is the biggest play of his career.

The Giants have won their first three games at home for the first time since MetLife Stadium opened, and they last accomplished the feat in 2009 - the final season for the old Giants Stadium.

On a day when the Giants honored the 40-year anniversary of their Super Bowl XXI championship team, the Giants showed grit and the ability to deliver in the clutch yet again.

title: A dominant Inter beats Como Women 2-0 with goals from Vilhjálmsdóttir and Bugeja
description: Two wins from two, four goals scored and none conceded. Inter Women’s excellent start to the season continued with a second successive league victory, as goals from Vilhjálmsdóttir and Bugeja secu...
fullText:
Two wins from two, four goals scored and none conceded. Inter Women's excellent start to the season continued with a second successive league victory, as goals from Vilhjálmsdóttir and Bugeja secured a 2-0 win over Como Women at the Mino Favini in Meda. It was a performance full of character and quality from the Nerazzurre following their midweek Champions League clash with Austria Wien. Sassarini's side were positive, well organised and determined throughout, eventually making their superiority count with two goals in an intense second half. Vilhjálmsdóttir opened the scoring from the penalty spot before Bugeja added the second. In between, Vilhjálmsdóttir missed another penalty and Bugeja struck the post, further underlining Inter's attacking threat. The Nerazzurre move to six points in the table and bring the first run of fixtures before the international break to a perfect close.

The sun was beginning to set on the first Sunday of October as the game got underway. Both sides looked to build from the back and combine quickly on the ground, but the intensity of the contest made clean execution difficult at either end. Inter gradually took control. Sassarini's side pressed aggressively, won the ball back well and created a number of promising situations as they searched for the breakthrough. The first real scare came through Raphino, who turned brilliantly in a tight space inside the box before sending a left-footed effort narrowly wide. The Nerazzurre found plenty of joy down the right, with Glionna heavily involved. She went close twice, first after winning the ball high up the pitch and curling a left-footed shot just past Gilardi's right-hand post, then with a right-footed volley from a corner that flew over the bar. Despite their territorial dominance, Inter were unable to find the opening goal before the break. Como Women looked to threaten on the counter, but without creating any clear chances to trouble Rúnarsdóttir.

Inter continued to dictate the game after the break, with Sassarini turning to his bench and introducing Bugeja, Payne and Bartoli to add fresh energy. The breakthrough arrived in the 59th minute. Glionna once again met a corner with a volley at the far post, and the ball struck Berardi's arm. Following an FVS review, Inter were awarded a penalty, which Vilhjálmsdóttir converted emphatically, sending a right-footed finish across Gilardi for her second goal of the season. Como Women struggled to respond and the Nerazzurre kept pushing, although the hosts did threaten briefly when Simonetti's long-range effort flew narrowly wide. Inter raised the intensity again as they looked to put the game beyond doubt and won a second penalty in the 77th minute, once more for handball from a corner as Borbye blocked Raphino's header with her arm. This time, however, Gilardi kept out Vilhjálmsdóttir's spot-kick. Sassarini's side were undeterred and continued to pour forward in search of a second. Bugeja hit the post at the end of a huge double chance, a warning of what was to come just moments later. In the 83rd minute, the Malta international got the goal her performance deserved. A superb, fast-flowing move was opened up by an excellent through ball from Glionna, and Bugeja finished right-footed past Gilardi, with the ball going in off the post. Inter comfortably managed their two-goal advantage through ten minutes of added time to seal a second successive league victory and another clean sheet. The Nerazzurre will return to action on 18 October, when they host Parma.

title: Baltimore Ravens stuff Tennessee Titans in Derrick Henry reunion
description: The Tennessee Titans largely limited their former star running back Derrick Henry. But overall, it didn't matter in a loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Oct. 4.
fullText:
BALTIMORE — Derrick Henry didn't exactly run the ball down his old team's throat.

That might be all the comfort the Tennessee Titans took away from their 24-18 loss against the Baltimore Ravens on Oct. 4 at M&T Bank Stadium.

Henry rushed for 73 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in his first meeting against Tennessee, which fell to 0-4 for the second consecutive season and fourth time since 1997.

The Titans were scoreless in the second half until their final touchdown with under two minutes in the fourth quarter, and the Ravens (3-1) recovered an onside kick to seal it.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, who left the game with an ankle injury at intermission, needed one half to sink the Titans, throwing for 222 yards and two touchdowns as Baltimore (3-1) built a three-score lead that the Titans ultimately didn't overcome.

Titans first-year coach Robert Saleh — who remains searching for his first victory in Nashville — watched his team for the third consecutive week miss opportunities to snap what's now a six-game losing streak dating back to last season.

Titans quarterback Cam Ward finished 20-of-31 passing for 222 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

The Titans had the ball for nearly a minute longer than Balti

And yet the Titans trailed 24-7 after Baltimore kicker Tyler Loop hit the second-longest field goal in Ravens history, a 64-yard make through drizzly air as time expired in the first half.

The Titans' two first-half turnovers created a 14-point swing.

Tennessee gave the ball away within the game's first minute for the second straight week when Ward's forward lateral deflected off running back Tony Pollard's hands, directly to Baltimore linebacker Trenton Simpson for an interception.

Five plays later, Henry plowed Titans safety Kevin Winston Jr. into the end zone for a 5-yard touchdown and the Ravens led 7-0 with 12:09 in the first quarter.

The Titans missed a chance to cut the deficit to one score late in the first half. The Titans were driving past midfield when Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton stripped the ball away from receiver Carnell Tate after a 32-yard pickup.

The Titans' third-down defense was good in the first half, getting off the field on 3-of-4 chances.

But Jackson led crushing drives of 81 and 98 yards and the Ravens were perfect in the red zone by halftime.

Baltimore shredded Tennessee's defense on the 81-yard drive to start the second quarter, needing six plays to score. The Ravens went up 14-7 with 12:16 until halftime when Zay Flowers raced past linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. and extended his arms for a short pass that went for a 19-yard touchdown.

Along the way, Baltimore added heavy doses of Henry, who averaged 6.6 yards per carry on his first six touches.

Tennessee squandered a scoring chance from fourth-and-goal from the Ravens' 2-yard line in the second quarter. Pollard took a direct snap and was stuffed at the line on his fourth straight carry from inside the 8-yard line.

Jackson hit a wide-open Mark Andrews for a 3-yard touchdown on the next series to go up 21-7 after a dominant 98-yard drive.

Tennessee's response to the early interception was encouraging.

After the turnover, Ward led a 10-play, 70-yard drive that lasted 6:13 and ended with Pollard's 3-yard TD to tie it at 7-7.

Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach him at tpalmateer@tennessean.com and on the X platform, @tpalmateer83.

title: Should Aston Villa Hijack Tottenham’s Transfer Plans For This €40m Rated Striker?
description: Aston Villa could face competition from Tottenham Hotspur for Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis, who reportedly wants to fulfil his ambition of playing in the Premier League. According to Portuguese n...
fullText:
Aston Villa could face competition from Tottenham Hotspur for Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis, who reportedly wants to fulfil his ambition of playing in the Premier League. According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, via Sport Witness, the Greek international remains interested in English football and would welcome an opportunity to leave Lisbon if Benfica approve his departure.

Pavlidis hasn't forced an exit, though. The 27-year-old continues to perform professionally for Benfica, but his preference for a Premier League move could become relevant if an interested club submits an acceptable offer.

Benfica previously placed a €40 million valuation on the forward despite his €100 million release clause. Several major European clubs explored opportunities during the previous transfer window, including Barcelona, AC Milan, Juventus and Beşiktaş. However, those approaches failed to produce an agreement.

Marco Silva considered Pavlidis an important part of his plans and made retaining the striker a priority. Consequently, Benfica refused to sanction his departure despite interest from several established European sides.

His performances explain that resistance. Pavlidis registered 30 goals during his previous campaign and has already recorded 14 goals and three assists this season. Those numbers give interested clubs a clear indication of his finishing ability and attacking contribution.

Tottenham's interest could develop into something more concrete. A Spurs scout reportedly watched him during Benfica's meeting with FC Porto, suggesting that the London club continues to assess his performances.

LISBON, PORTUGAL – JULY 30: Vangelis Pavlidis of SL Benfica in action during the UEFA Europa League Qualifier match between SL Benfica and St. Gallen at Estadio da Luz on July 30, 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. (Photo by Gualter Fatia/Getty Images)

Aston Villa have several attacking options, including Nicolas Jackson, Tammy Abraham and young Brian Madjo. That competition could discourage Unai Emery from pursuing another centre-forward, particularly if his existing players remain available.

However, squad numbers don't always tell the complete story. Jackson's fitness, Abraham's performances and Madjo's development will influence Emery's recruitment decisions. Pavlidis offers considerably more established goalscoring experience than a teenage prospect, although signing another senior striker could restrict opportunities elsewhere.

Tottenham could have a clearer opening if Richarlison leaves after falling outside Roberto De Zerbi's plans. Pavlidis would then compete with Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush for attacking responsibilities.

My opinion? Aston Villa shouldn't dismiss this opportunity, but they must establish their actual requirements before entering negotiations. Jackson deserves an opportunity to establish himself, while Abraham and Madjo need clarity about their positions.

Spending €40 million on Pavlidis makes little sense unless Emery identifies a genuine need for another starting striker. Tottenham currently appear better positioned to explore the transfer, while Villa should monitor developments without committing significant resources prematurely.

title: ‘The brain isn’t there anymore’: Joe Burrow faces criticism after game-changing interception
description: Cincinnati Bengals superstar quarterback Joe Burrow faced some heavy criticism last week after a stat surfaced highlighting his failures in clutch moments. Unfortunately, he did not exactly bounce back the way he, the Bengals, and the fans would have expected, leading to more criticism. During Sunday’s showdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Burrow faced some heavy…
fullText:
Cincinnati Bengals superstar quarterback Joe Burrow faced some heavy criticism last week after a stat surfaced highlighting his failures in clutch moments. Unfortunately, he did not exactly bounce back the way he, the Bengals, and the fans would have expected, leading to more criticism.

During Sunday's showdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Burrow faced some heavy criticism as he threw two interceptions in a loss, including one ugly red zone interception on 1st and goal with a chance to put the Bengals on top.

With the Cincinnati defense playing a strong game and keeping the Jaguars out of the end zone for much of the afternoon, Burrow and the Bengals had plenty of chances to put up points of their own. Unfortunately, Burrow made a few costly mistakes.

Burrow's first interception of the game came late in the second quarter when Burrow was hit as he released a third-down pass. The ball sailed and was picked off

The second interception, however, was far worse.

The @Jaguars pick off Joe Burrow in the red zone!

CBS | Paramount+ https://t.co/tX0jOZymNT

— NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026

Trailing 16-10 in the fourth quarter, Bengals found themselves 1st and goal inside the Jacksonville 10-yard line with a chance to take the lead in the game with a touchdown. Unfortunately, Burrow tried to force a late pass to the middle of the field, where it was intercepted.

It's also worth noting that Burrow threw another interception in the first half, but it was negated by a roughing the passer penalty.

Needless to say, the play led to a lot of criticism on social media.

"Joe Burrow has made too many costly mistakes today. First INT he was hit so I can excuse it. This one right here was just egregious. Bengals defense has been doing it's job. At some point Joe Burrow has to do his," wrote Joel Moran of the Pick a Side podcast.

"Joe Burrow just isn't Joe Burrow anymore. Panicky. The brain isn't there anymore," wrote Cincinnati sports outlet Nati Sports.

"And that Joe Burrow interception just cannot happen," wrote James Rapien of BengalsTalk.com.

"Joe Burrow throwing meatball subs," wrote SleeperNFL of his interceptions.

"Well there's no defending Joe Burrow on that one," wrote Jake Liscow of the Locked On Bengals.

"Very Joe Burrow to be playing incredible and then throw the worst INT you've ever seen in your life," wrote longtime NFL analyst Willie Lutz.

We'll have to see how Burrow bounces back from this.

title: How Sullivan, Hall Have Turned Heads With U.S. Men’s National Team
description: Two teenagers - Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall - continued to stand out for the U.S. Men's National Team in its 3-0 victory over Mexico in an international friendly on Saturday night.
fullText:
Three games into Mauricio Pochettino's second tenure as U.S. Men's National Team head coach, life could not be much better for the side.

The Americans have won three consecutive matches.

Their success with a 4-1 victory over Peru on Sept. 26. It continued with a 4-2 win past Chile. And then it hit a high note with a resounding 3-0 triumph over archrival Mexico on Saturday, Oct. 3. The USA hosts Canada in the final match of their rare four-game friendlies in St. Paul, Minn., on Tuesday night.

Beyond the impressive results have been the performances of several teenagers who have gotten their collective feet wet in international soccer.

Two teens produced some history at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz.

Forward Julian Hall, 18, scored to give the U.S. a 1-0 first-half lead against the Mexicans. The New York Red Bulls forward became the third player in USMNT history to score in his first three appearances. He also became the youngest player to accomplish that feat.

Midfielder Cavan Sullivan, 17, became the youngest player to score for the men's national side in the final half, five days after celebrating his 17th birthday on Sept. 28.

"I think it's a fantastic problem for us," Pochettino was quoted by ESPN.com about his young players. "I think we will take the right decision in the right moment, but I think it's a very good problem to see.

"Now it's not a moment at all, but yes, we appreciate that situation and of course hope that we will be in that situation that young players perform in the way that they deserve to be with us."

Why USMNT Coach Pochettino Is Doing Some Forward Thinking

Sullivan, named Major League Soccer's Player of the Month for September, has been highly touted as the next big thing on the national team. The Philadelphia Union midfielder's overall play with the USMNT was impressive in these matches, but he didn't score a goal. He remedied that in the 63rd minute.

He intercepted a horrible clearance by Mexican goalkeeper Raul Rangel before lofting an uncontested 34-yard shot into the net for a two-goal lead. Teammate Mathis Albert, who scored earlier in the week, held the record at 17 years and 131 days.

"I remember pressing the goalie," Sullivan told TNT Sports. "I remember I probably shouldn't press the goalie. It felt like there was not really anybody pressing behind me. But that's why you put the work in, and I was rewarded for doing so. From there, it was sort of a blackout. I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn't hit the crossbar or go over. I kid you not. I was getting nervous when it was in the air. And then, t's a blur. Knee slide. My knees hurt. I'm really happy that the guys ran down and celebrated with me."

Why USMNT Coach Pochettino Decided On A Fresh Start With Youngsters

Pochettino loved what he had seen.

"I think he's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession," Pochettino said, according to ESPN.com. "He's a fighter, he's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player with a tremendous quality.

"And then I think Cavan showed in possession with the ball on the field [and] when he need to be chasing people and recover the ball. That is my impression after maybe three weeks together. And that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it's a fantastic news for USA. Hope that continues in that way."

Hall, who bolted off to a quick start with the Red Bulls by scoring nine goals before the 2026 FIFA World Cup break, went into a personal 12-game scoreless streak. He recently rediscovered his scoring touch in Major League Soccer and has continued it with the national team.

On Saturday night, the Manhattan, N.Y. native continued his scoring onslaught to give the hosts the lead in the 28th minute.

Gio Reyna beat his man down the right flank. Just as he was about to run over the end line, Reyna sent the ball toward the net. Goalkeeper Raul Rangel, who produced four clean sheets in the World Cup, could not handle it. An alert Hall made El Tri pay by tapping the ball into the net from point-blank range.

"I mean, three goals in three games is not bad for a striker, especially in your first three games in the national team," Reyna was quoted by FoxSports.com. "He sort of has that eye for goal."

After he did damage against Chile on Tuesday, Hall talked about his experience.

"It's been amazing to share the field with some amazing players," Hall said on the TNT post-game show. "They put me in the right spots, and I'm just doing as much as I can to put them away."

Hall praised Red Bulls head coach Michael Bradley for helping him and USMNT and club teammate, 17-year-old midfielder Adri Mehmeti, for their development this MLS season.

"It's been amazing," he said. "We have a lot of young guys on our team, including Adri. He's helped us so much in our development. He's a big reason as to why me and him are here right now. So, he's been amazing. He gave us amazing advice before we got here, and he's been awesome."

Vozinha's Amazing Legend Keeps Growing With Yashin Nomination

After the win over Mexico, Pochettino talked about not rushing the burgeoning stars of the next generation of USMNT players.

But Hall's performances might open the door for him to be a part of the U.S. squad when it plays a home-and-home series in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals in November.

"It's a fantastic problem for us," Pochettino told FoxSports.com's Doug McIntyre when he asked if the performances of Hall and the other youngsters might alter their plans.

Most national team coaches live for "problems" like that.

Why Emma Hayes Wants USWNT To Play Top-Ranked Spain

Michael Lewis, the sixth recipient of the Clay Berling Media Career of Excellence Award in 2025, can be followed on X an Bluesky at @Soccerwriter. His 10th soccer book, Around the World Cup in 40 Years: An American sportswriter's perspective, has been published.

title: With Aaron Judge sidelined, Yankees' next generation takes over October
description: The Yankees are leaning on homegrown stars such as Ben Rice and Cam Schlittler in October as Aaron Judge remains out with a calf injury.
fullText:
Three summers ago, George Lombard Jr. was a high school shortstop in Miami. Now he's 21, playing shortstop in October and part of the reason the New York Yankees still believe they can get past the Tampa Bay Rays.

The Rays won Game 1 of the American League division series 1-0 on Saturday. Drew Rasmussen struck out 10 and held the Yankees to one hit, the fewest in their 447 postseason games. Teams that win Game 1 of a best-of-five series go on to win it about 73% of the time.

Monday night at Tropicana Field, the Yankees hand Game 2 to another one of their own picks. Cam Schlittler, a seventh-rounder out of Northeaster in 2022, led the AL with a 1.95 ERA. He went 14-6 and struck out 239 in 193⅔ innings. Only Spud Chandler in 1943 and Ron Guidry in 1978 posted a lower ERA for the Yankees as qualified starters.

Aaron Judge hasn't played since Sept. 16 because of a right calf strain. Without him, the Yankees have been winning with homegrown players. Ben Rice was a 12th-rounder out of Dartmouth in 2021. Spencer Jones went 25th overall out of Venderbilt in 2022, the same draft as Schlittler. Lombard went 26th overall out of Gulliver Prep in 2023.

Damon Oppenheimer's amateur scouting department drafted all four. Oppenheimer, the Yankees' vice president and director of amateur scouting, has run the club's draft since 2005. His department also took Judge 32nd overall out of Fresno State in 2013.

"I think it's been a very gratifying couple of weeks for our player development, and deservedly so," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said during a Zoom call Sunday.

Boone gave credit to Kevin Reese's player development staff for turning those draft picks into big leaguers, too.

"In a season where we've been beat up and banged up, we've had answers," Boone said.

Rice has been the loudest answer, and he made his presence known in 2025.

He went 4-for-5 in the wild-card opener against the Boston Red Sox with a double, a solo homer and an eighth-inning grand slam. His six RBI tied the franchise postseason record, and he became the first Yankees player with four hits and six RBIs in a playoff game. On Sunday, Boone joked that he almost pinch-hit Giancarlo Stanton for Rice right before the slam.

Matt Hyde, the Yankees' Northeast area scout, didn't find Rice at Dartmouth. He found him playing summer ball for the Worcester Bravehearts in the Futures League. The Yankees took Rice with the 363rd pick. This July he was an All-Star with 29 homers at the break and swung in the Home Run Derby.

Boston found that out first in the wild-card opener. Schlittler struck out 10 over 6 ⅓ scoreless innings to back Rice's performance. Both grew up in Massachusetts and played college ball in New England.

On Monday Schlittler goes against Freddy Peralta, the AL Pitcher of the Month for September. The Rays got Peralta from the Mets on Aug. 2. Boone said Tropicana Field really accentuates a good four-seam fastball, and that Tampa Bay has tweaked Peralta's mix so he uses his changeup "a good bit."

In Game 2 of the Yankees' wild-card series against the Red Sox, Jones became the first player in postseason history to score in an inning he started and ended the sixth with a strikeout. He reached on a dropped third strike, stole second, took third on a throwing error and scored on Lombard's single. New York put up six runs in the inning, which ended with Jones going down swinging.

Jones waited a long time for that. He hit 35 homers between Double-A and Triple-A in 2025, second most in the minors, and he wasn't called up this year until May. His first big-league homer on June 9 came off the bat at 112.2 miles per hour, the hardest-hit first homer by a Yankees player in the Statcast era. Yes, that includes Judge.

Lombard, the son of former big-leaguer George Lombard, debuted Aug. 4 and hit .237 with seven homers and 22 RBIs. In one inning against the Rays on Sept. 24, he jumped over the catcher to score on a pitch that got away, then came back and hit a go-ahead two-run homer into the second deck.

Boone said what impressed him most was how Lombard handled a bad week early on.

"He loves the game, which I think is always impressive," Boone said. "Like he loves the stuff that's not sexy, the behind the scenes, the grind the routine."

title: Eagles went for kill shot, and Rams made them pay. 5 observations
description: The Eagles couldn't hold a 10-point lead late in the fourth quarter and lost to the Rams. Here are 5 observations:
fullText:
PHILADELPHIA − The Eagles went for the kill shot against the Los Angeles Rams.

Then they paid the price, losing 24-20 as the Rams scored 2 touchdowns in the final four minutes of the game to overcome a 10-point deficit.

But the decision to go for a touchdown on 4th-and-goal with 7:30 left in the fourth quarter made some sense. If the Eagles had converted, the Rams would have needed three scores to win. Even if they had kicked a field goal to go up by 13, the Rams could have won with two touchdowns, which they did.

Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets

It was easy to see why the Eagles gambled there.

The Eagles were already down six starters. Then right tackle Lane Johnson was scratched 90 minutes before the game for personal reasons. Then Saquon Barkley left with a hamstring injury early in the first quarter. Later, cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard left with injuries and didn't return.

And yet, there the Eagles were, leading by 10 points as they lined up for the fourth-down play.

But Jalen Hurts threw incomplete to Darius Cooper, who had already caught two touchdown passes. The Rams then raced down the field, going 98 yards in 3 minutes, 27 seconds. Then after the Eagles missed yet another third down, the Rams raced down the field again, getting the winning TD on Kyren Williams' 7-yard run with 1:10 left.

The Eagles had no answer, and no offense.

They only had 100 yards at halftime, 119 after 3 quarters. And yet, they got contributions from the defense, which had 2 interceptions (the first two of the season) and harassed Rams QB Matthew Stafford.

Special teams came up big, too, as Jake Elliott hit a 56-yard field goal in the rain, and Britain Covey returned a punt 41 yards to the Rams' 17, setting up a touchdown.

It wasn't enough as the Eagles fell to 2-2. Hurts was 12-for-27 for 93 yards and 2 touchdowns. They had 172 yards total.

Here are four more observations:

It couldn't have been easy for rookie Markel Bell even if he had a full week to prepare to start in place of star right tackle Lane Johnson. But Bell had just 90 minutes when the Eagles scratched Johnson for personal reasons.

This was Bell's first NFL start, and all things considered, the 6-foot-9, 346-pounder held up reasonably well. He was called for an illegal formation penalty, and he gave up a sack to the Rams' Byron Young.

The Eagles needed the short fields because they were 0-for-12 on third down. But twice, they got field goals because they started deep in Rams' territory, already in field goal range.

The Eagles did convert a 4th-and-2 from the Rams' 47 in the second quarter when Hurts hit Makai Lemon for 8 yards. But the Eagles were also stopped on a tush push late in the third quarter, and Hurts threw incomplete from the Rams' 2 yard line with 7:26 remaining.

Twice, the Eagles special teams unit came up big. The first was when Jake Elliott nailed a 56-yard field goal in the second quarter. He also hit a 29-yarder. Through 3 quarters on Oct. 4, he's 9-for-9 for the season, including 2-for-2 from 50 or more yards.

Elliott had made less than 80% of his attempts in each of the last two seasons. But he came up big when the Eagles needed him, especially considering the rainy mist that fell throughout the game.

The other big special teams play came when Britain Covey returned a punt 41 yards midway through the second quarter, setting the Eagles up at the Rams' 17 yard line. On that drive, Hurts hit Cooper for a touchdown, giving the Eagles a 13-3 lead with 5:44 left in the first half.

The Rams Harrison Mevis, meanwhile, missed a 49-yard field goal.

Through three games, the Eagles didn't have any takeaways on defense. It was the only time that has happened in more than 90 seasons of the Eagles' existence. That changed quickly and dramatically. Drew Mukuba intercepted Rams QB Matthew Stafford early in the first quarter, setting the Eagles up at the Rams' 28.

The drive stalled, in large part because of Barkley's hamstring injury, and the Eagles settled for a field goal.

But the Eagles' defense struck again in the final 34 seconds of the first half. That's when Cooper DeJean picked off Stafford at the Eagles' 40 and returned it 25 yards to the Rams' 35 with 19 seconds left. The Eagles cashed in on Hurts' TD pass to Cooper with 3 seconds left for a 20-10 halftime lead.

title: OU football vs Texas TV channel, odds, scouting report for Red River Rivalry
description: Fresh off a bye week, Oklahoma heads to the Cotton Bowl to face No. 1 Texas on Saturday in Dallas. Here's everything you need to know about the game.
fullText:
NORMAN — Fresh off a bye week, Oklahoma is looking to flip the script on what's been a disappointing season thus far.

The Sooners, which sit at 2-2 after losses to Georgia and Michigan, now head to the Cotton Bowl to face No. 1 Texas (4-0) in the Red River Rivalry in Dallas.

OU has lost two consecutive games to the Longhorns and three of the last four in the series. From 2016-21, the Sooners won six of the seven contests but since coach Brent Venables took over OU is 1-3.

"It'll be a great challenge," Venables said on his coach's show last week. "It's something that we need to get on the right side of it, we haven't been on the right side of it. It's always an awesome atmosphere and a big deal to people on one side or the other of the Red River."

Texas defeated then-No. 1 Ohio State on Sept. 12 at home and then-No. 14 Tennessee on Sept. 26 on the road.

Venables is sticking with quarterback John Mateer for now even after he turned the ball over three times in the first half of the Sooners' road loss to the Bulldogs. This time last year, Mateer played against the Longhorns 17 days removed from surgery to repair a broken thumb.

If OU wants to compete with Texas, it'll have to limit its disastrous turnovers. In the Sooners' last three games, they've lost the turnover battle 9-2.

It'd certainly help OU if it was able to get back some injured players like safety Michael Boganowski, left tackle Michael Fasusi and linebackers Owen Heinecke and Cole Sullivan.

Here's everything you need to know about the 122nd edition of the Red River Rivalry:

Stream OU vs Texas live via ESPN

More: What's gone right, wrong for OU football through four games of 2026 season?

Best player: Texas third-year edge rusher Colin Simmons will be the best player on the field Saturday. The 6-foot-3 Dallas native recorded 5.5 sacks in the Longhorns' win over the Volunteers. No OU player has more than 2.5 sacks the entire season. Simmons is a projected top-10 pick in next year's NFL Draft and should feast against a struggling Sooners offensive line.

The case for Texas: As listed above, the Longhorns have two of the best wins in the nation. Quarterback Arch Manning has done enough with 862 passing yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. He also has perhaps the most explosive supporting cast in the country with former OU running back Hollywood Smothers and receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo. Texas' defense ranks eighth among Power Four teams in points allowed per game and will have a field day if the Sooners continue to turn the ball over at an alarming rate.

The case for OU: The Sooners' defense should give the Longhorns offense some issues. OU's unit is also one of the nation's best and will only improve if it can get healthier. The tallest task will be moving the ball on offense. If offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle can show some of the things we saw in the Georgia game without Mateer's turnovers, OU will have a shot.

title: Rams come back to beat Eagles, 24-20: Instant analysis of thrilling win
description: The Rams came back to beat the Eagles, 24-20, after trailing all day, a dramatic win by Sean McVay's group after last week's collapse.
fullText:
There's just something about playing the Eagles in Philadelphia that does weird things to the Los Angeles Rams. Having lost their last two games to the Eagles in Philly, the Rams once again struggled on Sunday afternoon in an ugly, sloppy game at Lincoln Financial Field.

Both teams had issues on offense, in large part because of injuries. The Rams were without Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson, while the Eagles were missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert before losing Saquon Barkley on the opening drive. But for the Rams, the mistakes were self-inflicted. Penalties, drops and interceptions were the story of the game, failing to get anything going on offense.

Despite allowing 20 points, the Rams' defense did its job. Los Angeles held the Eagles to only 172 yards and zero third-down conversions on 12 attempts, but the Rams didn't take advantage of any stops made by the defense – until late in the fourth quarter.

After the Rams stopped the Eagles at the 2-yard line, they went 98 yards and scored a touchdown to pull within three points, making it 20-17. Following another third-down stop, the Rams got the ball back with 3 minutes to play and trailing by only three points.

They drove down the field in 1:45 and scored the go-ahead touchdown on a 7-yard touchdown run by Kyren Williams, his second score of the game. It gave Los Angeles its first lead of the day, capitalizing on a great defensive stop by the Rams on the previous drive.

The defense once again stood tall, stopping the Eagles on third and fourth down to seal the win, 24-20.

4: Matthew Stafford has thrown an interception in four straight games, his longest streak ever to start a year.

146: For the second straight week, Kyren Williams went over 100 yards from scrimmage.

0: The Rams held the Eagles to zero third-down conversions, forcing Philadelphia to go 0-for-12 on third in this game.

19: Puka Nacua put up 125 yards receiving, which was his 19th career game in the regular season with at least 100 yards.

... Byron Young knocked the ball out of Jalen Hurts' hand for a fumble on the Eagles' last-ditch drive in the final seconds. That put the Eagles in fourth-and-25 and essentially sealed the game.

There weren't too many to choose from, but Nacua's first catch of the game was a great one. He juggled it at first but kept his focus and managed to haul it in as he was going to the ground for a 28-yard catch.

Welcome back, @AsapPuka 😮‍💨

📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/YhT4UHK7nX

The Rams will fly back to Los Angeles and get ready for another tough game against the Bills next Monday night. At 2-2, the Rams are in much better shape now than they would've been had they lost to the Eagles and dropped to 1-3. Meanwhile, the Bills lost, 29-26, to the Patriots.

title: BVB women stay unbeaten in Cologne
description: Line-upThere were three changes to the BVB women’s starting XI compared to the previous week: Lara Schmidt came into central defense for Melanie Schuster, Noreen Günnewig replaced Ricarda Walkling ...
fullText:
There were three changes to the BVB women's starting XI compared to the previous week: Lara Schmidt came into central defense for Melanie Schuster, Noreen Günnewig replaced Ricarda Walkling in midfield, and Lena Ostermeier started in place of Ann-Sophie Vogel, who came on at halftime.

Playing in their usual 4-3-3 formation, the BVB women took to the well-kept artificial pitch in Cologne in summery temperatures. The hosts from the cathedral city started boldly, testing the black-and-yellows' defensive shape early on and giving Laura van der Laan her first task in the seventh minute. The BVB goalkeeper had to come off her line decisively to clear the danger.

At the other end, the BVB women took the lead from their second corner of the game (12'). Rita Schumacher's delivery was headed home by Lara Schmidt for her third headed goal of the season.

With the lead behind them, the BVB women gained even more control of the game, enjoying increasing possession and creating further chances through Alex Popp (24') and Annika Enderle (28'). During a Cologne counterattack, it was Laura van der Laan again who successfully slid in to cut out a through ball in the 30th minute. On the counterattack that followed, Cologne goalkeeper Felicitas Müller took center stage by parrying Jacqueline Meißner's volley on the line. Further attacks in the first half failed to find the net, and the black-and-yellows went into the break with a 1–0 lead.

At the restart, head coach Markus Högner made a triple substitution: Ann-Sophie Vogel, Jenske Steenwijk, and Ronja Leubner were brought on to provide fresh attacking ideas. While the first efforts were blocked by Cologne's defense, a rebound fell to substitute Ronja Leubner in the 56th minute, and she fired home ruthlessly from eleven meters to make it 2–0. Shortly before that, Alex Popp had intercepted a goal kick from the Cologne goalkeeper and started the move with her cross into the box.

After that, the Borussia women pushed for more goals. Long-range efforts from Ostermeier (63') and a volley from Schumacher (70') either missed the target or were saved by the in-form goalkeeper. So it was once again a corner from Rita Schumacher that found its way into the opposition net via Lara Schmidt – 3–0 in the 71st minute.

Eight minutes later, Ann-Sophie Vogel broke through down the left wing. Her cross found Ronja Leubner, who did not make full contact with her shot and in doing so forced an own goal for 4–0.

Shortly before the end, Rita Schumacher capped off a run in behind with a goal of her own (84'), which also sealed the final score. That means the BVB women remain unbeaten at the top of the table after seven matchdays, ahead of Bayer 04 Leverkusen's also unbeaten U23s.

On matchday eight of the Regionalliga West, the BVB women host promoted Niederrheinliga side Rhenania Bottrop at Stadion Rote Erde. Kickoff is on Sunday (11/10) at 3 p.m. Standing tickets (€3) and seated tickets (€5) are available online in the ticket shop. In addition, Pluto TV will broadcast the match live and in full free of charge.

fullText:
Missouri HC Eli Drinkwitz rips 'crap' media narratives after crushing Florida appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Eli Drinkwitz and the Missouri Tigers did an absolute beatdown on the Florida Gators in the 45-17 ranked upset on Saturday afternoon.

Drinkwitz and Missouri are off to a strong start to the 2026 season, standing out as one of the best teams in the nation. Their win over Florida, ranked No. 8 in last week's poll, saw them jump up from 25th place to No. 14. Meanwhile, Gators fell down to 16th.

Drinkwitz does not have any concern about that. When reporters asked him about the significance of the ranked win, the head coach shut it down with a blunt answer.

"Doesn't mean anything. This is about this game," he said Saturday evening. "It was a good win versus a really good team today. That's all it was, guys."

"Nobody in our locker room could have cared less about that. I couldn't have cared less about that. Again, that's stuff for you all to tweet about and to make up stories about and try to create some sort of narrative about me or my program. I really couldn't care less. OK, the SEC is a hard league. Yeah, I'm done with that."

Coach Drinkwitz says he "couldn't care less" what people say about his top-25 record.#Missouri media kept asking about the significance of the win, and he had enough.

Here's how he answered: pic.twitter.com/3fUSLqSR8V

— The Tiger Kickoff Show! 🐯 (@tigerkickoff) October 4, 2026

Many fans anticipated the matchup between Missouri and Florida to be a competitive one. Eli Drinkwitz and the Tigers had other plans, beating the brakes off of the Gators.

Missouri controlled the momentum for most of the game. After being even at three apiece in the first quarter, the Tigers went on to torch Florida 42-14 in the last three periods of the contest.

Austin Simmons prevailed with his performance leading the attack. He completed 23 out of 30 passes for 340 yards and two touchdowns.

Jamal Roberts torched Florida defenders whenever he got the chance to run with the ball. He racked up 24 carries for 211 yards and a hat trick of three touchdowns. Meanwhile, Cayden Lee had a strong day in the receiving corps, making eight catches for 110 yards.

The No. 14 Tigers will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Texas A&M Aggies in Week 6 as kickoff commences on Oct. 10.

title: 2026 Lehigh Valley Classic: Steven Alker wins for fourth time this year
description: Five weeks after overtaking Michael Block at the Ally Challenge, Steven Alker did it again in Allentown, Pennsylvania, on Sunday to earn his fourth win of 2026.
fullText:
New Zealander Steven Alker closed with a 4-under 66 on Sunday to win the Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic at 14 under, one shot ahead Tag Ridings.

The victory marks fourth time that Alker has reached the winner's circle this season, while increasing his career total to 14 titles on the PGA Tour Champions.

Michael Block shot a bogey-free 63 on Saturday to gain a one-shot lead over Alker, but Alker caught him for the second time in five weeks.

The final-group pairing was a rematch of the Ally Challenge in August, where Block lost a two-shot lead to Alker.

Alker went on to win by three shots, making it back-to-back victories after his win at the Rogers Charity Classic a week prior.

In Allentown on Sunday, Alker birdied the first to pull even with Block.

At the second hole, a cart driven by Alker's 19-year-old fill-in caddie slid on wet grass and struck Block's cart from behind with Block seated inside.

The teenager was on the bag because Alker's regular caddie, Troy Martin, had fallen ill.

The contact was described as a "light bump." An on-site physio checked Block and reported he was fine.

Close call today at the PGA Tour Champions event.

Steven Alker's 19-year-old, fill-in caddie was driving a cart on the second hole when the cart slid on wet grass and crashed into Michael Block's cart from behind.

The collision was described as a "light bump," though Block, who…

Alker moved ahead of Block for good at the par-4 fifth, where he made birdie and Block made bogey for a two-shot swing. He gave one back with a bogey at the eighth and made the turn a stroke ahead. The bigger threat came from Ridings, who shot 64 in an earlier group to reach 13 under. Alker and Block both birdied Nos. 11, 16 and 17, and the last vaulted Alker past Ridings. Alker parred No. 18 to win by one.

Block bogeyed the last to finish alone in third at 12 under for the best performance of his senior career. The week was also consequential for Block because Sunday was his seventh start, the number a non-member needs for his earnings to become official and for postseason eligibility.

The head professional at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club in Mission Viejo, Calif., is headed to the Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs less than four months after turning 50 on June 15.

Ridings closed with a 64 for second place at 13 under. Stewart Cink, No. 1 in the Schwab Cup standings, matched Block's 63 for the low round of the week and tied for fourth at 11 under with Robert Karlsson and Richard Green.

The PGA Tour Champions regular season has two events left before the Schwab Cup playoffs begin Oct. 23 at the Stifel Charity Classic in St. Louis.

title: Fantasy Football Early Week 5 Waiver Wire: Eagles' backfield depth, Bills' WR duo worth adding after more injuries
description: In need of some lineup help? Here are some early fantasy football waiver wire pickups to consider going into Week 5.
fullText:
We're at about the quarter mark of the 2026 NFL season — crazy we're already there, right? That's given us about four weeks of a sample for fantasy football, but it feels like there are still a bunch of question marks on plenty of offenses. Whether it's due to a breakout or injuries mounting, here are some early fantasy football waiver wire options to consider going into Week 5.

To add injury to insult, the Eagles lost RB Saquon Barkley to a hamstring ailment early in their brutal Week 5 loss to the Rams. While we await further word on Barkley, we have to consider both the backs behind him for fantasy at this point. Saquon had been underperforming and this is the second game he was essentially knocked out due to injury; the same happened in Week 2 due to a stinger/neck injury.

Bigsby and Shipley led the backfield with Barkley out. The former had the bulk of the work with 14 carries for 55 yards, while Shipley had six carries for 23 yards (he also had the goal-line work). Each back saw just one target in the passing game.

If Barkley is out in Week 5 versus the Jaguars in London, Bigsby and Shipley should split work again. Bigsby is who you would prioritize given the volume, while Shipley may be easier to snag in deeper formats.

DJ Moore continues to struggle to stay on the field. After being injured in Week 2, Moore was able to shake it off and play the next two games. But he was knocked out of Week 4 against the Patriots due to that lingering shoulder issue and didn't get back in the contest.

With Moore out, the target tree at WR is very clear with Coleman and Shakir leading the passing attack. New England keyed in on TE Dalton Kincaid, who had a goose egg with just one target on Sunday. But Coleman and Shakir both ate. Despite stepping up in Week 2 with Moore out, Coleman wasn't added to many rosters. That'll likely change going into Week 5.

Coleman scored a late 34-yard TD to cap off a six-catch, 116-yard performance in the wild loss to the Patriots on Sunday, good for the WR6 spot in fantasy with 20.6 points. Shakir didn't find the end zone but turned eight targets into seven catches for 82 yards, a strong showing in PPR formats.

In such an explosive offense, both Shakir and Coleman should be on more rosters. We don't know if Moore will be ready for Week 5 but we know he's struggled to stay healthy. Shakir and Coleman will each have flex appeal for a matchup with the Rams on Monday Night Football.

We know that when Aaron Rodgers keys in on a receiver, he usually looks their way pretty regularly. While we thought that receiver could be Michael Pittman Jr. after the offseason trade, it looks like it's Roman Wilson.

The Steelers fell to the Browns in Week 4 on TNF but Wilson scored for the second straight week, finishing with three catches for 74 yards and 14.9 fantasy points. Wilson now has six targets in every game this season, and while the volume isn't great, he's got splash plays of 38 yards and 49 yards in the past two games. We've seen enough from Wilson that he should be rostered in more leagues. He'll be a decent WR3/flex option in PPR formats given Pittsburgh's upcoming schedule.

title: Women handballers celebrate second Champions League win
description: SquadThe squad is slowly starting to look a bit thin. Ona Vegué was also unavailable against Sola. The Spaniard had injured her ankle in training and therefore did not travel to Norway at all. Backco...
fullText:
The squad is slowly starting to look a bit thin. Ona Vegué was also unavailable against Sola. The Spaniard had injured her ankle in training and therefore did not travel to Norway at all. Backcourt player Mareike Thomaier was also ruled out at short notice. She underwent appendix surgery on Sunday. Emma Olsson (thigh), Lena Hausherr (knee) and Pam Korsten (knee) were also absent.

The game in Sola got underway with a penalty for BVB after just 30 seconds. Alina Grijseels converted confidently. With regular penalty taker Ona Vegué injured and Mareike Thomaier also unavailable, the captain took over the responsibility – and settled into the game very well.

The match started evenly, with a high tempo on both sides. After eight minutes, the score was 5:5, including two converted penalties from Grijseels. What stood out for BVB was their strong transition defense, which prevented the Norwegians from taking the lead. Alongside Grijseels, goalkeeper Sarah Wachter and Guro Nestaker also impressed, with the latter already scoring three times in her home country after 15 minutes.

The second 15 minutes of the first half began with BVB holding a two-goal lead (11:9). Kelly Vollebregt showed her finishing ability on the right wing with a quick double. Grijseels also remained composed from the penalty line and made it 13:11 with her third goal in the 19th minute. After that, neither team could quite maintain the high pace. Sola increasingly took advantage of gaps in the BVB defense. Fortunately for the Black & Yellows, things continued to click in attack, while Sarah Wachter was having a strong day in goal.

After Malin Holter missed a penalty, Wachter produced a fine throw into the empty Sola net to make it 17:14 in the 25th minute. Three minutes before the break, Kay Rothenpieler reached into his bag of tricks and switched to playing with four backcourt players. During the timeout, the BVB coach called for "another two or three goals before halftime." Guro Nestaker responded with her fourth goal to make it 18:14, Dana Bleckmann increased it to 19:15, and Nestaker again produced the nicest goal of the game for the 20:15 halftime score.

After the break, the question was how Sola intended to make up a five-goal deficit. Camilla Herrem initially cut it to 17:20 after three minutes. BVB were slow to get going again. It took three and a half minutes before Nestaker scored Dortmund's first goal of the second half to make it 21:18. Rothenpieler demanded more movement in defense. Understandably so, because the five-goal lead had temporarily been reduced to a narrow 24:22 by the 40th minute.

At that stage, Lisa Antl's goal for 25:22 was extremely important. Shortly afterwards, Merel Freriks made it 26:22 in the 43rd minute after a brilliant assist from Dana Bleckmann. Following a strongly won ball by Grijseels, it was Freriks again who scored for 28:23 in the 45th minute.

Lisa Antl was incredibly combative yet completely fair on the unfamiliar left side of the defense, winning ball after ball. But Sola stayed in it. Ten minutes from the end, BVB led by only three goals (28:25), and five minutes later it was 29:25. But time was now on the side of the Black & Yellows. When Grijseels converted her fifth penalty to make it 30:25, the atmosphere in the arena grew noticeably quieter. Sola increasingly looked out of ideas.

Four minutes from time, Rothenpieler took another timeout and ended the seven-against-six numerical overload. Grijseels called for them to run down the clock. Lara Egeling removed the last doubts with a brilliant lob to make it 32:27 with 120 seconds remaining. That sealed their second win in the EHF Champions League.

Kay Rothenpieler (Coach): "It was a deserved win, I'd even call it a big point because it was a key game against Sola. I think we always had the game under control. Between the 40th and 42nd minute, we had a difficult spell when we missed two shots, but we dealt with it convincingly. Sarah Wachter had a really good day in goal. With Mareike Thomaier out, we naturally had fewer options in the backcourt, but Alina Grijseels and Guro Nestaker did a very good job. By using Lisa Antl out wide in defense, we gave ourselves new momentum. You could see that we've continued to develop and showed a completely different body language."

The next game in the Alsco Women's Handball Bundesliga is on Wednesday, 7 October. Buxtehuder SV will then come to Halle Wellinghofen (throw-off 7:30 p.m., live on Dyn and Sporteurope.TV). A highly interesting opponent who, like BVB, has also qualified for the quarter-finals of the DHB Cup. During halftime of the Bundesliga match, BVB women's footballer Alexandra Popp will conduct the draw for the next round of the DHB Cup.

title: Titans fail to capitalize on opportunities and Fall 25-18 to Ravens
description: Turnovers and questionable play calling cost the Tennessee Titans in a 24-18 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans showed some life, but poor ball security and splash plays cost them, and the Baltimore Ravens dominated the scoreboard in a 24-18 win at M&T Bank Stadium.

The Titans moved the ball, but multiple turnovers and questionable play calling cost them. Cam Ward threw a critical interception early, and Carnell Tate lost one of his two fumbles, both of which cost the Titans points on offense and set up the Ravens for scores.

The game stayed close after Baltimore lost quarterback Lamar Jackson to an ankle injury late in the first half, but Tennessee couldn't get anything going in the second half and missed a golden opportunity to come back. The effort was there, but the execution didn't match.

Special teams penalties: The Titans again committed multiple special teams penalties that cost them valuable yardage and wiped out some solid gains in the return game. Chimere Dike looked better, but the unit kept pinning the Titans' offense deep and giving the Ravens an advantage.

Turnovers: Tennessee lost the turnover battle against the Ravens, and their turnovers came at inopportune times, killing momentum and setting the Ravens up to add points. The Titans defense did what it could, but it couldn't hold up against the explosive Baltimore offense. Tennessee had the two turnovers and another turnover on downs, and Baltimore scored 17 points off those miscues.

Offensive playcalling: Brian Daboll's play calling was better in the first half, but it fell off a cliff in the second, and Tennessee couldn't get anything going or take advantage of the Ravens' injuries. Couple that with a questionable fourth-down wildcat call as the Titans tried to punch in a game-tying touchdown in the second quarter, and it's clear Daboll needs to be held accountable for his decision-making.

The Titans failed to punch in a game-tying touchdown in the second quarter when offensive coordinator Brian Daboll called a head-scratching wildcat run with Tony Pollard. Baltimore changed momentum and quickly extended the lead to 21-7.

WR Carnell Tate: Tate had his best game as a pro, breaking out with nine receptions for 145 yards, and is quickly developing into a game-changing threat for the Titans offense.

LB Cody Barton: Barton had one of his best games of the 2026 season and helped lead the charge for the Titans defense. The veteran linebacker finished with eight total tackles and made some big stops when Tennessee needed them.

RB Tony Pollard: Pollard didn't put up game-changing numbers in this one, but he ran hard and was consistent, finishing with 16 carries for 48 yards and one touchdown, and chipped in two receptions.

Tennessee had some bumps and bruises with Jeffery Simmons and Marcus Harris leaving the game at different stages, but both returned to the field during the contest.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh will meet with reporters on Monday afternoon to wrap up the week and set the stage for Week 5. Select players may be made available after Saleh's press conference.

Tennessee will return to practice on Wednesday ahead of a Week 5 game against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee. Kickoff is scheduled for Noon CDT.

title: Jaguars hold off Bengals for 22-17 win
description: Joe Burrow didn't have Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins on the field at the end of Sunday's game, but he almost brought the Bengals back against the Jaguars.
fullText:
Joe Burrow didn't have Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins on the field at the end of Sunday's game, but he almost brought the Bengals back against the Jaguars.

Burrow hit Mitchell Tinsley, Mike Gesicki, and Dohnte Meyers with passes that covered 62 yards and moved the Bengals to the 21-yard-line in the final minute with the Jaguars up by five, but three straight incompletions left Cincinnati with a fourth-and-10 to keep the game alive. Burrow hit running back Chase Brown with a short pass and he was brought down by defensive back Rayuan Lane one yard short of the sticks.

That made the Jaguars 22-17 winners a short time after it looked like they were in position to run the clock out on their own. Wide receiver Parker Washington broke loose for a 39-yard gain up the sideline on a third down after the two-minute warning, but replays showed he stepped out short of the first down and the Jaguars had to punt the ball away.

The defense was able to hold at the end and that was fitting because they were strong all day. Burrow threw a pair of interceptions and had a third wiped out due to a roughing the passer penalty on defensive lineman Arik Armstead. The Bengals quarterback finished the day with 428 passing yards, but the second pick was particularly painful as it came in the red zone with the Bengals in position to take their first lead of the afternoon.

Chase was ruled out after going for a concussion evaluation in the second quarter and Higgins went to the medical tent late in the fourth quarter. Higgins had 11 catches for 157 yards and Brown also had 11 catches as the Bengals found a way to get their offense moving despite Chase's absence, but they had no success running the football and the Jaguars were able to give themselves breathing room with a 76-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter.

That drive was aided by a facemask penalty that was one of 11 Bengals penalties on the day. The Jaguars had 13 penalties of their own and the sloppiness is something that head coach Liam Coen will likely focus on despite the result.

Jags quarterback Trevor Lawrence was 18-of-23 for 227 yards and was sacked four times over the course of the afternoon. Bhayshul Tuten ran 17 times for 73 yards and Chris Rodriguez capped that fourth quarter drive with a 25-yard touchdown run.

Jacksonville is now 3-1 with a visit from the reeling Eagles on tap next Sunday. The Bengals have lost two in a row, but should have a chance to get right against the Dolphins in Week 5.

title: U23 impress in Siegen too
description: BackgroundAfter a grueling run of midweek fixtures and a well-earned three-day training break, head coach Daniel Rios’ side traveled to Siegen sitting second in the table. Another win against Sportf...
fullText:
After a grueling run of midweek fixtures and a well-earned three-day training break, head coach Daniel Rios' side traveled to Siegen sitting second in the table. Another win against Sportfreunde would allow the U23s to keep the pressure on leaders Rot-Weiß Oberhausen, who were three points ahead.

The team's development over the past few weeks is encouraging: match by match, they have looked more solid – despite the major squad overhaul in the summer. "Positive results are the best therapy. The team has simply handled every situation very well. Week after week, they show this desire to improve," Rios said ahead of the match.

Compared to the 4-2 win over 1. FC Bocholt, coach Rios made three changes to his starting XI. Takato Yamamoto, Fadi Zarqelain and Kevin Mutove came into the lineup for Ayman Azhil, Connor Krempicki and Daniel Sumbu.

The match in Siegen got off to a slow start. The first real big chance came after 15 minutes – and it fell to the hosts: after a misplaced pass from Silas Ostrzinski, Matona-Glody Ngyombo got a shot away, but it was deflected behind for a corner. At the other end, Finn Fuchs beat several opponents and drove inside, but his pass into the box was intercepted by the alert Marcel Johnen. Overall, it was an evenly balanced contest, with much of the play taking place between the two penalty areas.

However, the Black & Yellows were clinical in front of goal and took the lead in the 31st minute. Tim Degener beat three opponents and pulled the trigger, but his shot was blocked. Kevin Mutove reacted quickest, pounced on the rebound and only had to tap the ball in.

Shortly before half-time, Rios' side struck again: Arne Wessels made it 2-0 in style. The wide player had some space on the right, cut inside and curled the ball from the edge of the box onto the inside of the post. From there, it bounced into the net (44').

After the break, BVB came out better and created further chances. Malik Hodroj slipped Mutove through, but his effort flashed just wide of the left post. Three minutes later, Zarqelain beat several opponents and found Degener, whose shot was superbly saved by Johnen.

Siegen remained dangerous, though, and pulled one back in the 64th minute. Following a corner, Jan-Luca Rumpf got the better of his marker in the box and headed home for 1-2.

The Black & Yellows' response was not long in coming. Just two minutes later, Dortmund combined brilliantly through the Siegen defense: Zarqelain found Yamamoto, who immediately laid it off to Mutove. The striker kept his cool in front of goal and slotted home for 3-1 (66') – Mutove's seventh goal of the season already.

BVB continued to look dangerous afterwards: Yamamoto picked out Sumbu with an excellent through ball, but the Dortmund man was denied by Johnen in a one-on-one (70'). Both teams continued to put a lot into the game in the closing stages. After a long ball from Hodroj, substitute Benedikt Wüstenhagen got a shot away, but once again the Siegen goalkeeper was equal to it. In the end, the Black & Yellows held on for a deserved 3-1 away win.

Daniel Rios: "We said before the game that this was a top match. It's extremely difficult to come here to Siegen and get a result. In the first half, we controlled the game, didn't create that many chances, but had a lot of control. Defensively too, apart from one moment, we allowed very little and went into half-time 2-0 up thanks to individual quality, like with Arne's goal. We knew Siegen would come out and try a lot in the second half and that they have the quality to turn the game around. After it became 2-1, it was important that we showed a good response and made it 3-1. Overall, we're very happy that we came through here in Siegen with a good, controlled first half and a second half in which we defended ourselves well. Of course, we're delighted with the three points."

Dortmund's U23s are back in action on Saturday (10 October/live on LEAGUES). In the Regionalliga West, the Black & Yellows host SG Wattenscheid 09 at 2 p.m. at Stadion Rote Erde.

Goals: 0-1 Mutove (31'), 0-2 Wessels (44'), 1-2 Rumpf (64'), 1-3 Mutove (66')

title: Legends appearances, kind words from DeAndre Hopkins: How Texans celebrated 25 years at halftime
description: The Houston Texans commemorated their 25th season with a halftime show that included Andre Johnson, Arian Foster, DeAndre Hopkins, Brian Cushing, Gary Kubiak and J.J. Watt
fullText:
At halftime of their game with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the Houston Texans celebrated their 25th season, honoring legends on the field and getting a quick heartfelt speech from former star DeAndre Hopkins.

On a day when the Texans paid tribute to the franchise's first win, which came against the Cowboys in the team's first game on Sept. 8, 2002, by wearing the red socks the team wore that night and painting the end zones with the same design, the team looked back at all 25 seasons by having a player from each season on the field during the halftime ceremony.

Franchise legends Andre Johnson, Arian Foster, Brian Cushing, DeAndre Hopkins and Gary Kubiak all received introductions, as well as Billy Miller - who scored the first touchdown in team history - before team CEO Cal McNair, the son of the late Bob and Janice McNair, spoke on the field.

"We're here because my parents brought football back home to Houston in 1999," said McNair, referencing the year the NFL granted Houston the expansion franchise. "They had big dreams, believing something special was possible for our team both on and off the field. We're so proud to be here today celebrating 25 season of Texans football. Over the past two decades, we've shared many extraordinary moments and we're looking forward to even more ahead of us. We're grateful to all our players, coaches, staff and fans who have been a part of our story over the past 25 seasons and we can't wait to write the next chapter with y'all."

Johnson, the franchise's only Hall of Famer until Watt goes in, presumably in 2028, said a few words before introducing Hopkins, who was dealt away in 2020 by Bill O'Brien in the most unpopular trade in team history.

"Ever since I left, I feel like a part of me has been in Houston," Hopkins said. "This is home. I love you guys. This always will be home. As long as I'm here, just know, listen, I love you guys. I embrace everything. I love it."

Watt, who couldn't attend because he is calling the Chiefs-Raiders game in Las Vegas for CBS, recorded a message that was played on the screen at the conclusion of the ceremony.

"All these people gathered here today, that's what makes it so special: You the fans, the players, the organization, the ownership. Very honored and privileged to be a part of it," Watt said. "Wish so badly I could be there with you today, but I know you're going to celebrate the right way. H-Town forever.

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle. 

This article originally published at Legends appearances, kind words from DeAndre Hopkins: How Texans celebrated 25 years at halftime.
