Replacements: Caine, McIntyre, Francis, Tshiunza, Canakaivata, Hanson, Louw, Loganimasi.

title: El Niño could reshape Thanksgiving and Christmas travel
description:
A potentially record-breaking El Niño could leave Thanksgiving and Christmas travelers in southern states battling storms and heavier rainfall but reduce the chance of snow and ice-related travel disruption for those in northern states, forecasters have told Newsweek.
The developing super El Niño, which has already broken a 170-year record, is expected to continue strengthening over the fall meaning its impact on the weather patterns in the United States will likely be affected over Christmas and Thanksgiving.
All forecasters Newsweek spoke to stressed that it is too early to know for sure what the climate phenomenon will do during the festive season, but, “based on past events there is a tendency for cooler, wetter and stormier conditions to affect the southern United States over the winter, but with warmer and drier conditions in the northeast,” Professor Richard Allan, a climate scientist at the University of Reading in the U.K., said.
fullText:
A potentially record-breaking El Niño could leave Thanksgiving and Christmas travelers in southern states battling storms and heavier rainfall but reduce the chance of snow and ice-related travel disruption for those in northern states, forecasters have told Newsweek.

The developing super El Niño, which has already broken a 170-year record, is expected to continue strengthening over the fall meaning its impact on the weather patterns in the United States will likely be affected over Christmas and Thanksgiving.

All forecasters Newsweek spoke to stressed that it is too early to know for sure what the climate phenomenon will do during the festive season, but, “based on past events there is a tendency for cooler, wetter and stormier conditions to affect the southern United States over the winter, but with warmer and drier conditions in the northeast,” Professor Richard Allan, a climate scientist at the University of Reading in the U.K., said.

This could mean states that typically experience what the NOAA describes as “exceptionally stormy winters and increased precipitation” during El Niño months, such as Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and southern California, could be in for flooded roads, reduced visibility on the roads and weather-related flight delays.

Conversely, northeastern states, such as New York, Massachusetts, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, often see drier and warmer conditions during El Niño winters, meaning they could see smoother travel conditions than the south. But temperature patterns are much less consistent than precipitation, “even during the strongest events,” the NOAA warns, so it is more difficult to predict what travel will be like for these states.

El Niño is a naturally recurring climate pattern that affects temperatures and rainfall worldwide when it warms waters in the Pacific.

The NOAA officially refers to the climate pattern as “very strong,” referring to an event in which waters are warmer than average, usually by around 2 degrees Celsius. But many independent meteorologists and other weather agencies have been referring to the current event as a “super El Niño”—used to point to the same thing.

The current El Niño is 3.05 degrees Celsius above average, WFLA-TV chief meteorologist Jeff Berardelli reported last week, marking a new record for the highest ocean anomaly in 170 years.

The NOAA predicts that, between October and December, there is a 75 percent chance of a “historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Niño events dating back to 1950.”

Allan warned specifically of “deluges and associated flooding” which are being “super-charged by the warmer world we live in, driven by our greenhouse gas emissions.”

If southern states see spells of heavy rainfall during the Christmas and Thanksgiving season, they could face roads left unusable from floods, danger from being on roads when they do flood and mudslides—all of which would continue to cut off routes even after the individual events are over.

The 1997-98 El Niño, often cited as an example of a strong El Niño, saw southern California battered with heavy rainfall and mudslides which closed Highways 1, 126 and Highway 150 in early December, according to the NOAA Storm Events Database.

A few months later, when another storm hit in February, multiple roads and bridges were damaged because of mudslides and high water, the National Weather Service recorded on its Southern California weather history report. A large sink hole forced the closure of Santiago Canyon Road for several days.

The 1997-98 El Niño reached 2.3 degrees Celsius, the NOAA’s Relative Oceanic Niño three-month Index shows.

While one of this season’s El Niño’s single-day ocean-temperature peaks surpassed this with its 3.05 degrees Celsius reading last week, its current average is 1.4 degrees Celsius, according to the index. But the NOAA predicts it will hit more than 2.5 degrees Celsius in October-December.

Atmospheric science Professor Paul D. Williams pointed Newsweek to a June report he co-authored for turbulence-forecasting company Skypath which predicted that flights may be “a lot bumpier than normal in the year ahead” because of how strong El Niño conditions can create a greater chance of air turbulence over the North Atlantic.

The article, which has not been peer reviewed, concluded that, this, combined with the strength of the current El Niño “suggest statistically that large parts of the world could experience stronger windshear and increased turbulence.”

During the 1997-98 El Niño winter, hundreds of flights were delayed by an hour or more at the San Francisco International Airport on a day in January, local media reports from the time show. This was because conditions forced the Federal Aviation Administration halved the number of flights arriving each hour and low visibility only two of the airport's four runways could be used.

In a February storm, several flights were delayed at Los Angeles International Airport—not because of floods on the runways, but because the travel disruption on roads had been so severe multiple passengers and flight crews were not able to get to the airport on time, The Los Angeles Times reported that day.

Akshay Deoras, senior research scientist at the National Centre for Atmospheric Science, advised travelers to keep track of local National Weather Service forecasts before they set off this festive season.

Both Allan and Deoras stressed that it is too soon to predict what impact the El Niño will have on weather patterns and when.

“Due to the fickle nature of weather, it is only possible to get a clearer picture in the days running up to the busy holiday period,” Allan said.

Deoras added that even if predicted weather effects take place, it is “impossible to predict this far in advance whether there would be particularly strong impacts during this year’s holidays” as they can happen any time between November and spring the following year.

The NOAA says that while this year’s stronger El Niño event means “the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Niño are larger,” they are “not guaranteed.”

The next official update on El Niño is scheduled for October 8.

Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Ben Kelly and Emma Lee-Sang

title: World No. 979 Stewart's dilemma after finishing fourth at Alfred Dunhill Links
description: Scotland's Michael Stewart has a choice to make after securing his best finish at a DP World Tour event.
fullText:
Alfred Dunhill Links Championship

-20 A Meronk (Pol); -18 C Jarvis (SA), N Norgaard (Den); -17 M Stewart (Sco), T Fleetwood (Eng); -16 R MacIntyre (Sco), B Koepka (US)

Selected others: -13 C Syme (Sco); -12 S Bairstow (Eng), C Hill (Sco); -12 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), M Jordan (Eng); -11 D Law (Sco), R Mansell (Eng); -9 P Harrington (Ire), A Fitzpatrick (Eng), S Jamieson (Sco), C Adam (Sco), E Walker (Sco)

On Wednesday, Michael Stewart earned £2,500 for finishing runner-up in the Tartan Pro Tour event at Duddingston Golf Club near Edinburgh.

Four days later, the world number 979 has just picked up nearly 100 times that by finishing joint fourth behind winner Adrian Meronk at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

But what the 36-year-old Scot regards as "without doubt" the best week of his career has left him with a dilemma.

Finishing in the top 10 - two shots behind Poland's Meronk, one behind Denmark's Niklas Norgaard and South Africa's Casey Jarvis, and tied with England's Tommy Fleetwood - means he qualifies for next week's big-money Spanish Open.

However, that clashes with the conclusion to the Tartan Pro Tour, the Gleneagles Masters, after which Stewart will qualify for next year's second-tier Challenge Tour should he protect his current second place.

"Right now, in all honesty, in my mind, it's definitely play the Tartan Pro Tour final at Gleneagles," Stewart said.

"If I don't go and somebody overtakes me, I don't think that's the right thing to do.

"I've played so well to put myself in that position as well. There's so many good players behind me. One of three or four guys can catch me and, if one of them plays well, they can win.

England's Jordan in contention at Alfred Dunhill Links

Kim wins Asian Games gold to secure military exemption

"It would be silly if I wasn't to go to Gleneagles and at least tee it up and try and secure my Challenge Tour card.

"That was my goal at the start of the year."

While Meronk was earning his fifth win on the DP World Tour, Stewart, who finished one stroke ahead of compatriot and defending champion Robert MacIntyre, was making only his sixth appearance - having missed the cut in his previous five events.

The Ayrshire-based former Walker Cup player finished joint 52nd at The Open Championship at Royal Liverpool in 2023 but described his performance at Kingsbarns, Carnoustie and St Andrews this week as a career highlight.

"The Open was amazing, but I felt really disheartened after the Sunday at The Open because I felt like I threw away what could have been a really special weekend," he said.

"But this is amazing. It gives yourself a little bit more belief that you can go on and compete at this level."

MacIntyre was delighted to see his fellow Scot's hard work rewarded.

"It's brilliant," he said. "That's exactly what I was hoping for.

"When we spoke at Kingsbarns when he had a good second round, it was like, hopefully he can do something special that gives him a chance.

"I play the odd game of golf with him and his short game is superb."

title: Hamilton bemused after glitch turns F1 into 'Lego race'
description: Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton liken the effects of a software bug that affected multiple cars before the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to a "Lego race".
fullText:
Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton likened the effects of a software bug that affected multiple cars before the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to a "Lego race".

The problem led to several cars, including those of the two multiple world champions who were sharing the front row of the grid, not working in the wet conditions that preceded the race.

A tropical downpour delayed attempts to get the grand prix under way for the best part of an hour. And when the cars set off on formation laps behind a safety car to test the conditions, audiences were treated to the bizarre sight of many of them struggling to move.

A bug in the software that mandates how the engines' electrical power can be used in wet conditions had been triggered by a combination of low engine speeds, low grip and specific aspects of the circuit layout.

Verstappen, who went on to take a dominant win that was his first victory of the year, said: "These engines are so complicated and a lot of software is implemented.

"I triggered [the problem] first and then I looked in my mirror, I was like, 'Wait, are they waiting for me or what's going [on]...?' It was like the Lego race."

Verstappen was referring to a show run in battery-powered Lego F1 cars that was held before the British Grand Prix in July.

Hamilton, sitting beside Verstappen in the post-race news conference after finishing third, interjected to say: "Yeah, we had the same speed. I had to stop on track and stop the car and engine and restart it. I've never done that before."

Verstappen added: "It was insane. Like, it's the Lego power. At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn't understand what was going on.

"Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still, and I saw you (Hamilton) by yourself crawling. That's not what you want, right, for the sport."

Mercedes driver George Russell, who retired from the race with an engine failure, said: "It didn't feel very F1."

Nikolas Tombazis, the single-seater director for governing body the FIA said there would be a full investigation.

The issue arose, he added, because, while the software had been tested, it had not been tested in these specific conditions. Largely because there has been so little running in the wet this year.

"Cars are complicated," Tombazis said. "We would all like it to be simpler, but when you have electrical energy and combustion energy all working together, and obviously when you want to ensure that there's sporting fairness between the teams, that is complicated.

"We haven't done a full debrief of the situation and see how we can avoid such an issue. Every race, we have a long debrief afterwards, where we identify criticalities.

"Obviously, that was a major criticality, and we need to make sure we avoid it. Can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no, but we will do our best to avoid it, of course."

This is far from the first issue created by the huge complexity of the latest hybrid engines introduced this year, with their near 50-50 split between internal combustion and electrical power.

Because the engines are fundamentally energy starved, and so cannot deploy their full combined power output at all times, a series of complexities were added into the management of the engines to try to sticking-plaster solutions.

Many of these led to the counter-intuitive driving about which many of the sport's stars have been complaining all season - and more changes have been added since.

Off-track conversation has been dominated by this all year, and rules are changing for next year to alter the energy split to try to ameliorate the issue.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "What happened at the start obviously is not ideal in terms of presentation of the sport.

"But at the same time it is the first year of new regulations, quite complex from a regulatory point of view, and it was also the first time we started in such conditions.

"So we have to concede that F1 has done an excellent job in making some new regulations that came with some question marks from a power-unit behaviour point of view when it came to racing for instance.

"We have to acknowledge there has been really good work to make the show and racing work, and if there are some glitches occasionally, we have to accept they are glitches for everyone, be supportive and make sure it doesn't happen again."

The problem had a secondary consequence - the field order was jumbled up, and one reading of the rules could have meant the grid order should change for any restart.

But while the FIA's software engineers were rewriting the code as fast as possible, it was determined that, as this situation had never occurred before, and as the problem was out of any competitor's control, the most appropriate order was to revert to the original grid.

Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord said: "If you think of the millions of people watching around the world, they tune in for the start and suddenly the cars are all in a jumbled up order because of something that happened 40 minutes earlier and it was behind a safety car on a formation lap. That would have been a much harder thing to explain than resetting and then going from where we did."

"Amazing" was the word Verstappen chose to describe his and Red Bull's first win of the 2026 season at a chaotic, bizarre and, in some ways, unprecedented race.

It would be wrong to say the victory was a complete surprise, as it came after three consecutive podium finishes in which the four-time champion appeared to be edging closer and closer to such an achievement.

But it certainly adds a fresh twist to a season of fluctuating fortunes at the front, in which the only real constant has been Kimi Antonelli, as the championship heads into its final stretch.

It was Verstappen's 72nd victory and it came in a manner entirely familiar to those who have followed his career - but entirely unfamiliar to this season.

The Dutchman was the man all weekend at Sepang, where Verstappen also won the last time the track held a race in 2017. As early as Friday afternoon his rivals were all saying he was going to be difficult to beat.

He duly delivered a dominant win, which barely looked in doubt even through the chaos of a delayed start, software glitches caused by a bug in the mandated FIA engine settings that wreaked havoc for him and several other drivers on a formation lap, losing the lead to the two Mercedes off the line and a late safety car period.

What was remarkable about that, though, is that until Malaysia not once so far this season had Verstappen had been in this position.

Red Bull started this year in a bit of a state.

The fourth fastest car among the big four teams, it was debatable at times in the early races whether their car was even better than that of their junior team, Racing Bulls.

All year, Verstappen has been battling an inconsistent handling balance and there was doubt for some time as to whether he would even stay at Red Bull beyond this year.

Although contracted until the end of 2028, it was widely known there were performance-related clauses in his contract that allowed him to leave, and McLaren courted him in the summer.

In the end, though. Verstappen decided to stay, saying he liked the environment at Red Bull, he had faith they would return to the front, and he did not mind a bit of extra work helping them do it.

Those sentiments were expressed in an interview at the Italian Grand Prix a month ago. He finished third that weekend, but even that recently there was no indication a performance such as this was in the offing.

But a trickle of upgrades in the past few races finally all came together with the introduction of a new floor in Baku, the weekend before Malaysia.

There, awkward circumstances in qualifying left him eighth on the grid when by merit he would have been on the front row. But a late safety car closed up the field, and he spent the final stint right on the gearbox of George Russell's leading Mercedes, and lost out on the win by less than 0.2secs.

Malaysia proved that promise was more than a flash in the pan.

"We had a very complicated and tough start to the year with all sorts of problems and just not being competitive enough,' Verstappen said on Sunday.

"But throughout the year, the team has been working very hard to understand our issues and bring good performance upgrades to the car and make it more driveable.

"Step by step, we've been getting closer and closer, and today, and of course especially this whole weekend, we've been really in good form. So, yeah, it's amazing."

There are six or seven races remaining, depending on whether F1 gets the security reassurances it needs to give it the final confidence to commit to the end of the season grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi in the context of the war in the Middle East.

On this basis, Verstappen could well be a factor in all of them.

If the championship battle had any jeopardy remaining in it, that would certainly up the ante. But Russell's retirement from third place with an engine failure with five laps to go in Malaysia has pretty much eradicated that.

Antonelli's second place and Russell's retirement extended the Italian's lead to 84 points. With either 158 or 183 remaining in total, depending on how the season ends, that size of lead means only some kind of miraculous turn of events could turn the tide back in Russell's favour.

He said: "I don't need to say I think it's gone, but, of course, it's exceptionally unlikely and that's just the reality.

"I knew if I wanted to come back, I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I had luck not on my side.

"So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if it was on the other side it would have been an 18-point gain. So it's a real shame, but that's just how it is."

It's not the first time an engine problem has robbed Russell of big points this year. But Antonelli has had his reliability issues, too, and to about the same level.

The reality is that Antonelli has been the better performer this year - as he was again in Malaysia after his odd off weekend in Baku - and he will deserve the title when it comes.

"So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if it was on the other side it would have been an 18-point gain. So it's a real shame, but that's just how it is."

It's not the first time an engine problem has robbed Russell of big points this year.

"You've almost got to laugh," he said. "I'm beyond disappointment. It's just so many times this season it's happened. It's a real shame. Of course, but just keep on fighting."

But Antonelli has had his reliability issues, too, and to about the same level.

The reality, as Russell has acknowledged many times, is that Antonelli has been the better performer on balance this year - as he was again in Malaysia after his off weekend in Baku - and he will deserve the title when it comes.

title: Lions elevate DB ahead of 'Sunday Night Football' vs Panthers
description: Ahead of its "Sunday Night Football" date at the Carolina Panthers, the Detroit Lions elevated one of their defensive backs from the practice squad.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions (2-1) elevated defensive back Jalen Mills from their practice squad to the active roster ahead of their "Sunday Night Football" date at the Carolina Panthers (1-2). It marks back-to-back weeks where the Lions have elevated Mills to their active roster, as Mills was available for Detroit's Week 3 matchup against the New York Jets.

The Lions signed Mills to their practice squad on Sept. 21. Mills, 32, spent the end of last season in Detroit after the Lions claimed Mills off waivers on Dec. 10.

Originally a seventh-round pick out of LSU by the Eagles in 2016, Mills has played in 122 games and started 92, registering 460 tackles, 60 passes defended, 10 tackles for loss, eight interceptions, seven quarterback hits, three forced fumbles, 1.5 sacks, and one fumble recovery. He has also returned one interception for a touchdown.

Lions have elevated DB Jalen Mills from the Practice Squad to the Active/Inactive list

Mills played in three games with the Lions at the end of last season, logging 65 defensive snaps and 12 special teams snaps, per Pro Football Focus.

Mills has spent time with the Eagles, New England, the Jets, Houston Texans, and the Lions.

Detroit inked Mills after defensive back Avonte Maddox suffered a season-ending foot injury. The Lions are also without safety Thomas Harper, who the organization placed on injured reserve.

Detroit starting safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch both remain sidelined with injuries as Joseph navigates a degenerative condition in his knee and as Branch recovers from a torn Achilles.

title: Roma Reportedly Revive Talks for Real Madrid’s Endrick
description: Roma and Real Madrid could revisit a January loan for Endrick after the Brazilian’s proposed summer move fell apart.
fullText:
They say the transfer market never sleeps. In a world constantly bombarded by status updates and breaking news, it can be hard to tune out the transfer noise and focus on the actual football, to the point where it sometimes feels like the sport itself is nothing more than a minor distraction in between Here We Go updates.

In the case of AS Roma and Real Madrid forward Endrick Felipe Moreira de Sousa, not only has this rumor never gone to bed; it appears stuck on a loop. Two months after missing out on the Los Blancos U-20 sensation, the Giallorossi have circled back to the kid affectionately known as Endrick, with multiple sources in Europe claiming the two sides will return to the bargaining table in January.

While raising €100 million footballers is nothing new to Real Madrid, every now and then, Los Merengues need a little help applying the finishing touches to their most prized assets. Whether it's Nico Paz becoming a world-beater with Como or Franco Mastantuono harnessing his considerable skills with Fiorentina, Italian clubs have found great success incubating talents for Real Madrid.

As talented as Paz and Mastantuono are, Endrick may take the cake. Appearing on numerous top prospect lists over the past several years, including ESPN FC and The Guardian's Next Generation countdown, Endrick has been under the spotlight for several years now, prompting the Spanish club to pay an incredible €47.5 million to acquire his rights from Palmeiras in 2024.

Given their investment in Endrick, Real Madrid has been treating the now-20-year-old with kid gloves. After spending his first season in Spain on the sidelines, Endrick finally got his chance to shine, spending the 2025-2026 season on loan with Lyon, bagging five goals and seven assists in 16 Ligue 1 appearances.

After such a promising season, Real had a bit of an Endrick problem: Was it better to renew his loan, or roll the dice and hope he could crack the rotation under new/old manager José Mourinho at the Bernabéu?

For a brief moment this summer, Madrid seemed to be leaning toward the former, arranging a loan deal with Roma. However, for reasons unknown, Mourinho nixed the deal at the last minute, leaving Endrick's fate twisting in the wind and Roma holding the bag as yet another pacy left winger slipped through their fingers.

However, according to the Corriere dello Sport, Endrick may still make his way to the Eternal City, as the two clubs are reportedly discussing a January loan for the Brazilian winger. The CdS reports that, while Madrid aren't likely to let him go for less than €50 million, Roma may be open to a purely temporary move for Endrick, though that won't prevent them from attempting to arrange a loan with an option or obligation to buy.

The Corriere dello Sport expects the negotiations to pick up when Real Madrid plays Roma at the Stadio Olimpico later this month in the Champions League, so expect plenty of updates later this month.

title: USWNT head coach Emma Hayes has called up Utah Royals defender Kate Del Fava to replace injured Naomi Girma, set to take on No. 1 ranked Spain
description: URFC star center-back Kate Del Fava has finally earned a deserved call-up to the senior USWNT.
fullText:
Today, it was announced that U.S. Women's National Team head coach Emma Hayes has called up Utah Royals defender Kate Del Fava from the U23 team to replace the injured Naomi Girma.

Kate Del Fava via Instagram: "Biggest dream come true."

"Del Fava was already set to travel to Atlanta on Monday as an "overage" player in the U.S. Under-23 Women's National Team training camp that is being held concurrently with Hayes' camp at the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center. She will now just switch hotels."

The URFC star has played every minute for her club since re-joining in 2024. The team is on the verge of making history as they look to book their first-ever NWSL playoff spot.

title: Who's in, who's out for Texans-Cowboys in Week 4?
description: Who is in and who is out for Week 4's matchup between the Houston Texans and the Dallas Cowboys?
fullText:
Who is in and who is out for Week 4's matchup between the Houston Texans and the Dallas Cowboys?

The Texans look to stop the bleeding and pick up their first win against the Cowboys in Week 4. Houston has started slowly out of the gate in the DeMeco Ryans era, going 0-3 in back-to-back seasons, but an 0-4 loss would almost certainly end any playoff chatter behind an elite defense.

The Texans' Week 4 showdown between the Lone Star State foes will air on FOX at 12 p.m. CT on Sunday afternoon. The television commentators for the game are Kenny Albert (play-by-play), Greg Olsen (analyst) and Pam Oliver(sideline).

The big storyline for Houston is the return of Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins and offensive lineman Ed Ingram. Both were cleared to return to practice after missing the past two games and should bolster both the passing attack and run game that's been depleted in back to back losses.

As for the Cowboys, newcomer Joey Porter Jr. is expected to play after missing the first three games with the Pittsburgh Steelers. During an interview on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said they believe the former second-round pick would get "some snaps" in Week 4 after practicing the past two days. "We're just trying to take things day by day, and if everything looks good, then we should be out there," Porter said following his first Cowboys practice on Thursday, per ESPN's Todd Archer.

Here's the actives and inactives for the Texans and Cowboys in Week 4.

title: Fans Call Hawkeyes’ Emotional Tradition ‘Awesome’ After Full Stadium Waves to Hospital Kids
description: No. 5 Ohio State Buckeyes secured a convincing 31-14 victory over the No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes at Kinnick Stadium on Saturday. The loss dropped the Hawkeyes to 4-1. Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught his 36th career touchdown pass, officially breaking Chris Olave’s all-time Ohio State record.
fullText:
No. 5 Ohio State Buckeyes secured a convincing 31-14 victory over the No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes at Kinnick Stadium on Saturday. The loss dropped the Hawkeyes to 4-1. Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught his 36th career touchdown pass, officially breaking Chris Olave's all-time Ohio State record.

Despite the loss, both teams won over college football fans at the end of the first quarter as everyone on the field participated in the traditional "Hawkeye Wave."

At the end of the first quarter, the game paused as players, coaches, and referees joined the crowd to face the UI Stead Family Children's Hospital. Together, thousands of fans turned toward the windows to wave at the young patients watching from above.

ESPN shared a clip of the wholesome moment, which showed officials holding their hats high as the stadium united for the tradition. The video quickly went viral, pulling in over 868,000 views by Sunday morning.

One of the greatest traditions in college football, the “Hawkeye Wave”

Iowa and Ohio State fans, players, and coaches turn to wave at patients in the UI Stead Family Children’s Hospital after the first quarter https://t.co/NApYmeKipX

Former Iowa basketball star Caitlin Clark also took part, joining the children inside the hospital to wave down at the field.

Fans praised the moment online, with many calling it the best part of their day.

One fan wrote, "It's awesome that both teams and the officials joined in. Some things are bigger than football."

Another one added, "The wave gets me every time, kinnick at dusk hits different."

A third one penned, "As a buckeye fan, the Iowa wave is the coolest tradition in college football."

The fourth noted, "The greatest tradition in sports is in Iowa… It doesn't get any better and more heartfelt than that

A random X user claimed, "The most wholesome thing I've ever seen. This is humanity at its peak

Ohio State prepared carefully for the tradition. Coach Ryan Day sent a letter to every patient before kickoff. "We know you are facing challenges that take real strength," Day wrote, noting that his team looked forward to waving from the field.

The Hawkeye Wave has been a staple at Iowa games since 2017. Fan Krista Young first suggested the idea on Facebook, prompting the stadium's first collective wave during a 24-3 win over Wyoming. Coach Kirk Ferentz called it a "grass-roots" movement at the time.

Ohio State first participated later that season on Nov. 4, 2017. To keep the focus on the children, Iowa has allowed its weekly Kid Captain to pick the accompanying song for every home game since 2022.

fullText:
Breiden Fehoko has demanded accountability from the Los Angeles Chargers after their 0-3 start, naming offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, general manager Joe Hortiz and head coach Jim Harbaugh as possible candidates to be fired if the team loses again.

Los Angeles entered Sunday's Week 4 road game against the Seattle Seahawks averaging 14.7 points, leaving the former Chargers defensive lineman frustrated with the direction of his old team.

Fehoko shared a blunt message on X before the Chargers faced Seattle at Lumen Field.

"After the chargers lose tomorrow I don't care who but someone needs to be fired. Whether it's Mike McDaniel, Joe Hortiz, or Jim Harbaugh. Stop leading fans with false hope and start taking accountability," said Fehoko.

After the chargers lose tomorrow I don’t care who but someone needs to be fired. Whether it’s Mike McDaniel, Joe Hortiz, or Jim Harbaugh. Stop leading fans with false hope and start taking accountability.

— Breiden Fehoko (@BreidenFehoko) October 4, 2026

The comments placed responsibility across the organization rather than focusing only on the coaching staff. McDaniel oversees the offense, Hortiz controls personnel decisions as general manager and Harbaugh remains responsible for the team's overall direction.

Fehoko spent three seasons with the Chargers from 2020 through 2022 before joining the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2023.

His criticism followed an 0-3 start in which the Chargers lost 26-14 to the Arizona Cardinals, 26-14 to the Las Vegas Raiders and 24-16 to the Buffalo Bills.

Fehoko's prediction added more pressure before Los Angeles visited a Seattle team that entered Week 4 with a 2-1 record.

McDaniel's offense entered the Seattle game ranked 29th in scoring at 14.7 points per game. The Chargers had scored 44 points through their first three games while averaging 308.7 yards per contest.

Justin Herbert completed 52 of 88 passes for 627 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions during that stretch. His 59.1% completion rate and 73.4 passer rating reflected the offense's early struggle to find consistency.

McDaniel accepted responsibility for the unit's poor start, while Harbaugh publicly maintained his confidence in the offensive coordinator.

Three games would still be a small sample for any major organizational decision. However, Fehoko's post captured the frustration surrounding a winless team that entered the season expecting to contend.

Another loss would not guarantee a coaching or front-office change, but it would intensify questions about McDaniel's offense and the direction established by Harbaugh and Hortiz.

title: 'I messed up': Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer takes accountability for costly error in Rio loss
description: With Dallas heading into Week 4 under .500, Schottenheimer reportedly acknowledged his own mistakes in clock management from Week 3.
fullText:
'I messed up': Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer takes accountability for costly error in Rio loss originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

As the Cowboys head into a Week 4 matchup with the Texans, they find themselves under .500 due to a last-second loss to the Ravens in Rio.

Tyler Loop's walk-off field goal in Week 3 beat Dallas, which gave Baltimore the ball back with seven seconds remaining. Over the past week, the Cowboys have taken plenty of heat for their clock management.

At one point, head coach Brian Schottenheimer reportedly spoke to his players, acknowledging his own fault in the loss.

Here's what's known about Schottenheimer's apology to Cowboys players for how the team handled the end of the Week 3 Ravens loss.

MORE: NFL Week 4 power rankings

In the final minutes of Cowboys vs. Ravens, Dallas had an easy chance to tie the game, if not win. With 23 seconds remaining and trailing 31-28, the Cowboys had 1st & Goal, able to tie with an easy field goal, if not go into the end zone for the win. Time, of course, was also a factor, looking to leave little time for the Ravens to answer.

The next four Cowboys plays went:

Incompletion (20 seconds remaining afterward)

2-yard scramble from Dak Prescott (14 seconds remaining afterward, final timeout)

Incompletion (7 seconds remaining afterward)

Brandon Aubrey's kick tied the game at 31 for the Cowboys, but the time remaining meant they would have to kick off to the Ravens. Miraculously, after a touchback on the kickoff that took no time off the clock, Baltimore advanced the ball enough to call a timeout, then win the game.

According to ESPN, Schottenheimer, who admitted that he "overcoached" his quarterback, instructed Prescott to throw the ball away at the end of the game on the Cowboys' final play before their own field goal. He had the option to go through his progressions to guarantee an incomplete pass, or take one read and throw the ball away if a receiver wasn't open.

Ultimately, Dallas left too much time on the clock to play it safe, and Schottenheimer addressed the team last week to take accountability.

#Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer on Sunday's ending vs. the #Ravens: "I didn't do very good in the last 28 seconds. ... I felt like I overcoached Dak on 3rd down. ... I'll take accountability for it. I hurt our chances to win that game. I'll be better. And I'm better than that." https://t.co/3B1DaWa9f8

The head coach told his players that "if a coach is going to hold players accountable, he must apply the same standard to himself," per ESPN, and Cowboys players "responded in a positive way."

"I make a lot of mistakes," Schottenheimer told reporters after the game. "I'm certainly not perfect. ... I hurt our chance to win that game, and I'll be better."

title: Commanders QB Marcus Mariota out for the rest of the game vs Colts
description: Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota is out for the rest of the game against the Indianapolis Colts due to a knee injury.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders entered their game against the Indianapolis Colts without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels because of a left elbow injury. Now, they are without backup quarterback Marcus Mariota for the rest of the game because of a knee injury. He left in the first quarter, and rookie Athan Kaliakmanis has been in the game since.

"We're gutted for him," head coach Dan Quinn told the NFL Network at the start of the third quarter. "He'll be out for the rest of the game."

In addition to Mariota being out for the rest of this game, defensive end Charles Omenihu was also ruled out with a groin injury. Both injuries add to the Commanders' ongoing injury problems this season, as they were already dealing with numerous players, including Daniels and star receiver Terry McLaurin, going into this game.

Mariota was playing well prior to his injury with three completions for 46 yards as well as a 35-yard run that set up Washington's second field goal of the game. He was also coming off his performance against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3, which gave the Commanders their first win of the season.

While the extent of Mariota's injury is currently unknown, Quinn seemed concerned. Mariota has a long injury history, though he has not had significant knee issues. With Kaliakmanis as the only healthy quarterback on the roster, Washington will likely be in the market for a quarterback after this game, whether they acquire one in a trade or free agency.

fullText:

The New England Patriots have struggled a lot to start the 2026 season. Patriots QB Drake Maye has not looked good, playing poorly through the first three games of the year. It appears that scouts around the NFL all share the same concerning opinion about Maye in his third professional season.

NFL writer Ralph Vacchiano asked multiple people around the league about Maye after his rough start to the season. Scouts did not have kind things to say about the third-year quarterback.

"He looks like a rookie, and not a particularly good one," one AFC scout told Vacchiano. "If he were anyone else, based on those three games, the [coaching] staff would say, 'He's just not ready yet.' But how do you say that about a guy who nearly won MVP?"

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This is a shocking development for Maye, who almost won MVP last season. He has 585 passing yards with one touchdowns and six interceptions through three games this year. To make matters worse, Maye already has some incredible bloopers after making some comical mistakes in recent games.

Another scout noted that Maye "looks lost" so far during the 2026 season.

"His confidence is completely gone, and you can see why," the scout added, per Vacchiano. "He's making comical errors — like real rookie stuff. The ball popping out of his hand, lofting it towards tightly covered receivers with no zip on the ball, not seeing any of the coverage in the area and thinking a guy is open, not stepping up in the pocket to avoid the rush, or stepping up into it. It seems like every other decision he makes is wrong."

Something is clearly wrong with Maye this season, but it is difficult to pinpoint exactly why. Luck could be part of the equation, but Maye's confidence now seems to be gone either way.

Unfortunately, Maye is unlikely to get his confidence back in Week 4 while going up against the NFL's best team.

fullText:
Mississippi State Bulldogs saw its unbeaten start end on Saturday, and the bigger worry came late. The 16th-ranked Bulldogs fell 56-23 to No. 7 Alabama in Starkville, a game that ran away from them early. Sophomore quarterback Kamario Taylor was visibly limited before he left the field in the fourth quarter. Coach Jeff Lebby has now given a first look at what comes next.

Mississippi State is not rushing to put a timeline on its star quarterback, and Lebby's update was short.

"It will be day-to-day for him. We'll let the injury report Wednesday for LSU speak to where we're at," Lebby told reporters.

The school has not named the injury. Taylor left early in the fourth quarter and walked to the locker room with team staff. He later appeared on the sideline in a walking boot.

Taylor picked up a lower-leg issue in the win over Missouri a week earlier, and Lebby praised him for playing through it. The effects showed on the field.

Taylor finished 19-of-34 for 258 yards and three touchdowns. He also threw two interceptions, lost a fumble and was sacked five times. His rushing line read minus-26 yards on six carries.

That lack of movement hurt a dual-threat passer who had been among the nation's most dangerous players. Alabama outgained Mississippi State 179-18 on the ground, and backup Parker Puckett finished the game.

Lebby later admitted, "It's pretty obvious that he wasn't able to do anything with his legs."

Before Saturday, a different Taylor story was already shaping the past week, and it explains why this injury matters so much.

Taylor's name was already everywhere before kickoff. Last weekend, Nick Saban said on College GameDay that he would try to get Taylor into the transfer portal. The comment sparked days of debate, and Paul Finebaum later blamed Saban for stirring it up.

Taylor answered quickly: "If you know me, you know I bleed maroon and white."

His play backed up the message. He entered Alabama week tied for the FBS lead with 14 touchdown passes, and he extended a streak of three-plus scoring throws to five games, the first by an SEC quarterback since Jayden Daniels in 2023.

That makes his health the biggest story around the program now. Mississippi State built its offense around his arm and legs, and the loss showed how much that plan relies on both.

Mississippi State sits at 4-1 and gets a bye week before visiting LSU on Oct. 17. Alabama moves to 5-0 and hosts Georgia on Oct. 10. Taylor's Wednesday injury report before the LSU trip will shape how the Bulldogs plan.

description: Baker Mayfield is facing a significant spell on the sidelines after suffering a thumb injury that has suddenly changed Tampa Bay’s plans at quarterback. fullText:
Baker Mayfield is facing a significant spell on the sidelines after suffering a thumb injury that has suddenly changed Tampa Bay's plans at quarterback. The Buccaneers will now have to turn to a player who entered the NFL without hearing his name called during the draft.

Mayfield is expected to miss three to six weeks, according to NFL insider Adam Schefter. The exact timeline will depend on when the veteran quarterback can grip the football well enough to return.

Schefter reported on X that Mayfield is dealing with a dislocated thumb and could miss several games. That leaves undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels in line for the biggest opportunity of his young career.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will become the first rookie quarterback this season to start a game. None of the 10 rookie quarterbacks drafted this year — Fernando Mendoza, Ty Simpson, Carson Beck, Drew Allar, Cade Klubnik, Cole Payton, Taylen Green, Athan Kaliakmanis, Behren… https://t.co/qzolflN19h

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 4, 2026

Daniels was not expected to be Tampa Bay's starting quarterback when the season began. Now, an injury to Mayfield has pushed him into a role that could last long enough to shape the Buccaneers' season.

The timing makes the opportunity even more unusual because Daniels is set to become the first rookie quarterback to start a game this season. None of the 10 quarterbacks selected in the 2026 NFL Draft had made a start entering Week 4.

That list includes first-round picks Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson, along with Carson Beck, Drew Allar and Cade Klubnik. Daniels will get there before all of them, despite entering the league as an undrafted player.

Schefter pointed out the unusual situation after reporting Mayfield's injury. The Buccaneers rookie will now become the first player from this year's rookie quarterback class to make an NFL start, even though he was not one of the 10 quarterbacks selected in the draft.

That says as much about opportunity as it does about Daniels. Injuries can change a team's plans quickly, and Mayfield's thumb injury has created a chance that Daniels likely could not have expected this early in his career.

The challenge ahead is much bigger than just the hype surrounding his first career start. Daniels now has to run an entire NFL offense while Tampa Bay figures out how to survive without its starting quarterback, who could be sidelined for over a month.

For now, the Buccaneers are left with an unusual quarterback story. Mayfield's injury has taken their veteran starter out of the lineup, while an undrafted rookie has suddenly moved ahead of an entire draft class and into the record books.

title: Jerry Jones Demands Answers After Brian Schottenheimer Owns Cowboys’ Costly Mistakes: ‘I Messed Up’
description: Jerry Jones made clear that accountability alone could not explain how the Dallas Cowboys squandered their opportunity to beat the Baltimore Ravens. The Cowboys owner wanted an evaluation of the mistakes and assurances that they would not happen again. Before Jones delivered that public challenge, coach Brian Schottenheimer had already confronted his team. He walked […] The post Jerry Jones Demands Answers After Brian Schottenheimer Owns Cowboys’ Costly Mistakes: ‘I Messed Up’ appeared first on
fullText:
Jerry Jones made clear that accountability alone could not explain how the Dallas Cowboys squandered their opportunity to beat the Baltimore Ravens. The Cowboys owner wanted an evaluation of the mistakes and assurances that they would not happen again.

Before Jones delivered that public challenge, coach Brian Schottenheimer had already confronted his team. He walked to the lectern during a meeting and acknowledged that his decisions contributed to the 34-31 loss in Rio de Janeiro.

Schottenheimer's opening message was effectively that he had messed up, according to ESPN's reporting from people inside the meeting. The wording was a paraphrase rather than a direct quotation, but his larger point was clear.

If Schottenheimer expected players to accept responsibility for their mistakes, he had to apply the same standard to himself. One person in the room characterized his approach as an example of a leader operating from the front.

The meeting followed a series of breakdowns during the final 28 seconds against Baltimore. Dallas reached first-and-goal at the Ravens' 2-yard line with 23 seconds remaining and one timeout.

A false start moved the Cowboys backward. Dak Prescott then scrambled on second down before Dallas used its final timeout, leaving 14 seconds for a third-and-goal play.

Schottenheimer later said he "overcoached" Prescott by giving him instructions that placed the quarterback in an unfamiliar mindset. Prescott quickly threw the ball away, forcing Dallas to settle for Brandon Aubrey's tying 23-yard field goal.

"I make a lot of mistakes," Schottenheimer told reporters. "I'm certainly not perfect. … I hurt our chance to win that game, and I'll be better."

ESPN reported that Cowboys players responded positively to Schottenheimer's private admission and turned their attention toward their game against the Houston Texans. His message accepted responsibility without shifting the blame to Prescott or another part of the team.

Aubrey's field goal left seven seconds on the clock, but his ensuing kickoff went through the end zone for a touchback. Baltimore received the ball at its 35-yard line without losing any time.

Lamar Jackson completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers, setting up Tyler Loop's winning 56-yard field goal. Schottenheimer also acknowledged communication failures surrounding the kickoff and Dallas' final defensive call.

Jones addressed the ending Tuesday during his appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

"They don't have one that they're satisfied with," Jones said. "We made mistakes during that time. There's no question about it. So there is no explanation."

Jones did not publicly question Schottenheimer's job security or reject his decision to accept responsibility. His message was that taking ownership of the failure could not replace identifying its causes.

Schottenheimer demonstrated accountability by standing before his players and acknowledging his role in the loss. Whether that moment produces meaningful change will become clear the next time the Cowboys must manage a game in its final seconds.

description: Philip Ellis’ late pass completed a four-win run across the final five races and secured both the GTD drivers’ and Mercedes-AMG manufacturers’ championships
fullText:
Winward Racing capped off a historic campaign in dramatic fashion, securing its first Motul Petit Le Mans victory and wrapping up a third consecutive Grand Touring Daytona (GTD) championship at the 2026 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship finale. Drivers Philip Ellis, Russell Ward, and endurance co-driver Indy Dontje steered the #57 Mercedes-AMG GT3 across the finish line to seal both the race victory and the class crown.

The championship was effectively decided early in the race as its main title rivals hit trouble. The #27 Heart of Racing Team Aston Martin Vantage GT3 Evo, which entered the weekend 116 points behind, was forced into an overnight engine change that required Zacharie Robichon to start from pit lane; the car fell more than 60 laps behind before eventually retiring. Meanwhile, second-place contender Turner Motorsport suffered a race-ending blow just 30 minutes after the green flag when Robby Foley pitted the #96 BMW M4 GT3 EVO with a water-pressure issue that proved terminal.

AMAZING BATTLE FOR P1 IN GTD CLASS! Battle between @LWadouxD44 in @AFCorse #21 and Philip Ellis in @WinwardRacing #57 #IMSA #IMSApl #PetitLeMans https://t.co/v9f09GJwYh

— Jędrzej Bocian #IMSApl (@JBocianIMSA) October 4, 2026

Despite locking up the season title early, the fight for the race win remained unsettled until the final minutes. Ellis withstood intense pressure from Riccardo Pera in the #912 Manthey 1st Phorm Porsche 911 GT3 R before passing Lilou Wadoux for the lead on Lap 320. Wadoux was piloting the #21 AF Corse USA Ferrari 296 GT3 EVO — a car that had quickly rebounded from a stop-plus-60-second penalty incurred during Antonio Fuoco's stint.

A late full-course caution ultimately relieved the GTD leaders' dire fuel concerns, allowing Ellis to manage energy through the final restart and secure Winward's maiden Petit Le Mans trophy.

"I think I might have yelled at my engineer trying to get more information out of him," Ellis said.

"No, It was super tight. Obviously the yellow saved a lot of the cars that were on the same strategy. Until the yellow came out, we knew we had no chance of making it. With the yellow, there was a very slim chance of making it. We had to have the prototypes lap us for one.

"I had saved fuel on the last five or six laps after the restart, and that despite having the 9, 12 up behind us, having a bit more energy than us, so they could push a bit more, gamble on that extra lap, whereas we couldn't.

"I was on the radio telling my engineer I'm just going to stay out and hope that either we have a yellow or it's going to be enough till the end.

"Yeah, I was a little bit lucky at some points with the prototypes coming through where I could save a bit more fuel, remake it to the end. Glad it worked out that way."

The victory completed a remarkable second-half surge for Ellis and team owner-driver Ward, with Dontje joining for the endurance rounds. Over the season's final five races, the team recorded four victories and a runner-up finish at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, completing the second-largest championship comeback since IMSA introduced its restructured points system in 2021.

Winward's third straight title stands as the longest active championship streak by any program across all IMSA classes and clinched the manufacturer crown for Mercedes-AMG. Ward credited the team's mechanics for establishing the approach needed to complete the run after the team was caught up in an incident at Watkins Glen.

"Hats off to the dedicated group of people," Ward said. "When we got taken out at Watkins Glen, involved in the incident between the #70 car and the #13, I mean, us three drivers were pretty sorry in the paddock, looking at the car, watching the mechanics just jump all over it.

Laurens Vanthoor holds off BMW to give Porsche historic IMSA Petit Le Mans win

"From our standpoint we thought the race was done, let's pack this thing up, move on to the next. Those guys were like, 'Hell, no. We need to get out there and capitalize on points.' They really set the tone for the second half of the season. We can't quit, keep pushing as hard as we can.

"We went on a five-race streak with podiums, four wins and a second in Indianapolis, which very well could have been a win as well. Could have been five wins in a row. That really just set us up."

title: FIA Don’t Buy Norris’ Explanation For Erratic Bahrain GP Drive Amid Painful Outing
description: The FIA didn’t buy the excuse from Lando Norris about low sun for erratic driving at the end of the dismal F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia for the Brit. Already the start didn’t work for McLaren’s Norris at the F1…
fullText:
The FIA didn't buy the excuse from Lando Norris about low sun for erratic driving at the end of the dismal F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia for the Brit.

Already the start didn't work for McLaren's Norris at the F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia when he switched to medium tyres on a wet track which set him to the back of the field. He had to work through it for several laps and the moment things started to come back on him, the safety car was deployed.

It neutralised some of the advantages of the pack, which did not help Norris' case. In hindsight, the Brit would have boxed like teammate Oscar Piastri did, even though he caught the back of the Australian later in the race. He didn't have enough data eventually to take the right call.

"It felt maybe a little bit of a risk because the slick on a wet track is always a bit of a risk, but there's enough people on it that it kind of, it was quite convincing at the time that it was supposedly going to be the right decision," said Norris to media after the F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

"And the laps to the grid on the inter, when it was a similar kind of condition, they had so much grip and my inter was completely shredded after one lap. Yeah, we were convinced that slick would work, but I think it was just the fact you've never really been on the inter before, it made things just felt a lot better than they should have done in a way.

"So, if we would have had a read on an inter from a previous weekend, maybe I would have been able to understand it more, but that convinced us and it clearly convinced a lot of people. Yeah, obviously Oscar probably made the right decision in pit boxing. And we got it wrong today, that's all. Proved that we shouldn't have any of that stuff with the electronic signs," summed up Norris.

As noted, he made some recovery to be around seventh and eighth. At max, he would have finished either sixth ahead of teammate Piastri or seventh behind him after Mercedes' George Russell stopped towards the end. However, a mistake by the Brit meant he was only ninth in the end.

He recovered a couple of places after dropping outside the Top 10, but couldn't get by Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso. He was summoned by the FIA stewards for erratic driving when he almost clouted the back of Piastri when Russell stopped and was also checked for unsafe re-join.

In his explanation, Norris highlighted low sunlight which caught him out as he couldn't assess what happened ahead of him. When he did, he braked as hard, which is why he went off. He re-joined in front of Aston Martin's Lance Stroll, but was cleared of any wrong there.

He was also checked for overtaking under a safety car, whether at Piastri or Stroll, but the FIA cleared him in both cases. However, they did not buy Norris' excuse of low sunlight and reprimanded him for driving erratically. He escaped any major penalty as the stewards cautioned him to be better in judgement.

"The Stewards also considered that, particularly while driving behind the Safety Car, NOR should have managed the gap to the cars ahead and his closing speed with greater care," said the FIA in the stewards note. "The prevailing visibility conditions were circumstances which NOR should have taken into account when determining an appropriate speed and gap tothe cars ahead, rather than a reason which excused the resulting driving.

"The need for heavy braking and an avoiding manoeuvre into the gravel demonstrated that NOR had not maintained an appropriate margin in the circumstances. The Stewards therefore determined that NOR had driven erratically in breach of Article B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations.

"Such a situation should not arise while driving behind the Safety Car, and NOR was required to maintain a sufficient margin to the cars ahead. However, taking into account that NOR reacted promptly once he recognised the situation and successfully avoided contact, the Stewards consider a Reprimand as appropriate," the note summed up.

Norris, meanwhile, said: "It's just everyone just hit the brakes into Turn 1 because of George. And I was far enough back that I couldn't really see how slow they were going and it caught me out." The Brit, though, lamented the continued lack of straightline speed on his side.

He says it is painful and hurting. "I have no idea, I mean the team are trying, but I'm losing almost two tenths every lap," continued Norris. "Two tenths a lap over 55 laps, it's just painful as hell, so it's making my life pretty damn difficult.

"But there's also other things, like today I could have done better, so I can't just have that. That's not just an excuse, but there's also things I can do better and the team to do better as well."

title: Arizona State's third-down defense struggles mightily in Baylor loss
description: Baylor finished the game 9-for-15 on 3rd downs, with multiple explosive plays. The Bears had gains of 27 yards, 19 yards and 11 yards on third downs.
fullText:
Prior to the Baylor game, most of Arizona State's fans' complaints centered on the offensive side of the ball. Now, that attention is likely to turn to the defense.

ASU's defense had almost no answers for Baylor's offense, particularly on third down. That part of the defense hasn't been a concern for ASU under defensive coordinator Brian Ward, but it was exposed in the blowout 55-19 loss to Baylor on Oct. 3.

Baylor finished the game 9-for-15 on third downs, with multiple explosive plays. The Bears had gains of 27 yards, 19 yards and 11 yards on third downs, just in the first half alone. At one point, Baylor was 8-for-11 on third-down conversion attempts.

Coming into the game, ASU was allowing opponents to convert 30% of their third downs — tied for 27th in the NCAA. But that was nowhere to be seen against Baylor. The unit looked completely different.

With 9:29 left in the third quarter, ASU students started to file out of Mountain America Stadium in Tempe.

"We couldn't create a pass rush," coach Kenny Dillingham said. "If you can't create a pass rush — they were getting the ball downfield because you can't create a pass rush — you're not going to be good on third-down defense. Then, you gotta give them credit. They throw some nice back shoulders too. They made some plays on one-on-one situations."

Dillingham emphasized the need to create a pass rush and what his team is doing to start it.

"As a coaching staff, we gotta evaluate that, what we're doing to create a pass rush," he said. "You gotta impact the quarterback. He wasn't impacted in the game, got into a good rhythm. The wideouts were playing well, and they got into a rhythm with him."

ASU finished the game with two sacks and five quarterback hurries.

There were also plays of 63 yards, 32 yards, 25 yards, 17 yards and 15 yards, all coming in the first half as well. Missed tackles were left all over the field. There were wide-open holes for Baylor's offense, both in the running game and passing game. Baylor had 496 yards of offense by the end of the third quarter. The Bears finished the game with 564 yards.

It was part of a dismal night on defense for ASU, which allowed the most points in a game since the 59-23 loss to Arizona in 2023.

Linebacker Owen Long said it isn't on one person or position group.

"It just obviously wasn't good enough tonight," Long said. "Not a good feeling right now. I don't know exactly what to say specifically. I have to go back and watch the tape, but including myself and everyone else, we've got to find a way to get better. So it starts right after this, tomorrow. Just find a way to get better. We just have to get back to work and find exactly what's going on.

"But it's on everyone. It's not just one person. Everyone's got to do a little bit better. It's just feeling the vibe in the locker room already. We just have to find a way to keep getting better."

Was there any hangover from the long overseas trip to London two weeks ago, followed by the bye week? Maybe. ASU's journey to London for the Kansas game was 10,518 miles, making it the longest trip of the 2026 NCAA season for any team.

But Dillingham thought his team was mentally prepared for the game.

"I'm still getting a feel for this team," he said. "Every team has different energy. Some are very passionate, emotional. Some, that's not really their deal. I'm getting a better feel for what this team's 'play good' is. But I thought we were fine going into the game. I liked our energy, our focus, our week of practice, and that's the disappointing thing. I gotta figure out why that didn't translate."

There will be a lot of soul-searching after the performance, which also took place in front of a large crowd of high school recruits that ASU brought in. There were a handful of Golden Ticket recipients at the game.

This is one of the lowest points of the Dillingham era since the 2023 season, when the Sun Devils were just trying to hang on with a depleted roster in Dillingham's first season on the job.

"It was an atrocious game," Dillingham said. "We can either point the finger at who was wrong, or we can all take extreme ownership and fix it. The blessing and the curse of it is we've lost games poorly before, and we've bounced back from those games. I think our guys are gonna respond great."

Logan Stanley is a sports reporter with The Arizona Republic who primarily focuses on high school, college and Olympic sports. fullText:

fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers have released their inactive lists ahead of Sunday's Week 4 matchup at Raymond James Stadium.

The biggest absence for Tampa Bay is quarterback Baker Mayfield, who will miss his first start as a Buccaneer after dislocating his right thumb against Minnesota. Mayfield's absence ends a streak of 57 consecutive starts for Tampa Bay, including the postseason, and clears the way for rookie Jalon Daniels to make his first NFL start.

Outside linebacker Rueben Bain Jr., tight end Ko Kieft and cornerback Benjamin Morrison are also inactive after being ruled out Friday. Defensive lineman DeMonte Capehart and guards Luke Haggard and Billy Schrauth round out Tampa Bay's list.

There is some positive news for the Bucs. Cornerback Jacob Parrish, linebacker SirVocea Dennis and defensive lineman Rakeem Nuñez-Roches were all questionable entering the weekend but are active Sunday.

Green Bay will be without four players, including three offensive linemen. Guards Aaron Banks and Kevin Zeitler and offensive lineman Jacob Monk are inactive, as is defensive lineman Anthony Campbell. Zeitler was signed by the Packers earlier this week, while rookie guard Jager Burton — who entered the weekend questionable with a groin injury — is active.

The Buccaneers and Packers kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

title: NFL Players Coughed Up $300K in Week 2 Fines Before Unsportsmanlike Conduct Penalties Dropped 79%
description: NFL players received 22 unsportsmanlike conduct fines totaling $300,089 in Week 2, creating one of the most expensive stretches of the young season. The league’s latest accountability report showed a very different picture in Week 3. Five players received unsportsmanlike conduct fines totaling $63,908, representing a 78.7% decline from the previous week. NFL Unsportsmanlike Conduct […] The post NFL Players Coughed Up $300K in Week 2 Fines Before Unsportsmanlike Conduct Penalties Dropped 79% appe
fullText:
NFL players received 22 unsportsmanlike conduct fines totaling $300,089 in Week 2, creating one of the most expensive stretches of the young season.

The league's latest accountability report showed a very different picture in Week 3. Five players received unsportsmanlike conduct fines totaling $63,908, representing a 78.7% decline from the previous week.

The NFL fined Lee Hunter, Quinn Meinerz, Jaylen Waddle, Mack Hollins and Abdul Carter for unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 3.

Meinerz and Waddle were fined $14,926 each for illegal celebrations and vulgar acts. Hunter received a $10,174 fine for taunting, while Hollins and Carter were each fined $11,941 for taunting.

Those five fines totaled $63,908. That was $236,181 less than the $300,089 that players were fined for unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 2.

The number of fines also fell sharply. Week 2 produced 22 unsportsmanlike conduct fines, compared to only five in Week 3. That represents a 77.3% decrease.

Hollins also received a separate $22,500 fine for unnecessary roughness involving the use of his helmet on the same play as his taunting violation. That fine is not included in the Week 3 unsportsmanlike conduct total.

The league recorded 30 fined plays across all violation categories in Week 3, down from 38 in Week 2.

In Week 2, the NFL handed out 22 fines for unsportsmanlike conduct to just 13 players. The penalties covered everything from illegal celebrations and taunting to vulgar acts and obscene gestures, with several players getting hit with multiple fines.

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase received two $14,926 fines for obscene gestures. Teammate Tee Higgins received four fines, including three for obscene gestures and one for an illegal celebration or vulgar act.

Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown received four fines for illegal celebrations and vulgar acts. Jahmyr Gibbs and Penei Sewell were also fined for the same violation, while Jameson Williams received separate fines for taunting and an illegal celebration.

San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk received two $14,926 fines for duplicating his 'Juice' chugging celebration against the Miami Dolphins, which the NFL ruled an offensive demonstration. Teammate Upton Stout was fined $7,501 for taunting during the same game.

Week 3 still produced several notable fines, but the volume did not approach what players faced one week earlier. Unsportsmanlike conduct accounted for only five of the league's 30 fined plays, bringing the combined cost down by nearly 79%.

title: Why at least 1 ‘NFL QB evaluator’ thinks Giants’ JJ McCarthy can be saved after Vikings disaster
description: JJ McCarthy’s Minnesota Vikings tenure may have unraveled. However, his arrival with the New York Giants could give the former first-round pick a much-needed second chance. fullText:
Why at least 1 'NFL QB evaluator' thinks Giants' JJ McCarthy can be saved after Vikings disaster appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

JJ McCarthy's Minnesota Vikings tenure may have unraveled. However, his arrival with the New York Giants could give the former first-round pick a much-needed second chance. At least one NFL quarterback evaluator believes McCarthy can rebuild his career in New York. A familiar coaching connection and reduced expectations could help him regain his footing.

Speaking to FOX Sports, the evaluator pointed to head coach John Harbaugh's connection to his brother, Jim Harbaugh, who coached McCarthy at Michigan, as a potential advantage.

"A fresh start with people that chose him is a good thing," the evaluator said. "The Harbaugh history helps, too. Matt Nagy, I would think, knows what he's doing, too."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

McCarthy also will not immediately carry the burden of rescuing the Giants' franchise. With Jaxson Dart sidelined by knee surgery, veteran Jameis Winston will handle the starting job. That leaves McCarthy room to develop without the pressure of being New York's unquestioned answer at quarterback. The evaluator compared the situation to quarterbacks such as Mac Jones, Sam Darnold, and Baker Mayfield. They found opportunities to reset their careers after difficult initial stops.

Selected 10th overall by Minnesota in 2024, McCarthy missed his first season after meniscus surgery before making 10 starts in 2025. He threw 11 touchdowns against 12 interceptions. He also showed flashes of potential but struggled to establish consistency. Minnesota subsequently traded him to New York for a 2027 fifth-round pick. McCarthy's path back to a starting role remains uncertain. Still, the Giants offer him an opportunity to reset without carrying the entire franchise. If he can sharpen his decision-making and improve his consistency, the change of scenery could keep his NFL future alive.

title: Joey Porter Jr. active for Cowboys days after trade, eyeing first action of season
description: — Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was active for Dallas against Houston on Sunday just days after he was traded from Pittsburgh.
fullText:
HOUSTON (AP) — Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was active for Dallas against Houston on Sunday just days after he was traded from Pittsburgh.

If he plays Sunday, it will be his first action of the season after he was inactive for the first three games while upset about his contract situation and dealing with a back issue.

Porter was acquired to boost a secondary that has been plagued by injuries.

The 26-year-old Porter, a second-round pick out of Penn State in the 2023 draft, is in the final year of his four-year rookie deal.

The Cowboys agreed to the trade for Porter on Wednesday after earlier putting safety Jalen Thompson (hamstring) on injured reserve with a designation to return. They also signed three defensive backs to their practice squad.

Safety P.J. Locke (torn plantar fascia) was already on injured reserve. He and Thompson were offseason acquisitions by the Cowboys as they revamped their secondary.

title: England call up late replacement for injured Nico O’Reilly
description: O’Reilly was sent back to Man City for ‘further assessment’ ahead of the Croatia rout and Thomas Tuchel has now called up another left-back ahead of Tuesday’s game against Czech Republic
fullText:
Thomas Tuchel has belatedly called up a replacement for the injured Nico O'Reilly, with Manchester City teammate Rico Lewis being added to the England squad.

O'Reilly completed 90 minutes in England's Nations League opener earlier in the international window but made a crucial error for Spain's second goal as the Three Lions fell to a 3-2 defeat.

The 21-year-old left-back then missed England's 2-0 victory over Czech Republic in Prague after suffering an injury in training and was sent back to his club for "further assessment" ahead of Saturday's 7-0 thrashing of Croatia in Rijeka.

In the aftermath of O'Reilly's departure, the Football Association (FA) confirmed that no replacement would be added to the squad, with a statement reading: "Nico O'Reilly has returned to Manchester City and will play no part in the forthcoming Uefa Nations League fixtures.

"No further replacements are planned as the Three Lions prepare to face Croatia in Rijeka on Saturday before returning to Wembley to take on Czechia on Tuesday."

As the statement intimates, England have one game left in this extended international window, with Czech Republic visiting Wembley on Tuesday evening, and the FA have changed their stance, with Lewis now being given a call-up.

The 21-year-old has been promoted from Lee Carsley's under-21s squad, whom he helped secure qualification for the 2027 U21 European Championships earlier in this international break.

Lewis has won five caps for the senior England team, with his debut coming against North Macedonia in November 2023 and his most recent cap coming a year later against Greece.

He is yet to play a match under Tuchel but could be in line to make his first international appearance for 23 months against the Czechs, with Lewis Hall the only other full-time left-back in the squad.

The Newcastle star played 90 minutes in the win over Czech Republic and started against Croatia before Myles Lewis-Skelly – who is more often utilised in midfield these days – replaced him late on.

Hall impressed in both matches but Tuchel may deem three games in a week a needless workload for the 22-year-old, perhaps giving Lewis the chance to shine at full-back.

title: Harry Kane moves into tie for 7th place on all-time international scorers list
description: The Bayern Munich and England striker is an incredible goalscorer.
fullText:
Harry Kane has added another remarkable milestone to an international career that is already loaded with them.

The England captain has moved into seventh place on the all-time international goalscoring list, reaching 89 goals for the Three Lions. Kane is now level with Malaysia legend Mokhtar Dahari and sits within striking distance of another Bayern Munich legend, Robert Lewandowski, who has 92 goals.

Kane is now alongside some of the greatest international goalscorers the sport has ever produced. The list is topped by Cristiano Ronaldo with 146 goals, followed by Lionel Messi (125), Iran's Ali Daei (108), India's Sunil Chhetri (95), Belgium's Romelu Lukaku (94), and Lewandowski (92).

Harry Kane now has 89 goals for England, putting him in 7th place in the all-time list of international top scorers pic.twitter.com/fzlUMhiHpM

At 33 years old, the Bayern Munich striker has already established himself as England's all-time leading scorer, and his continued international output means the players immediately ahead of him are firmly within reach.

Lukaku is only five goals ahead, Chhetri is six ahead, and Lewandowski is just three ahead.

That makes his climb up the leaderboard particularly compelling. Kane could realistically pass several legends before his England career comes to an end, even if Cristiano Ronaldo's record remains in another realm entirely.

For Bayern Munich fans, there is another reason to appreciate this milestone. Kane's goalscoring feats for England place him in the same historical conversation as Lewandowski — and Kane still has plenty of football left to play.

Knowing Harry Kane, he likely already has the next milestone in his sights.
