title: Carlos Alcaraz sends message to Denis Shapovalov on social media after he retired injured from their Japan Open match
description: Carlos Alcaraz has made it through to the semifinals of the Japan Open after knocking out Denis Shapovalov. Alcaraz now boasts 30 wins in his...
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz has made it through to the semifinals of the Japan Open after knocking out Denis Shapovalov.

Alcaraz now boasts 30 wins in his 2026 ATP season, although his latest was via a walkover after Shapovalov was unable to continue. The Spaniard was, however, leading the Canadian 7-6(7-3), 2-1 at the time of the retirement. The Japan Open quarterfinal tie was brought to an end after 82 minutes.

Shapovalov appeared to suffer an injury at the beginning of the second set, right after Alcaraz had saved set point in the first. The former stretched for a forehand and pulled his hip, leading to an off-court medical timeout. He has now received a message from his opponent following the retirement.

In a classy touch from Alcaraz, the Spaniard posted on his Instagram: "Wishing you a quick recovery, Denis Shapovalov. Thanks everyone for the support, see you tomorrow in the semis!" Shapovalov has since responded, commenting with the person with folded hands emoji, which commonly represents prayer, gratitude, and respect.

The class from the ATP superstar certainly doesn't end there, with Alcaraz having embraced his rival at the net at the time. He then posted a message of support immediately after, writing on the camera: "Be back soon Denis." Alcaraz has been labelled the best loser on tour, and he has certainly shown that in abundance in Tokyo.

While Shapovalov will be eager to get back to full fitness as soon as possible, there is very little time for Alcaraz to ponder his latest win. He must quickly move on to the Japan Open semifinals, where he meets Jaume Munar. And history is very much on his side when it comes to the head-to-head record between the two Spaniards.

Intriguingly, Munar won their very first meeting in Marbella back in 2021, but Alcaraz has since recovered to win all three of their matches since then. But he will be taking nothing for granted against his compatriot, who started the ATP 500 tournament in qualifying, but has gone on to knock out Taylor Fritz.

Meanwhile, defending champion Alcaraz has beaten Alex Michelsen, Matteo Arnaldi and now Shapovalov. The world number three is chasing his third title of the 2026 season, which would bring him level with Daniil Medvedev and behind only Jannik Sinner (six) and Ben Shelton (four). The winner of the all-Spanish battle in Tokyo will take on the winner of Jiri Lehecka versus Valentin Vacherot in the final.

title: Cowboys vs. Texans live updates, inactives, where to watch: Nico Collins returns from injury, Joey Porter Jr. makes debut for Dallas
description: The Texans enter Week 4 still seeking their first win of the season. Can they make it happen in Sunday's Battle of Texas?
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys will make the short trip south to face the Houston Texans on Saturday afternoon in the "Battle of Texas." The Texans have been off to a brutal 0-3 start but received good news this week, as star wide receiver Nico Collins prepares to return from a hamstring injury that has held him out of the past two weeks.

The Cowboys (1-2) have been off to a similarly challenging start, punctuated in Week 3 by a heartbreaking walk-off field goal from the Baltimore Ravens, as Tyler Loop was good for 56 yards. They will get one new weapon on defense this week, though, as cornerback Joey Porter Jr. makes his debut with the team after being traded by the Pittsburgh Steelers last week.

Cowboys-Texans start time: 1 p.m. ET
Location: Reliant Stadium | Houston
TV channel/live stream: ABC/ESPN

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Houston Texans host the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4 in this year's Battle of Texas.

As expcted, both Texans wide reciever Nico Collins and new Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. are officially active for Week 4. Collins was returning from a hamstring injury, meanwhile Porter will make his debut with the team following a trade from the Steelers last week.

This marks Porter's first action since the wild-card round last season, missing the first three weeks of the season with back and conditioning issues.

Here's a full look at the gameday inactives for Cowboys-Texans.

The Houston Texans got some great news as they look to begin the climb out of the 0-3 hole they dug to start the season with a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, as star wide receiver Nico Collins returns from a hamstring injury that's had him out for the past two games.

After totaling 75 receiving yards and a touchdown in Week 1, Collins suffered a hamstring injury in practice the following week and has since been out. Collins practiced in a limited fashion on Wednesday and Thursday before being listed as a full participant Friday leading up to Week 4, officially not carrying any injury designation prior to Sunday's matchup with the Cowboys.

The Texans looked to tight end Dalton Schultz to step up in Collins' absence, and he caught 15 of 17 targets over the past two games for a team-high 170 receiving yards.

Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is healed. After missing the start of the season due to a back injury, Porter is expected to play in Week 4 after being traded to the Cowboys, according to ESPN.

Porter, however, is expected to have his snaps limited during the contest.

It will mark the first game all season in which Porter has played. The 26-year-old missed the first three weeks of the regular season due to both back and conditioning issues. Despite being able to put in work during practices, Porter was constantly ruled out on game days by the Pittsburgh Steelers after missing time in the offseason due to a contract dispute.

That dispute ultimately resulted in the Steelers trading Porter to the Cowboys on Wednesday. The Cowboys sent a sixth-round pick and a second-round pick to the Steelers as part of the deal.

title: 2026 Mountain West Football Week 5 Recap
description: An absolute thrashing, a statement victory and a season going down in flames highlighted the MW slate in Week 5.
fullText:
Week 5 of the 2026 season is in the books, and the slate jam-packed with rivalry games sadly did not deliver many thrillers. Most games looked closer than they actually were, and the lone game that was truly tight throughout was a low-scoring affair. Despite this, we still have some important results to go over this week, so let's get right into the MW madness that took place in Week 5.

The Scoop: Air Force got their long-awaited win over Navy on Saturday, doing so in dominant fashion, despite what the score might indicate. The Falcons are now 3-1, placing themselves firmly in contention for Mountain West championship contention, well on their way to returning to a bowl game in 2026.

On a day dominated by defense, the Falcons held their opponent to 253 yards of offense, with 68 of those coming on the typical fluke explosive pass to be expected once or twice from these triple-option slugfests. That pass came midway through the third quarter, after which the Midshipmen were held to a fumble, three punts, and 41 yards of offense. Liam Szarka did throw two interceptions during this game, being thoroughly outplayed by his counterpart Jackson Gutierrez in that regard, but his team-leading 81 yards on the ground and accounting for both of AFA's touchdowns more than made up for it.

Air Force (3-1, 1-1 MW) will be on the road next week, heading to DeKalb, IL for a matchup with the Northern Illinois Huskies (0-4) on Oct. 10 at 5:30 p.m. MDT. This game will be the Huskies' MW conference debut, but fortunately for the Falcons, NIU appears to be an even worse team than their 0-4 record would indicate. This is the kind of filler game that this squad will need to put themselves in a bowl game this year, so it is not one that can be taken lightly, despite how awful NIU has been this season.

The Scoop: UNLV continued to show what their brilliant scheduling strategy can truly do on Saturday, earning their fourth victory over a power-conference team in four years. They did so by winning a shootout with the Cal Golden Bears, who were without starting QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for over half the game. UNLV raced out to a 24-7 lead, but blew the entire advantage to be losing 25-24 near the start of the fourth quarter. Thankfully for Rebels fans, 15 straight points in the fourth allowed UNLV to cruise to a 39-31 victory, their first in front of their home crowd in 2026.

Jackson Arnold completed just 11 of 22 passes, but accounted for five total touchdowns—three in the air and two on the ground. Former Colorado State QB Jackson Brousseau was inserted into the game after Sagapolutele went out, throwing for 200 yards and two TDs against the Rebels' porous secondary. UNLV's defense gave up a whopping 464 yards of offense, but they stole the show in the clutch, forcing an interception, a missed field goal and three turnovers on downs. Cal also committed 16 penalties for a ridiculous 147 yards. The Rebels were not the more talented team in this match, but what they were is the better, more well-coached unit, and that is what won them the day in the end. I don't think UNLV's problems are fixed in any meaningful way, but this looks far more like the MW title contender we all expected to see at the beginning of the year.

UNLV (3-2, 1-0 MW) will stay at home next week, this time hosting an even bigger game than either Memphis or Cal. They will be hosting the North Dakota State Bison (5-0, 2-0 MW) on Oct. 10 at 4:00 p.m. PDT. The Bison have looked like a team incapable of losing in the early part of the season, having won four of their five games by at least 21 points. The Rebels will have a tall task in front of them, but can earn eternal in-conference bragging rights by handing the Bison their very first loss as an FBS team.

The Scoop: The first annual "Battle of the Basins" wasn't really much of a battle at all. North Dakota State shut out Wyoming in a game that was far more lopsided than the final score might indicate, earning their fifth straight victory to stay undefeated as an FBS team. As for the Cowboys, they drop to 2-3 on the year, but still have four relatively winnable games remaining on their schedule, meaning bowl contention is still a possibility for Jay Sawvel's squad.

Wyoming's first play of the game was an interception thrown right to the Bison defense, which set the tone for the rest of the contest. While the Cowboys never turned the ball over again, every single drive after resulted in either a punt (seven), a turnover on downs (two), or having possession when the half ended. Meanwhile, NDSU had arguably their worst offensive game of the season so far, putting up only 407 yards, punting a whopping four times, and doing the unthinkable: settling for a field goal not once, but twice. Obviously, this criticism is fully sarcastic. North Dakota State, despite some offensive inconsistency, looks to be completely indominable in the Mountain West this year. There looks to be little stopping them from creating a battle of the best in Albuquerque in two weeks, a game that will likely end up serving as a preview of the 2026 Mountain West Championship Game.

Wyoming (2-3, 1-1 MW) will be back next week on Oct. 9, traveling to San Jose, CA to take on the SJSU Spartans (3-2, 1-0 MW) at 7:00 p.m. MDT. San Jose State started conference play strong last night, defeating Hawaii in an ugly game. They should be able to handle the Cowboys, who have only shown life this season against that same 'Bows squad. Perhaps Coach Sawvel can pull another rabbit out of his hat, but I fear this team's performance against Hawaii may have been a last-ditch effort to save jobs, rather than a repeatable recipe for consistent success.

North Dakota State (5-0, 2-0 MW) finds themselves just a game away from a bowl berth, but they will have arguably their toughest game of the season next week, traveling to face the UNLV Rebels (3-2, 1-0 MW) on Oct. 10 at 6:00 p.m. CDT. UNLV was a projected conference contender that struggled to begin the year, but just picked up a massive home win against Cal, which could give them a much-needed confidence boost for this crucial game. If NDSU does not prepare properly, UNLV could end up springing a trap and snapping the Bison's perfect FBS start.

The Scoop: For the second week in a row, I predicted New Mexico would blow out their rivals here, and I was spot on again, though I could not have possibly foreseen just how badly the Lobos would destroy every single remnant of what was once their southern rivals. New Mexico out-gained the Miners by over 200 yards, forced five turnovers, allowed just 101 passing yards among three quarterbacks, and recorded 24 first downs to UTEP's 11. UNM's defense out-scored UTEP 16-7, which is as sure of a sign as anything that this game went horribly awry for the Miners. There is nothing good here to say for UTEP, whereas I cannot express well enough how scary the Lobos are appearing to be right now. This is what a CFP contender looks like, I only can hope they get the chance to truly compete for a spot.

UTEP (1-4, 0-1 MW) will host their first MW conference game next week, facing off against the Nevada Wolf Pack (1-3, 0-1 MW) on Oct. 10 at 5:00 p.m. MDT. Despite how poorly the Miners just played this week, this is absolutely an opportunity for them to score their first conference victory in the Mountain West. Nevada has consistently found unbelievable ways to consistently lose by one score, regardless of the caliber of opponent or the importance of the game. If UTEP simply shows up ready to play, they will find themselves victorious at home against an FBS opponent for the first time in nearly two years.

New Mexico (4-1, 1-0 MW) has their final bye week this week, returning on Oct. 17 when they travel to face Hawaii (1-4, 0-3 MW) at time TBD. Hawaii is reeling after falling to 0-3 in conference, with their potentially magical season now sitting in tatters. This game should be little more than a speed bump along the Lobos' way to a seemingly inevitable Mountain West championship berth.

The Scoop: If this game proved anything at all, it is that Hawaii is more cooked than overdone Huli Huli. The Rainbow Warriors outgained their opponents by over 100 yards, holding MW leading rusher Jabari Bates to just 74 scoreless yards, yet still managed to somehow find a way to lose their third conference game of the season already. Meanwhile, SJSU ended up scoring a critical road win to begin conference play, which will surely help them reach bowl eligibility this season.

After spotting the Spartans a 14-0 lead, Hawaii did come back into the game to cut SJSU's lead to as little as 17-16. Trailing by four on their final drive, the 'Bows had 18 seconds left and no timeouts from the Spartans' 40-yard line when Cam Barfield made the erroneous decision to catch a pass in bounds behind the first-down marker. This decision took the clock from 0:13 to 0:03, which forced the Warriors to attempt a Hail Mary right away from the 37, which obviously failed, securing yet another gut-punching loss.

With the run game packing a punch to be mistaken for a water pistol, Micah Alejado had to play 60 straight minutes of hero ball on the night. Most resulted in good things, such as the QB accounting for 377 yards of combined offense, but threw two costly interceptions deep in his own territory that the Spartans capitalized on to the tune of 10 points in a game they won by four. Luke Weaver's 246 yards pale in comparison to that of the man who beat him out for the job last year, but his two touchdowns sit next to a big ole zero in the turnover column. Weaver did not make mistakes in this game, and it is the reason why the Spartans walked away with the victory.

San Jose State (3-2, 1-0 MW) will travel back stateside this week, hosting Wyoming (2-3, 1-1 MW) on Oct. 9 at 6:00 p.m. PDT. The Cowboys are coming off of a game where they were offensively stymied by North Dakota State, and have generally not looked to be a very good team for most of the season. This is a winnable game in every respect, one that the Spartans desperately need to make a bowl game with a brutal schedule coming up.

Hawaii (1-4, 0-3 MW) will take a break from Mountain West play this week, heading to Tempe, AZ for a matchup against the Big 12's Arizona State Sun Devils (2-2) on Oct. 10 at 4:30 p.m. HST. Once thought to be Big 12 title contenders, the Sun Devils were destroyed at home by a not-great Baylor squad this week, perhaps showing some vulnerability against a team like Hawaii. However, considering how Hawaii played on the road against Stanford, who were just railroaded by Wake Forest, I highly doubt that this game will go any better than the 'Bows' last trip to Arizona (40-6 defeat to the Wildcats in 2025). This season has been nothing short of a disaster in paradise, a fact that I do not foresee changing any time soon.

title: Dave Roberts Reveals How Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell’s Friendship Helps the Dodgers
description: Dave Roberts shares how Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell's blossoming friendship and sharing of trade secrets is paying major dividends for the Dodgers.
fullText:
With Tarik Skubal dominant performance Saturday and Blake Snell getting the start on Sunday for Game 2 of the National League Division Series, the Los Angeles Dodgers have an abundance of riches in their rotation.

More than just a pair of talented pitchers, though, the two have become fast friends since Skubal joined the Dodgers just ahead of the trade deadline.

That relationship is paying dividends on and off the field.

Dodgers Nation's Noel Sanchez asked Dave Roberts what it's been like to see the two star pitchers grow close.

Roberts said that while "it's great" to see them becoming friends, it's also benefiting the team.

"I think that they've kind of forged their own relationship," Roberts said. "There's a sharing of trade secrets. They're two of the best pitchers, not only left handed pitchers, but pitchers in the game. So, how they talk about attacking hitters, what makes them good, I think that only sharpens the knife. It's fun to watch their back and forth and how their relationship has really blossomed."

It's a scary thought for opponents that two two-time Cy Young winners could be making each other even better, but that's exactly what's happening.

Fans, though, seem to be enjoying their off-the-field relationship just as much as the winning on the field.

Dodgers fans have been eating up the blossoming bromance.

Skubal and Snell have adopted a relationship reminiscent of the Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly movie "Step Brothers," in which two adult male step brothers, who are initially cold and competitive with each other, grow into family.

Snell and Skubal, oftentimes with fellow ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, post captions on social media from the film, including quips like "did we just become best friends?"

The highlight of the friendship, though, might be their joining in on a recent online trend involving Quavo and Takeoff's performance of their song "Hotel Lobby" on A COLORS SHOW.

Quavo and the late Takeoff, both former members of the Migos, were family, as Quavo was Takeoff's uncle.

The pair also were, of course, good friends and professional collaborators.

An an AI-generated video posted to social media, Snell is depicted as Takeoff, while Skubal, with an intricate hairdo, appears as Quavo as the two perform the hit song.

After Saturday's performance, Skubal can take a couple of days to work on his dance moves before he gets set to pitch again — ideally, in the NL Championship Series.

Snell, meanwhile, needs to get ready to start Sunday's Game 2.

If he can match his friend's performance, the Dodgers will be in the driver's seat as this series heads to Atlanta.

title: Esteban Ribovics blames UFC 332 weight miss on hotel issue
description: Esteban Ribovics has an excuse for UFC 332 weight miss
fullText:
Esteban Ribovics had a costly weight miss ahead of UFC 332, which cost him a portion of his purse and at least $25,000 in bonus money as he went on to finish King Green.

However, Ribovics insists that there was some weirdness with his cut. A day ahead of official weigh-ins, Ribovics and his team were working to prepare him for a Friday morning weight cut, but whatever they did, it wasn't enough as Ribovics went on to register 0.5 pounds over the limit (his bout with Green was changed to a catchweight with Ribovics forfeiting 20 percent of his purse as penalty and becoming ineligible to win any post-fight bonuses).

Ribovics defeated Green by first-round knockout and later explained to reporters that there was an issue with the workout room that made it difficult for him to sweat off the pounds.

"On Thursday, there's something that we do, we do everything we could to get to a certain number, just to cut some stuff on Friday, but they turned on the air conditioning while we were just doing it and basically I stopped sweating," Ribovics said via a Spanish translator. "At one point, 'We have to leave this for tomorrow,' I stopped sweating because of it, so we got cold and just stopped sweating."

Ribovics laughed when he was asked whether the sudden burst of AC was sabotage arranged by Green and boxer Arnold Barboza Jr. The two have become partners in online streaming, and broadcasted a confrontation with Ribovics and his team ahead of the fight.

King Green and Arnold Barboza Jr got into a heated altercation with Esteban Ribovics after the UFC 332 weigh-in 😳

“Back the f*ck up! Don’t f*cking touch me. We can get down right now!” pic.twitter.com/m8xN7HJgbC

Some of that remaining tension boiled over into the finish of the bout as Ribovics and Green jawed at each other as the fight was waved off, though the two quickly made amends moments later.

"I said to him, 'Keep talking, keep talking,' but it's for the day before. … It's from the other thing, it's not Bobby, it's the boxer guy," Ribovics said in English. "I honestly saw nothing of him. I stopped following him on my social media, I don't saw nothing. If I saw a little bit, it's because my friend showed me the training because he filmed the training, but honestly, I don't saw nothing, I don't care what he do in his life."

Ribovics has now won consecutive fights for the first time since 2024, and could be poised for a bump up the rankings after knocking out legends Green and Edson Barboza. However, he's not making any bold proclamations or callouts just yet.

"I don't like to call out names," Ribovics said in Spanish. "I'll tell you that after that fight against [Mateusz] Gamrot, things clicked in my head, and I just became more professional, improved a lot of things to be ready for whenever and I can tell you I am ready. If called upon, I will face anyone."

title: Top defensive players in FSU's win over Virginia
description: The FSU Seminoles allowed a touchdown early, but them the pitched a shout out the rest of the way against Virginia. Here are their top defensive players.
fullText:
The Florida State defense appeared to be in for a long day when the Virginia Cavaliers went right down the field on their second drive to take a 7-0 lead. They would have to cherish that touchdown because not a single point was scored by them after that, as FSU put up the final 38 to roll to a victory.

For the game, Virginia only had 37 yards rushing and went three for 15 on their down, plus they missed all four of their fourth-down attempts. On top of that, their offensive line got absolutely dominated as Florida State's defense racked up 10 sacks.

Without question, this was the top defensive performance of 2026 for the Seminoles. Here were the top three defensive players for them on Saturday.

What else can you say about Jones? Week in and week out, he continues to prove that he's the leader of FSU's defense. Against Virginia, Jones was tied for the team lead with six tackles, with four of them being solo, which included a big fourth-down stop on the Cavaliers' first drive in the second half. Also, Jones had 1.5 sacks in the game. He's been a top-tier addition from the transfer portal.

Kennedy, another portal add, produced his best game for the Seminoles so far. Three of his four tackles were of the solo variety, and two were for loss. He also has two sacks against Virginia, giving him at least one in each of the last two games, and his four sacks on the year lead the team. He's definitely coming into his own in Tallahassee.

This can be seen as the transfer game defensively because Gbayor did his thing against Virginia as well. His six tackles tied Jones for tops on the team, with five being solo stops. He was also a part of the sack party as he amassed one himself. Along with Jones, Gbayor has helped the linebacker spot be the top group on Tony White's defense this season.

title: 7-foot-1 center Kimario Sherman commits to USF
description: Three-star big man Kimario Sherman committed to USF this weekend on his visit. Sherman is 7-foot-1 and ranked No. 130 overall in the 2027 Rivals150 rankings.
fullText:
Three-star big man Kimario Sherman has committed to USF, Rivals is told.

The 7-foot-1 center out of Westminster (FL) Academy visited the Bulls this weekend and committed to head coach Chris Mack before leaving campus. Sherman also claimed offers from East Carolina, Iona, Ohio, and others throughout his process.

Sherman is the second commitment of the 2027 cycle for USF, joining three-star point guard King Kendrick, who plays at Combine (NC) Academy.

The three-star big man played this summer with the OTP organization on Puma's Pro16 Circuit. He averaged 11.2 points, 4.7 rebounds, and almost a block per game in just over 23 minutes during Circuit play.

Kimario Sherman is ranked No. 130 overall in the 2027 Rivals150 rankings, making him the No. 20 center in his recruiting cycle.

title: London City Lionesses hit six past sorry Tottenham
description: Alexia Putellas and Kadidiatou Diani both score twice as London City Lionesses win in a rout against Tottenham, ending Spurs' unbeaten start in the Women's Super League.
fullText:
Tottenham Hotspur 1 - 6 London City Lionesses FT

Alexia Putellas and Kadidiatou Diani both scored twice as London City Lionesses hit six goals past Tottenham to end Spurs' unbeaten start to the Women's Super League campaign.

Putellas, a two-time Women's Ballon d'Or winner and a four-time Women's Champions League winner with Barcelona, grabbed her first WSL double following her summer move from Spain.

She had registered her first WSL goal in last week's 2-0 win over Brighton and only needed three minutes to open the scoring on Sunday at the BetWright Stadium.

The early strike came after Grace Geyoro's strike had been parried by home goalkeeper Lize Kop, with Putellas firing in the rebound with her left foot.

French forward Diani grabbed her first WSL goal in the 22nd minute when she got on the end of a fine move involving Freya Godfrey and Lucia Corrales.

Putellas scored her second and London City's third in the 34th minute with a shot into the roof of the net after Danielle van de Donk did superbly to get to the byeline to the left of goal and pull the ball back.

Tottenham nearly pulled a goal back just before the break through Julie Blakstad's well-struck free-kick, a left-footed attempt from 25 yards, but goalkeeper Elene Lete made an excellent save by pushing the ball on to the crossbar.

Van de Donk deservedly got a goal in the 52nd minute to make it 4-0, converting Diani's low cross from the right at the near post.

Tottenham immediately got one back as Victoria Pelova, a summer signing from Arsenal, scored for the fifth time in the WSL this season, controlling from Blakstad's cross and finishing well.

But London City restored their four-goal advantage when Kop's clearance was charged down by Diani, who had the easy task of walking the ball into an unguarded net.

London City grabbed a sixth in injury time when substitute Delphine Cascarino netted a fine individual goal, running at the home defence and performing a stepover to make space for the shot before firing past Kop.

Tottenham began the season with three wins and a draw from their opening four league matches.

A win on Sunday would have taken them top of the WSL, although that may have only been for a couple of hours with Manchester City, who won their opening four games, playing Arsenal later on.

But London City, given the huge investment they have made in their squad, look the more likely of these two to mount a title challenge.

They finished sixth in 2025-26 but made major signings in the summer, including Putellas and defender Mapi Leon from Barcelona, along with Diani from Lyon.

This was a fourth win in five WSL games, and its manner sends out a message.

Head coach Eder Maestre felt the result and performance would demonstrate to the rest of the league that his Lionesses can make a push for the title.

"The three points are the same as you can have in every game, but this kind of win can be a game changer in terms of showing everyone that we are pushing hard," said Maestre.

"But, at the same time, we need to be humble as well. The teams that are used to being there and occupying these places [at the top] are still there.

"I'm so happy we're hitting our targets. When you have these kind of players it is about trying to find chemistry and it takes time. It's a process and we're in the process of building something strong."

London City will not be in action for another two weeks because of the international break, and will hope that does not affect their momentum.

For Tottenham, the heavy defeat was a reality check.

Head coach Martin Ho said his team "looked scared with the ball" and added: "Really poor, not acceptable from us as a group. Defensively we didn't win a first ball, a second ball. Duels, we were poor. We have to move on.

"The team collectively needs to own that and we will, and that starts with me, I take responsibility for it.

"We were just not at it, but that can't be the level. Everyone will be disappointed - that was not the level we expect. We conceded six goals and you don't want to be doing that."

title: Florida appears set to tumble while Bama hopes to rise
description: A week after a huge promotion in the poll, Florida is bound to come down in the newest AP Top 25 after a lopsided loss. 25 Missouri on a Saturday while other ranked teams generally won in workmanlike fashion.
fullText:
A week after a huge promotion in the poll, Florida is bound to come down in the newest AP Top 25 after a lopsided loss.

The No. 8 Gators fell 45-17 to No. 25 Missouri on a Saturday while other ranked teams generally won in workmanlike fashion.

Elsewhere in the rankings, No. 8 Alabama put a 56-23 beating on No. 16 Mississippi State. Both teams entered the week undefeated.

No. 2 Georgia, No. 3 Notre Dame, No. 4 Miami also remained unbeaten — and mostly untested — as top-10 teams. No. 1 Texas was idle Saturday.

Stick around for projections and live updates when the latest rankings drop at 2 p.m. EDT.

Six AP Top 25 teams had the week off.

title: Six candidates for the Rams punt return job
description: Looking to rejuvenate the L.A. return game
fullText:
With regards to the Los Angeles Rams special teams, fans are chafing and coaches are desperately trying to correct the steering of a unit that careening towards disaster. The most recent move came late this week when L.A. parted ways with Xavier Smith, the Rams primary punt returner of three seasons. The release should be considered a mostly symbolic move At this point, the Rams simply don't have a lot of options to upgrade his absence. Any move made this close to game day should not be construed as permanent.

The L.A. braintrust does indeed have some in-house options, but should not be afraid to pull the trigger on a player from the outside that can improve the lineup.

Trying to look at the situation with a view longer than just the Philadelphia Eagles game, who can the Rams decide upon to rejuvenate their return game?

The current L.A. roster holds a couple of in-house options and a scan of available free agents provides six names that stand out as possible season-long replacements. Actually seven with the addition of Kyren Williams and although his profile is not in this exercise, the odds would favor him being the eventual choice.

Alex Bachman – ( age 30) 5' 11" 195 lb.

Originally signed by the Rama as an undrafted free agent back in 2019. He made stops with the New York Giants (2019-22), Houston Texans (1922-24), and Las Vegas Raiders (2025) before re-joining the Rams this August past. Over that six-year span, he's played in 22 games with one start, totaling 151 reps on offense and 213 on special teams.

With 22 punt returns, last season with the Raiders was his first as a team's primary returner. He accrued a modest 124 yards for a 5.6 average. His long was 25 yards and he had one fumble on the season. He has also put in work on coverage teams, making nine tackles over the pst two seasons. Bachman is physically bigger than most returners and it would be interesting to have access to his current speed numbers. Coming out in 2019, he ran a 4.47 forty with a 1. 58 10-yard split, quite similar to the man he endeavors to replace, Xavier Smith, just a shade less burst.

Brennan Presley – ( age 24) 5' 8" 175 lb.

The Rams plucked him from the undrafted ranks in 2025. He fits the Rams mold of over-achievers that win with effort, toughness, and football IQ. With his 4.53 forty and 1.64 split, Presley is not super fast. He is however an outstanding open-field runner and was a highly productive returner in college. On offense, he shows excellent hands and is a disciplined route runner. He has a stash of receiving/return records at Oklahoma State.

80 days until Oklahoma State Cowboy football

#80 Brennan Presley with the 100 yard TD return in 2021 Bedlam. So excited he’s back for one more year. #GoPokes pic.twitter.com/ffMfVo0vhx

Tutu Atwell – ( age 27) 5' 9" 165 lb.

Yes, I'm going to throw his hat into the ring. Whether the Rams do anything to fit his skillset into the offense or not, Atwell does have the tools for the punt returner/WR 4 role. Unless he shows to be a fumbler in practice, he has shown an ability to track deep passes and at 4.39 in the forty and a1.49 split, he most certainly has the burst and long speed. He is a linear runner, not a darter, more of a swerver. As a rookie (2021), he did some return work (10 punts, 5 kickoffs) without distinction before a shoulder injury cut his season short.

Ray Ray McCloud – (age 29) 5' 10 190 lb.

McCloud has made his bones as a vagabond return man. He began his NFL career as a Round 6 pick of the Buffalo Bills in 2018 and has made stops with the Carolina Panthers, Pittsburgh Steelers, San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta Falcons, New York Giants, and Chicago Bears. All told, played 766 special teams reps over 100 games. Not limited just return for, McCloud has 24 starts and 2512 reps at wide receiver.

While his numbers have been decline the past couple of seasons and his speed testing of 4.49 forty and 1.56 split may not be accurate anymore, McCloud has 140 punts for a 9.5 average and 126 kickoffs at a 23 yard rate. He's also added 159 receptions and a catch rate of 67.4 percent.

Tahj Washington – (age 25) 5' 10" 174 lb.

A Round 7 selection by the Miami Dolphins in 2024. He was injured early in camp and spent the season on the Injured Reserve List. In 2025, he saw action in six games with one start 45 snaps on offense and interestingly, only four on special teams. Miami cut him this August

And the Philadelphia Eagles signed, only to release him in final cuts.

Washington is different from the other candidates in that he is not an experienced returner, only taking a handful in college and the NFL preseason. While not having elite speed or burst, 4.52 forty and 1.63 split, he was, however, an outstanding receiver in college with a gift for playmaking in the open field. He was also known as a tough competitor on coverage units and by his own reporting, chose to participate on special teams, even after became an offensive starter.

Mecole Hardman – (age 28) 5' 10" 187 lb.

A former Round 2 pick in 2019 of the Kansas City Chiefs. Although he never became a full-time starter on offense, Hardman was a play making threat both as a receiver and kick returner. He

combined 4.33 speed in the forty and a 1.48 10-yard split with good open-field moves.

Over seven seasons, Hardman has played in 97 games with 28 starts, stacking up 2168 reps on offense and another 455 on special teams. Amongst the latter, he has returned 91 punts for 823 yards and 46 kickoff's for 24.7 per..

Mecole Hardman with a HUGE punt return!

📺: #KCvsSF on FOX
📱: https://t.co/waVpO909ge pic.twitter.com/3kj1puP7EU

The Rams braintrust has decided on— Alex Bachman. Put into service off the practice squad.

Stu Jackson of therams.com reports,

"McVay said wide receiver Alex Bachman, who is currently on the team's practice squad, will step into the punt returner role. Asked if he anticipates long-term trying to work some guys out to see if they might be fits at punt returner, McVay said "I think I'm interested to see how Alex does…"We're always looking at if there's way of improving the caliber of our team," McVay said. "Those will be avenues that we'll always explore within whatever parameters that we can do that within, and so I would certainly never say no. But I am also optimistic that I think we're gonna see some good stuff from Alex on Sunday."

While most Rams fans were not unhappy to see the move made to jettison Xavier Smith, I have to wonder how many would consider this move an upgrade. Although Bachman fielded a fair amount of kicks for the Las Vegas Raiders last year, he does not have a history as a returner., nor is he known as an open-field runner. His production was only mediocre It appears a lateral move, at best.

Although Bachman fielded a fair amount of kicks for the Las Vegas Raiders last year, he does not have a history as a returner., nor is he known as an open-field runner. His production was only mediocre It appears a lateral move, at best.

title: Valkyries' Janelle Salaün wins 2026 WNBA Sixth Player of the Year Award
description: Janelle Salaün has been a key contributor for the Valkyries all season.
fullText:
Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün has been named the 2026 WNBA Sixth Player of the Year, the WNBA announced on Sunday. Salaün's Valkyries squad begins their semifinals series against the Las Vegas Aces on Sunday after ousting the Dallas Wings in the first round.

A moment worth celebrating 🥹

Janelle Salaün gets the special news that she’s the 2026 WNBA @Kia Sixth Player of the Year!#KiaSixth | #WNBASeason30 pic.twitter.com/d6J8vEweT0

This award is given annually to the player who has had the biggest impact on their team while coming off the bench. To be eligible, the player must come off the bench in more games than they start.

The Valkyries forward played in 40 games this season, coming off the bench in all of them. She averaged 12.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 22.1 minutes per game, while shooting 42.5% from the field, including 39.2% from beyond the arc.

Salaün has been in the league for just two years. This is the first award of her professional career. She was named to the WNBA All-Rookie Team last year.

The Valkyries forward won the award over fellow candidates Sophie Cunningham, Cameron Brink and Jewell Lloyd.

Salaün helped lead Golden State to a 32-12 record during the regular season, the second-best mark in the league. The Valkyries trailed only the Minnesota Lynx, who finished 33-11 to earn the No. 1 seed for the WNBA playoffs.

Golden State was an expansion team ahead of the 2025 season. The Valkyries made the playoffs that year with a 23-21 record, but lost in the first round. Salaün committed to her role off the bench, took a step forward, and helped Golden State add nine more wins to its record in the Valkyries' second season.

Salaün signed a two-year extension with Golden State following the 2025 season. She is under contract through next year and is set to hit free agency in 2028.

title: Women’s Soccer: Northwestern falls to No. 7 Ohio State 3-0
description: The loss to the top-ranked Buckeyes was Northwestern’s worst of the season.
fullText:
Dealing with an extremely high press and a two-goal star power showing from Amanda Schlueter, Northwestern Women's Soccer (5-5-3, 3-2-1 B1G) fell 3-0 to No. 7 Ohio State (9-1-1, 5-1-0 B1G) Saturday.

The Wildcats were outshot by the Buckeyes 14-6, aiming just three shots on target compared to Ohio State's seven. Ohio State also led the game in corners, 11-2.

Individually, Megan Norkett led the 'Cats in offensive production with three shots. Schlueter had an all-around day for the Buckeyes, providing two goals and one assist for the home side.

Northwestern's Ava Goodin did not appear in the game after sustaining an injury against Indiana last Sunday.

Northwestern's game started off on the wrong foot. Just five minutes into the match, Schlueter and Ava Bramblett combined for a 1-2 setup on the left side of the field. Schlueter's ball passed through the 'Cats' three-back setup, and Bramblett's momentum took her through to the box to slot it past Nyamma Nelson and make it 1-0.

GOALLLL!!!!!! 

Ava Bramblett with her first of the season to kick things off against Northwestern!

OSU 1
NU 0#GoBucks pic.twitter.com/5RAqiT3GQK

The early goal did not stop the 'Cats' attempts to possess the ball, but Ohio State's pressure continued to loom over Northwestern's head.

In the 10th minute, Ohio State's Elle Britt played the ball down the right sideline to Ava Greco, who pulled a dummy move to get Holland Carey on her back and charged to the front post. Greco slotted the ball through the six-yard box to Anika Poremba, who met a strong challenge by Gwen Zimmerman. Eventually, the ball landed with Berkley Mape, who put up a shot for the Buckeyes, but Nelson made a calm save for the 'Cats.

The play was checked for a foul on Zimmerman in the box, but officials eventually ruled no error.

Northwestern's first real chance in the opening 45 minutes came with 28:52 to go, when Sarah O'Donnell pickpocketed Ava Bramblett off a poor touch. Though O'Donnell fell after making the initial challenge, she poked the ball through to Elle Phillips, who tried to get off a shot for the 'Cats but had two Buckeyes ready to clean up the mess.

Though the 'Cats maintained a relatively steady amount of time on the ball in the first half, their build-from-the-back philosophy cost them in the 26th minute. Pressure from Callie Tumilty outside the box forced a misplaced pass from Nyamma Nelson into the feet of Schlueter, who grabbed the extra space and slotted it past Nelson to make it 2-0 to OSU.

AMANDA SCHLUETER MAKES IT 2 FOR THE BUCKEYES! 

OSU 2
NU 0#GoBucks pic.twitter.com/Csd47auVxP

A combination play from Schlueter in the 36' curled in front of Naomi Lofthouse made it to Tumulti in front of the box, forcing Nelson and Lofthouse to come out and tackle down Tumulti.

Though it at first looked like Northwestern was going to dig itself deeper into this season's penalty-kick hole, the offsides flag flew up against Ohio State, saving the Wildcats just before the halftime whistle blew.

At half, the Buckeyes led the 'Cats on shots 7-2. They also committed 0 fouls to Northwestern's two, flipping the script from Northwestern's usual pattern of limiting fouls. Nelson had to put in the work for the 'Cats in the first half, making three saves to Peighton Northrup's one.

The second half was a lot less stable for Northwestern in terms of possession. The 'Cats tried to put a high press on the Buckeyes but quickly crumbled after significant amounts of pressure from Ohio State affected its three-back system.

Megan Norkett was a bright spot in the Wildcats' limited offensive production. In the 57th minute, she hit a left-footed shot to the top center of the goal, forcing Northrup to tip the ball over the bar and marking Northwestern's best opportunity of the game.

On defense, Amber Weaver and Finnerty continued to shine for the 'Cats. Weaver had a great moment in the 66th minute when she tracked back from behind to slide-tackle OSU's Britt on the right flank. Three minutes later, Finnerty dealt well with an impressive threaded ball from Decker in the midfield to Tumilty in the box. Muscling Tumilty off the ball, Finnerty tried to keep the Wildcats' deficit to two.

Yet, long balls continued to kill the 'Cats. With 3:36 to go, Mape played a long ball through three lines of Northwestern players to Schlueter, whose speed left Zimmerman and Finnerty chasing the ball. Schlueter finished off the 3-0 game for the Buckeyes, getting herself a brace on the day and increasing her goal tally to 12 on the season.

GOALLLL!!!!

Amanda Schlueter secures her third brace in a row and brings the Buckeyes to three!

OSU 3
NU 0#GoBucks pic.twitter.com/QvUjj6loQl

Norkett tried to recover for the 'Cats in the dying minutes of the game on the left side of the attack. She received a ball from Lofthouse just outside the halfway mark with 2:41 to go, beat an OSU midfielder and ripped a shot with her favorite left foot well outside the 18-yard mark. Northrup batted the ball outside the post for a corner kick, but that was Northwestern's last true offensive chance of the game, leaving the score at 3-0.

The 'Cats continue their road trip next against Rutgers on Thursday at 6:00 p.m. CDT. The Scarlet Knights have pulled off several close results against top teams in the country, including 1-0 losses to then-No. 12 Washington and No. 12 UCLA, and a 3-1 win over No. 14 Wisconsin last Sunday.

The game will stream on Big Ten Plus.

title: Rural Queenslanders have seen gas projects come and go – but a 725-hectare datacentre poses a whole new level of ‘stupidity’
description:
Residents of Dalby may soon live beside a $31bn datacentre. The premier sees ‘opportunity’ for the state – but others fear AI’s global creep
From the veranda on his bush block, Denver Kanowski has watched resources companies come and go from rural Queensland for 70 years.
The home cost him $800, and lets him live how he likes, in nature. It’s also in the middle of a gasfield, not far from the Linc Energy contamination site, down the road from a coalmine and three gas power plants.
Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Residents of Dalby may soon live beside a $31bn datacentre. The premier sees ‘opportunity’ for the state – but others fear AI’s global creep

From the veranda on his bush block, Denver Kanowski has watched resources companies come and go from rural Queensland for 70 years.

The home cost him $800, and lets him live how he likes, in nature. It’s also in the middle of a gasfield, not far from the Linc Energy contamination site, down the road from a coalmine and three gas power plants.

Last month came the biggest scheme yet, a $31bn datacentre to power Claude, the large language model developed by global AI giant Anthropic. If built, Australia’s largest datacentre would be about 15 minutes’ drive away from Kanowski’s home, outside Kogan, near Dalby, about 180km west of Brisbane.

In a community that has seen the boom and bust of coal seam gas, the response from many has been the same as Kanowski’s: once bitten, twice shy.

“This is the power of money and the power of greed and shortsighted stupidity,” Kanowski says.

Anthropic’s project is to be built on a 725-hectare plot of land now occupied by a 24,000 head feedlot, surrounded by gas wells.

According to Singapore-based developer Zerra DC, its cooling system will be far less water intensive than most existing datacentres’, generating about the same demand as an average shopping centre.

But like all AI, it will require an enormous amount of energy. The Western Downs datacentre will require a peak power capacity equal to about a quarter of total state energy demand, 2.16GW. It would also employ thousands during construction, with about 1,400 long-term jobs, according to the company.

The proposal was made public just last month.

Within days, Dalby travel agent Mordechai Winters had made up his mind: he didn’t want it.

“I was crushed. You know, it’s very disappointing that the council and also the government would consider it,” he says.

Issues like energy demand, noise and poor siting have driven a massive backlash against datacentres in the United States. Three-quarters of Americans now oppose them, and more than 500 counties have imposed a ban.

At least thousands have a similar view in Australia.

A petition that Winters helped to launch has been signed by more than 21,500 people – mostly from the area – in just a few weeks, he says.

He believes the project’s benefits are exaggerated and will trigger the same boom-bust cycle as gas.

Cecil Plains farmer Liza Balmain remembers the big – and eventually unrealised – promises of the gas industry when it arrived.

The industry brought massive change; academics later concluded that its scale and pace in a small agricultural community “was likely unprecedented anywhere in the world”. There was a huge influx of workers, with the high wages of gas attracting labour away from farms and local business.

Then – because setting up a gas well requires a lot more labour than operating it – the industry left, just as quickly as it had arrived, leaving business owners with debts they couldn’t pay on investments they no longer needed. Some academics believe the industry left the region worse off. Others think it was a slim net positive.

Balmain, who led a long campaign against the gas industry, says she can see “huge similarities” between the coal seam gas era and the proposed datacentre.

Australians across the country are concerned. Jo Shulman, CEO of the Environmental Defenders Office which has long helped communities fight resources projects such as coal seam gas, says the group had seen a 250% increase in queries about datacentres to the service’s free legal advice line since January.

“I would say the datacentre is the new frontier,” she says.

“Communities are concerned about [their] impacts on the environment and their wellbeing”.

Shulman says datacentres will form an essential part of the clean energy transition – but called for a pause to allow national standards to catch up.

“We think that there should be a moratorium on any further datacentres, or they risk repeating the same things that we saw with the coal seam gas boom,” she says.

The Dalby mayor, Andrew Smith, says the ultimate authority over the region’s largest ever project should rest with the Western Downs regional council, population 35,452. Speaking to Guardian Australia last month, he said council did not expect the project to be taken over by the state coordinator general.

“We did ask the question, but our understanding is it will stay with local government,” he says.

But then, on Friday, things changed. The state announced it would take datacentres out of the hands of local councils, under a new planning framework to ensure “a consistent and transparent framework across the state,” similar to the government’s renewables planning policy.

“We will treat these projects no worse and no better than we do mining, renewables or tourism projects. Any deals done must be with the backing of councils and communities,” a spokesperson for planning minister, Jarrod Bleijie, says.

“The state government will become the responsible assessor and coordinator of any data centre applications, instead of local councils”.

If given the green light, the project will be worth more to the local community than coal seam gas, he says.

“In general, the coal seam gas industry has been wonderful for our region. It’s diversified our economy, which we talk about a lot. It’s created jobs,” he says.

“Prior to coal seam gas, we were exporting a lot of our clever kids, because the opportunities weren’t back in the region.”

Anthropic wants to start using the centre as early as next year. But Smith says the planning couldn’t be rushed – and was careful not to endorse or oppose the project.

The Queensland premier, David Crisafulli, lobbied the company to invest in the state during a recent trade mission, he told parliament last week.

Crisafulli said the state would help the council assess the project, but said it had done an excellent job with the gas industry and could do so again.

“They see the same opportunity I do, and that opportunity is to make sure that there are jobs, very good jobs in regional areas, and if we get it right, lower power bills for every other Queenslander as well. I see a really good play with that,” the premier said.

Toowoomba and Surat Basin Enterprise chief executive officer Jo Sheppard says most residents of the area had not yet made up their minds about the project, but that it was important for the developer to maintain their social license.

She added it was a “a once in a generation opportunity for Western Downs region and our broader region”, with the power to transform the town from a “ “fairly quiet” farming community to something more, adding to booms triggered by gas, and then renewables.

“Someone actually did say to me the other day: ‘Gosh, should we all be buying a house in Dalby?’”

Kanowski says there was something different about the datacentre compared with coal and coal seam gas schemes. He believes it will go beyond harming the environment by contributing to an online “fantasy” world, disconnecting people from the things that genuinely matter.

“[The datacentre developers] don’t even see the trees. They don’t understand the relationship between all the things. This is my world, I love it,” he says.

“This is not a datacentre … This is part of a network that these money-crazed idiots are planning to put all over the planet.”

title: Trump names intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new White House AI czar
description:
Calyton said AI was a ‘gamechanger’ but it also posed ‘a threat’ during his DNI Senate confirmation hearing 
Donald Trump on Sunday named Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, to serve also as the new White House AI czar.
Clayton, who leads the US’s 18 intelligence agencies, previously served as the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan and led the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump’s first term.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
Calyton said AI was a ‘gamechanger’ but it also posed ‘a threat’ during his DNI Senate confirmation hearing

Donald Trump on Sunday named Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, to serve also as the new White House AI czar.

Clayton, who leads the US’s 18 intelligence agencies, previously served as the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan and led the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump’s first term.

During his Senate confirmation hearing, Clayton said AI was a “gamechanger”, but it also posed “a threat”.

“When something’s both an opportunity and a threat, you better get your arms around it,” Clayton told lawmakers when asked about AI.

CBS News was the first to report that Clayton would be appointed White House AI czar.

In a social media post on Sunday, Trump announced that Clayton would lead what the US president called “the Super Intelligence Force (SIF)”.

Trump’s post also said the SIF would “coordinate the federal government’s engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers, and super intelligence companies”.

In September, Trump announced he was creating an “AI Force” and a czar to oversee the technology’s growth and monitor for “bad” development. The announcement came after tech industry leaders warned that AI was developing too rapidly to control and that it could harm humans.

The president has largely brushed aside concerns about AI development and the construction of datacenters, which power the technology.

Trump has insisted continued development is paramount to defeating China in the global AI race.

But to address concerns, the president created an advisory committee in addition to the czar – who he previously promised would be led by a “High IQ” individual. Trump also recently met with AI industry leaders to discuss concerns.

On Tuesday, Trump and six executives signed an AI accord at the White House, promising to create internal and external monitors to ensure the technology is used as intended and any safety issues are addressed.

Trump had initially created the AI and cryptocurrency czar position when he returned to the White House in January 2025.

David Sacks, the venture capitalist and tech businessman, served as the administration’s AI and cryptocurrency czar until March 2026, when he reached his employment limit under his designation as a “special government employee”.

Sacks still co-chairs the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

Trump previously floated Clayton’s name as a potential AI czar, telling Axios in September that Clayton is ‘“a good man” and the prospect of appointing him was “a good idea”.

title: Researchers think they might have actually found remains of Noah's Ark
description:
A team investigating a boat-shaped formation in eastern Turkey says new evidence is strengthening its case that the site could hold the remains of Noah's Ark.
"In archaeology, you deal with probabilities, and we're inching towards where we believe we will have confirmation this winter after our soil analysis is done with Sivas University, who's our partner in this," Noah's Ark Scans founder Andrew Jones told "Saturday in America."
The focus of the investigation is the Durupınar formation, an approximately 538-foot-long geological structure near Mount Ararat. Its shape and proximity to the region identified in the biblical account have fascinated Ark hunters for decades.
The boat-shaped formation was first discovered in 1959 and has long-drawn speculation over a possible connection to Noah's Ark.
fullText:
A team investigating a boat-shaped formation in eastern Turkey says new evidence is strengthening its case that the site could hold the remains of Noah's Ark.

"In archaeology, you deal with probabilities, and we're inching towards where we believe we will have confirmation this winter after our soil analysis is done with Sivas University, who's our partner in this," Noah's Ark Scans founder Andrew Jones told "Saturday in America."

The focus of the investigation is the Durupınar formation, an approximately 538-foot-long geological structure near Mount Ararat. Its shape and proximity to the region identified in the biblical account have fascinated Ark hunters for decades.

The boat-shaped formation was first discovered in 1959 and has long-drawn speculation over a possible connection to Noah's Ark.

SITE WHERE JESUS WAS CRUCIFIED AND BURIED REVEALS NEW EVIDENCE THAT BACKS BIBLICAL ACCOUNT

Critics have maintained that the formation is naturally occurring, but Jones said recent drilling, soil sampling and ground-penetrating radar have given his team new reasons to challenge that conclusion.

"They've criticized in the past, saying all those scans you can interpret different ways, 'This is a solid mass of rock, a syncline or a block of bedrock,'" Jones said. "Well, we've core drilled… over 12 locations. We did not find bedrock at all."

AUTHOR DINESH D'SOUZA CHALLENGES BIBLE SKEPTICS WITH 'STARTLING' ARCHAEOLOGICAL DISCOVERIES

Jones said the drilling uncovered rich black soil, which researchers plan to test for organic content this winter at Ankara University.

"Noah's Ark was a giant wooden boat, according to the Bible," he said.

NOAH'S ARK MYSTERY ENTERS NEW PHASE AS RESEARCHERS PROBE DEEP BENEATH SITE

"As wood decays, you're gonna find elevated organic matter. This year, as we drilled into the formation, we did not find a solid rock layer, like the critics said. But we did find large deposits of highly rich black soil that has hopefully high organics."

The researchers hope the analysis will help determine whether there are signs of human activity or materials consistent with decayed wood beneath the formation.

Jones also pointed to a 2024 soil survey that he said contained three times more organic matter inside the boat-shaped formation than samples collected just outside it.

Fox News' Andrea Margolis contributed to this report.

title: The URC talking points as Wales hopefuls impress
description: Which players are impressing as Cardiff and Dragons enjoy strong starts in the United Rugby Championship while Scarlets and Ospreys are still hunting a win.
fullText:
Only two rounds of the United Rugby Championship (URC) have been completed but it is Cardiff and Dragons who are the early Welsh pacesetters, while Scarlets and Ospreys are languishing at the bottom of the table.

Cardiff have won both games and lie second, while Dragons in sixth are unbeaten after winning an entertaining 10-try derby against Scarlets in Newport.

Scarlets and Ospreys, 14th and 15th respectively, are battling for long-term survival, with only one west Wales side set to exist in two years, but currently they would love just a victory after two defeats each.

While Louis Rees-Zammit, Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan continue to star in England's Prem, BBC Sport Wales looks at what has happened in the URC over the weekend.

Wales wing Adams targets third World Cup

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

A year ago Dragons were lamenting missed opportunities in the first block of the season.

Now, aided by the belief built in the second half of 2025-26, they have started to take them.

Filo Tiatia's men are digging deep in tough moments when previously they have folded, with the head coach deserving great credit for that.

"You are not just fighting for the players on the field. There is a deeper understanding in the group around what they are actually fighting for," said Tiatia.

Dragons scored six tries against Scarlets and the driving line-out that earned a late leveller at Benetton was once again a weapon.

There is also variety to their game with balance in wide positions courtesy of the power of new recruit Anzelo Tuitavuki and the pace of Rio Dyer.

Dragons also blew several chances to add to their try tally and can certainly be more clinical in the 22.

"There is lots to grow, lots to improve, but to come away with the points at home was important," said Tiatia.

Dragons will hope to extend their unbeaten start to the campaign with Ospreys and Perpignan visiting Rodney Parade in the URC and Challenge Cup.

With those games followed by a trip to Swansea and a home fixture against Zebre, the first block could give Tiatia's side a launchpad.

Dragons trio continuing Gwent's Tongan tradition

Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies was left to reflect on some familiar problems as his side suffered a second successive defeat.

The continued inability to defend driving line-outs and giving away needless penalties, typified by the second-half yellow card picked up by captain Josh Macleod, contributed to another loss.

"There were probably three or four big moments which the game turned on," said Davies.

"Those moments added up eventually to a yellow card and we were under pressure in the last 20 minutes."

Scarlets, who also suffered a slow start in 2025-26, are missing influential injured back-row forwards Fletcher Anderson and Taine Plumtree.

"There is no doubt those two are high-quality players and would bring ability and quality to any team," said Davies.

“It would be nice to get them back and have them as options.”

Scarlets face a reunion on Saturday with former head coach Wayne Pivac, who is now coaching a Benetton side also looking for a first victory.

"It is very important," said Davies. "All points are crucial and that's why we're into a massive game next week."

A tour to South Africa to start the season was always going to test Ospreys and they failed to upset the odds against Sharks or Lions.

A four-try bonus in Durban at least got the points tally moving and Mark Jones should profit from team bonding and having given 27 members of his squad starts.

Another big plus came from former Australia captain Liam Wright wearing six on his back in successive professional fixtures for the first time since 2024 after several years of injury misfortune.

The blind-side flanker has already made an impression with his work rate, line-out skills and ability to do the simple stuff well, with his leadership an added bonus.

It could be argued that Ospreys lack big ball carriers – and they will hope to get that from a different department in the coming weeks with the availability of former Australia wing Marika Koroibete – but Wright can be an excellent addition if he stays fit.

There should be plenty more to come as the 28-year-old builds momentum.

Cardiff have claimed nine points from wins against Scarlets and Zebre but their programme will ramp up in the next two weeks.

After defeating teams that finished 14th and 16th in the URC last season, Corniel van Zyl's side will face defending league champions Leinster on Saturday in Dublin before a Champions Cup opener at English Prem winners Northampton.

Cardiff coasted into a 40-8 lead against Zebre but know they cannot afford to repeat the concentration lapse that allowed the Italians to score three tries and 19 points.

"It's something to work on," said Van Zyl. "It's stuff we can control but we take the win. We don't normally have that kind of lead, so it's unfamiliar territory."

Leinster have been in South Africa for the opening two games with narrow defeats by Lions and Sharks, claiming three bonus points.

The Irish province return for the first competitive game at their redeveloped home, which is now called the Laya Arena and has a capacity of 20,600.

"We know they're a mega club, have very, very good players, good systems and good coaches, so it will be a nice challenge for us," said Van Zyl.

"Hopefully we'll have a few players back. We have eight days this time around, so more time to prepare and recover."

The Zebre fixture was one to remember for 18-year-old Cardiff hooker Tom Howe, who celebrated his Cardiff debut as a replacement.

"It is unbelievable," said Howe. "I have grown up watching these games and my dad used to take me, so to get the chance to come here and play with my family watching is amazing."

WRU seek to sell SRC side RGC to private investors

Wales head coach Steve Tandy will have been an interested observer because he names his Nations Championship squad in 16 days' time.

There are only two more matches for some fringe players to impress, so the past weekend will have been important.

The player-of-the-match, two-try display from Dragons hooker Elliot Dee was timely as he looks to challenge Lake, Ryan Elias, Evan Lloyd and Liam Belcher in the international pecking order.

Scarlets wing Macs Page, who was an unused player in a Wales squad in 2025, demonstrated some of that past form with two tries of his own, including a superb solo effort.

He enjoyed a fascinating battle against Dragons favourite Rio Dyer, who had a mixed first half followed by an outstanding second period where his early kick-off regather set the tone.

Dyer’s searing break later led directly to Macleod‘s yellow card, which helped tip the match in Dragons' favour.

Rees-Zammit, Blair Murray, Ellis Mee, Josh Adams, Tom Rogers, Mason Grady, and Gabriel Hamer-Webb might be above Dyer, Mee and Tom Bowen in Tandy’s mind but this weekend in Newport just provided the Wales boss with a gentle reminder.
