title: Trump predicts a ‘big surprise’ for Republicans as he rallies voters in Ohio
description:
VANDALIA, Ohio — President Donald Trump rallied Saturday for Republicans in Ohio’s competitive races for Senate and governor, predicting that the party will defy expectations in a choppy midterm election climate.
“I think we’re going to have a big surprise, because they don’t know what’s happening,” Trump said while speaking onstage inside a high school gymnasium near Dayton.
“Just get out and vote,” Trump added. “If you do that, we’re going to win, and we’re going to win big. And we’re going to shove it up their ass.
fullText:
VANDALIA, Ohio — President Donald Trump rallied Saturday for Republicans in Ohio’s competitive races for Senate and governor, predicting that the party will defy expectations in a choppy midterm election climate.

“I think we’re going to have a big surprise, because they don’t know what’s happening,” Trump said while speaking onstage inside a high school gymnasium near Dayton.

“Just get out and vote,” Trump added. “If you do that, we’re going to win, and we’re going to win big. And we’re going to shove it up their ass.”

The visit, part of what White House officials have told NBC News will be a push through at least 17 states between now and Nov. 3, was aimed at boosting Sen. Jon Husted and GOP gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy.

Trump, who won Ohio three times by comfortable margins, opened his speech with praise for both before moving into broader remarks to promote himself and his administration. He also offered support for local Rep. Mike Turner and for several House candidates in attendance, including Derek Merrin, the Republican running against longtime Democratic Rep. Marcy Kaptur in northwest Ohio.

Husted’s bid to keep the Senate seat — which he was appointed to after JD Vance was elected vice president — has become a subject of concern among Republicans in Ohio and Washington. In August, the National Republican Senatorial Committee warned in a memo that Husted’s past enthusiasm for building data centers was hurting his campaign. Others have expressed worries that Husted, who has long wanted to be governor, has not put his full heart into the race.

The battle is one of the most expensive and competitive Senate races in the country this fall. Along with a handful of other key contests, the clash between Husted and Brown could determine partisan control of the chamber. This week, the Senate Leadership Fund, a super PAC affiliated with Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota, poured another $14 million into Ohio to prop up Husted, bringing the group’s investment in the state to $93 million.

“Sen. Jon Husted votes to put Ohio first, and he votes all the time,” Trump said before relating conversations he’s had with Thune and others: “They think he’s phenomenal.”

The high school gym where Trump spoke Saturday night was a smaller venue than has been typical for his rallies. The home court of the Butler High School Aviators seats up to 5,000. There were several stretches of empty seats in upper bleachers as Trump took the stage — and many more by the time he finished speaking 93 minutes later.

In Ohio and elsewhere, Republicans are wrestling with how to win at a time when polls show Trump and the war with Iran are highly unpopular and when voters most loyal to Trump might stay home because he’s not on the ballot.

“As a lifelong Republican who’s voted in every election since I was 18 and in every primary election as a Republican, I have real concerns that we’re going to be able to turn out the every-four-year Trump voter,” Nick Owens, a former GOP chair in Ohio’s Brown County and former member of the state Board of Education, told NBC News last month. “I have real concerns that those voters just will not come to the polls.”

Trump acknowledged that dynamic explicitly Saturday and repeated an argument he’s been making on the campaign trail this fall.

“When I run, we win,” Trump said. “But for some reason, when I don’t run, they draw 44% less people. So what I’m going to do is ask you to just pretend that I’m running, because if we do, and if you draw the people, you’re going to win, and we’re going to win big.”

Husted, speaking to reporters before the rally, described Trump as a unique asset in his race.

“Well, he won Ohio by 11 points in the last election, and if we get those same voters to turn out in this election, we’ll win,” Husted said.

Alex Triantafilou, the Ohio GOP chair, told NBC News that the rally was “hugely important” in the effort to motivate those low-propensity, Trump-loyal voters.

“We know in Ohio that if we turn out the same electorate that we turned out in 2024, that we’ll win every race,” Triantafilou said in an interview. “Nobody speaks to that crowd better than President Trump.”

The Saturday rally included a cameo from Jon Gruden, the former NFL coach who years ago was a teammate of Husted’s on the University of Dayton football team.

“Jon Husted is a lot more than my friend,” an animated Gruden told the audience. “He was a great player. … He will never quit on you or anybody.”

Trump marveled about Husted’s football-playing days, of which he said he was unaware until hearing about them from Gruden.

“Nobody told me you were a great athlete,” Trump said, before taking a jab at his Democratic rival: “And Brown was not — he was not an athlete. That guy can’t tie his shoes.”

For its part Saturday, the Brown team sent a mobile billboard linking Husted’s support for the Iran war to higher gas prices through Dayton and on the streets near the rally.

“Jon Husted has turned his back on working families — he’s only looking out for his billionaire buddies and special interests,” Brown said in a statement from his campaign.

Ohio also is home to what polls show is a close race to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. Ramaswamy faces Democrat Amy Acton, a physician who served as the state’s health director under DeWine. Ohioans have not elected a Democrat as governor in 20 years, but at a time when high prices are top of mind for voters, there are questions about the billionaire Ramaswamy’s appeal, especially in rural parts of the state.

Ramaswamy, like Husted, addressed the crowd early during the rally, and Trump invited both to return to the stage during his speech. Trump introduced Ramaswamy by noting how he had briefly run against him for the 2024 Republican presidential nomination.

“He was a nasty guy,” Trump said of Ramaswamy. “But you know what? He was smart. He loves the state. He’s actually got a great heart.”

Compared with Husted, Ramaswamy was otherwise less of a focus of Trump’s remarks. Trump, for example, criticized Senate Democrats who this week blocked Husted’s Ratepayer Protection Act, which aims to rein in higher utility costs associated with power-hungry data centers.

Republicans, Trump said, are “taking historic action to ensure that Big Tech data centers benefit local communities.”

Trump then made the argument for data centers, despite the fears it could be a losing issue for Husted.

“We want them,” Trump said. “Look, there’s so much money to be made for Ohio. You can’t just turn them off. They’ll go to China.”

Trump also recited the lyrics to the 1968 Al Wilson song “The Snake” — a recurring, crowd-pleasing bit in his rally speeches — with a new, localized twist. Trump dedicated the song, which he uses as an allegory for trusting communities that welcome immigrants, to nearby Springfield, Ohio.

The city became a flashpoint in the 2024 presidential election after Trump repeated the unsubstantiated and racially charged claim that Haitian immigrants in the city were eating pets.

At another point, the crowd broke into chants of “four more years” for the term-limited president.

“I’d love to do the four-more-year thing,” Trump responded in a teasing tone before suggesting that the press would overplay his remarks.

“We’re driving them totally crazy,” Trump said, referring to the media. “But I love doing it. I love being with you. I really do.”

title: Iran tells U.S. there is no military solution to Middle East war
description:
Ships anchored off the coast of Musandam governorate in Oman near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday (-)
Iran's top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States' war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.
A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.
The main point of contention remains Iran's attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker struck by an unknown projectile.
"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors. 
"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.
fullText:
Iran's top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States' war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

The main point of contention remains Iran's attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker struck by an unknown projectile.

"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.

"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.

The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations.

Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.

The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it.

On Sunday, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said a tanker in the Hormuz "reported being struck by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the engine room", though the crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was recorded.

The agency did not specify the date of the incident, the vessel's origin or destination, or whether it was an oil tanker or LNG carrier.

Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.

Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.

Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday characterised the latest US counterproposal as being "in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues".

"We have clearly indicated that we are focusing on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz," he said, adding that reopening the waterway required "an end to the disruptions to Iranian commercial maritime traffic and the lifting of sanctions".

The United States and Israel have characterised the war as being necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons -- a goal it has long denied pursuing -- though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets.

The United States has not struck Iran since September 1, but it has recently pursued a fresh military buildup in the region.

US media outlet Axios reported that Washington has deployed additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to help protect key energy facilities from possible Iranian retaliation.

It also reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group were heading to the Middle East, where they could join two other US carrier strike groups already in the region.

Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.

title: Drummond wins mixed doubles title on return to curling
description: Vicky Drummond marks her return to competitive curling in style, partnering Euan Kyle to an emphatic victory at the Scottish Curling Mixed Doubles Championship.
fullText:
Vicky Drummond marked her return to competitive curling in style, partnering Euan Kyle to an emphatic victory at the Scottish Curling Mixed Doubles Championship.

The 33-year-old intensive care nurse left the sport shortly after winning gold at the 2022 Olympics.

Drummond (nee Wright) and Kyle, a bronze medallist from this year's World Championship, won every match they played in Aberdeen this week.

Their 100% run culminated with an 8-1 victory over Katie McMillan and Archie Hyslop in the final, which was over after a mere five ends.

The runners-up lost two of their six group matches but edged out the previously unbeaten partnership of Sophie Jackson and Duncan McFadzean in their semi-final.

Drummond's Olympic skip, Eve Muirhead, 36, also came out of retirement for this tournament.

However, Team GB's chef de mission at this year's Olympics did not progress to the play-offs as she and Bobby Lammie finished fourth in their seven-team section.

title: Daryz claims rare back-to-back success in the Arc
description: Daryz repeats last year's success in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, becoming just the ninth horse to win Europe's richest Flat race more than once.
fullText:
Daryz became just the ninth horse to win the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe for a second time, repeating his 2025 success with a late burst to claim victory in the richest Flat race in Europe.

The Francis-Henri Graffard trained four-year-old became the first colt to double up in the Arc at ParisLongchamp since Alleged did it 48 years ago.

Mickael Barzalona, the winning jockey last year, took the ride again and expertly manoeuvred Daryz through the 16-strong field to hit the front in the closing stages.

The 13-8 favourite needed a photo finish last year but this time claimed victory by more than a length from Bay City Roller (28-1), with Aidan O'Brien's 10-1 chance Diamond Necklace finishing third.

Daryz pips Minnie Hauk to Arc win in photo finish

"To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse," Barzalona told Sky Sports.

"It was a really tough race, it didn't go as we expected but he showed his talent and that made the difference in the end."

It was considered a gamble to keep last year's Arc winner in training aged four, when most top-class colts are retired at three because of the lucrative breeding fees.

But it has paid off for owners Aga Khan Studs, who claimed the winner's cheque of more than £2.5m.

Daryz added two further Group One victories to his tally this season and won his Arc prep race in grand style last month.

"He's a good horse, he's a champion," said jubilant winning trainer Graffard, following his second success in the race.

"It's rare that I am confident in the race - I always try to keep my feet on the ground because it is so hard to win these races.

"But I knew that if things were going right for him during the trip he was very hard to beat because he is a real champion."

title: Dual-code winger Nawaqanitawase stars as Roosters win NRL Final
description: Mark Nawaqanitawase scores two tries in his last match before switching back to rugby union to help Sydney Roosters beat Newcastle Knights 19-18 in the NRL Grand Final.
fullText:
Australian National Rugby League Grand Final

Tries: Nawaqanitawase 2, Smith Goals: Walker 3 Drop goal: Cherry-Evans

Tries: Manuleleua, Ponga, Marzhew Goals: Smith 3

Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries to help Sydney Roosters end the Newcastle Knights' fairytale in the National Rugby League Premiership Grand Final.

Nawaqanitawase, who is stepping away from rugby league and could represent Australia at the rugby union World Cup next year, crossed once in each half to help prevent a big upset in front of a crowd of 80,814 at Stadium Australia.

Newcastle were looking to win a first title since 2001 and become the first club since 1934 to win the Premiership after finishing bottom in the previous season.

A late try from the Knights' Greg Marzhew made it a one-point game, but the Roosters held on to clinch a 16th title and first since 2019 in what was Nawaqanitawase's last game before moving to play union in Japan.

He played union for four years with Super Rugby's Waratahs before switching to rugby league in 2024 to line up for the Roosters, and Sunday's victory was the ideal sign-off as his two-year contract comes to an end.

"Credit to the Knights, they fought for 80 minutes there," said 26-year-old Nawaqanitawase.

"This is going to last me a lifetime. It's sad to go, but I love everyone here, I love all the boys, and let's celebrate this win, far out."

England beware - the Australia try magician who swapped union for league

Nawaqanitawase played 11 times for the Wallabies between 2022 and 2023 before becoming the first union-to-league switcher to feature for the Kangaroos since Scott Gourley in 1991 when he played in last year's Ashes series.

The Knights, who finished three places below the Roosters in the regular season, looked determined not to give Nawaqanitawase his perfect swansong, with Francis Manuleleua and skipper Kalyn Ponga scoring early tries to give them a 12-0 lead.

But Nawaqanitawase cut the deficit with a clever kick and chase five minutes before the break.

Roosters centre Billy Smith forced his way over in the 47th minute for a converted try that levelled the scores at 12-12.

Sam Walker put the Sydney side in front for the first time with a penalty seven minutes later, and Nawaqanitawase added his second try in the right corner before the hour to extend the lead to 18-12.

Daly Cherry-Evans, 37, playing his last NRL game before his switch to Super League side Hull FC for the 2027 season, slotted a drop-goal to extend the advantage to seven points.

Knights summoned the spirit of their sensational semi-final win over Penrith Panthers with 12 men, as Marzhew crossed with four minutes remaining, but they were unable to complete what would have been a famous comeback.

'An unbelievable story' - inside unfancied Wakefield's rapid ascent

title: Wu wins first title since Crucible as Chinese snooker hits new high
description: Wu Yize claims his first ranking title since he became world champion - a result that means China will have the top two players in the rankings for the first time.
fullText:
Wu Yize secured his first ranking title since becoming world champion with a 10-5 win over Yuan Sijun in an all-Chinese final at the Shenzhen Open.

A profitable week for 22-year-old Wu pushes him to a career high of second place in the world rankings, behind Zhao Xintong.

It means that China has the leading two players in the rankings for the first time, further illustrating the country's position as a snooker superpower.

Wu became the second-youngest player to lift snooker's most coveted title at the Crucible when he beat Shaun Murphy in May, and he followed that up with a composed performance to see off surprise finalist Yuan at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.

Having demolished Judd Trump 6-1 in the semi-finals, Wu had early breaks of 117 and 80 to move 3-1 ahead against Yuan.

But, playing in his first ranking final, Yuan then reeled off three frames in a row.

Wu responded with two more half-centuries in the final frames of the opening session to take a 5-4 lead in the best-of-19 match.

Prospects of a tight final all the way to the finish line soon evaporated.

World champion Wu returned with breaks of 74 and 62 to take control at 8-5 in the evening session as Yuan struggled with his safety play.

And there was no way back for Yuan, 26, as Wu made sure of the trophy and the £177,000 top prize.

While Wu moves to second in the rankings, going ahead of Trump and Neil Robertson, Yuan jumps seven spots to 26th and earns £76,000.

title: Djokovic beats Zverev to reach China Open semis
description: Novak Djokovic's quest to win a first trophy of 2026 continues with a hard-fought victory in the quarter-finals of the China Open.
fullText:
Novak Djokovic battled back from a set down to defeat top seed Alexander Zverev and book his place in the China Open semi-finals.

The 39-year-old Serbian triumphed 4-6 6-4 6-4 against world number two Zverev and will play Daniil Medvedev in the last four.

Djokovic's victory over Zverev dented the German's quest to finish the year as the world's number one-ranked player.

"These are the kind of moments that I still play for, compete for," Djokovic said.

"The motivation is big when you are feeling good and competing at par with the best players in the world in front of 15,000 people.

"These are the kind of moments that define dreams, I think, of every tennis player."

Sabalenka stunned by Bartunkova at China Open

In their first meeting in just under 16 months, Djokovic initially struggled to handle Zverev's power, and the 29-year-old secured the first set after capitalising on a break in the first game.

However, Djokovic managed to work his way back into the contest, and the 24-time Grand Slam winner seized an opportunity with a break at 5-4 in the second set to level the match.

Little separated the pair in the third set, but the veteran struck again at 5-4 on Zverev's serve to clinically seal victory.

It took Djokovic's unbeaten tally in Beijing to 32 matches as he moved a step closer to a seventh China Open title and a first trophy of what has been a difficult 2026, with form and fitness proving challenging.

"It's been a struggle this year for different reasons," Djokovic added.

"But I'm still there, still grinding, still making the youngsters work for their money. I'm just glad to push it through."

Djokovic will face third seed Medvedev, who earlier overcame Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7-4) 6-3, on Monday.

Poland's Hubert Hurkacz also progressed to the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 win over Karen Khachanov.

He will play Australia's Alex de Minaur who was off the pace in the first set against Andrey Rublev before he stepped up to record a 1-6 6-2 6-3 victory.

title: Evans claims dramatic WRC title after Solberg crash
description: Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashes in the final moments of Rally Italia Sardegna.
fullText:
Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashed in a dramatic finish to the Rally Italia Sardegna.

Sweden's Solberg was on course to snatch the lead on the final stage of the last round of the World Rally Championship (WRC) when he crashed with less than 100 metres to go.

"It hasn't sunk in," said a shocked Evans, who became the first British world champion in 25 years.

"I was sure it was over. I feel for Oliver, he had an incredible weekend. I don't know what to say."

The 37-year-old and co-driver Scott Martin had led for much of the 2026 season and took a 21-point advantage into the final round in Sardinia.

But that gap had shrunk to a solitary point by the time the drivers lined up for the last of 17 stages, bringing back painful memories of previous narrow misses for Evans.

Solberg, 25, needed only to beat his Toyota team-mate in the final stage to claim enough bonuses to be champion, but crashed two corners from the finish.

Evans becomes only the third British man to win the WRC title after Colin McRae in 1995 and Richard Burns in 2001.

Relive dramatic final stage shootout for title as it happened

The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory

Solberg, whose father Petter won the WRC title in 2003, won the rally by almost a minute ahead of nine-time world champion Sebastien Ogier.

He and English co-driver Elliott Edmondson were also on course to win the final stage and collect a maximum 35 points for the weekend to take the title by two points.

However, his crash meant he finished five points behind Evans in the overall standings.

A third Toyota driver, Sami Pajari, finished a further one point behind in third - having seen his own title challenge evaporate on the final weekend.

An inconsolable Solberg remained in his car for some time at the end of the stage before being encouraged to take to the podium by Gazoo Racing team principal Jari-Matti Latvala and team-mate Ogier.

"Two corners, two corners," said an emotional Solberg.

"First congratulations to Elfyn, he has been very consistent all season. That I even had a shot after my rollercoaster of a season is incredible.

"I tried everything. I knew I was pushing but didn't know if it was enough. I pushed even more and I couldn't save the car. I tried my very best."

Evans, from Dolgellau in north Wales, had previously missed out on the title on the final day three times and in two of those seasons he had taken a lead into the concluding rally before losing out to Ogier in 2020 and 2025.

"I don't really know what my reaction is. It's surreal with how it happened. It's a relief," he said.

"It wouldn't by my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done."

For Toyota sporting director Kaj Lindstrom there were mixed feelings.

"That was the hardest thing. The ending was quite something, I didn't expect it," said the Finn.

"It was a good fight and we all saw that Oliver was all or nothing. It held all the way to the end.

"Oliver still has time but Elfyn finally got his title so we're really happy for him."

The WRC season was reduced to 13 rounds when the Saudi Arabia event, originally planned for next month, was cancelled because of the ongoing unrest in the Middle East.

Rally Italia Sardegna marked the end of Jon Armstrong's rookie season at the top level of WRC, and he produced his best result when finishing seventh.

"It's been good to have a clean weekend with a strong result," said the M-Sport Ford driver.

"It's not been an easy year and this was a rally to show we can put it together. A big thanks to everyone who has been supporting us, it's been a great year and it's been a privilege to drive this car."

Armstrong's team-mate and fellow Irishman Josh McErlean did not fare as well despite running as high as sixth on Saturday before retiring after a collision with a tree.

He also had to stop twice on Sunday before finishing well off the pace but claimed ninth spot in the championship.

title: Dominant Verstappen & superb Hamilton recovery - driver ratings
description: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
fullText:
Max Verstappen secured his first win of the 2026 season with victory at a chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had an eventful race and finished third, while Kimi Antonelli extended his championship lead to 84 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell with his second place at Sepang.

Russell retired from the grand prix while in third place with a power unit failure.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Malaysia...

Verstappen wins Bahrain GP in Malaysia after long delays

Hard to find much wrong this weekend. Dominant through every part of qualifying for his first pole of the season. A poor start but then recovered after losing out to both Mercedes drivers to control a hugely difficult race.

Proving Baku was just a blip for the championship leader. Produced an excellent start to take the lead and ultimately brought home second on a weekend where Mercedes never looked entirely comfortable.

A superb recovery after Ferrari's decision to start on slick tyres sent him tumbling from the front row to 18th. Hamilton fought all the way back to the podium and passed Isack Hadjar after the final safety car to complete one of his best drives of the season.

Close to team-mate Hamilton in qualifying before suffering the same early tyre nightmare in the race. Recovered impressively through the field to fourth and ensured Ferrari salvaged a huge result from a strategy that initially looked disastrous.

Third fastest in qualifying was an excellent performance before his engine penalty dropped him to eighth on the grid. A great battle with Hamilton even if he did lose out with Leclerc denying him fourth at the end too.

Never quite had McLaren at the sharp end but made the right early call to abandon the slicks and start from the pit lane on intermediate tyres. Recovered to sixth and comfortably beat Norris on a day when simply keeping everything clean counted for plenty.

One of his strongest races of the year. Just missed Q3 and then made a sensational start in the wet conditions, gaining seven positions and briefly running fourth before eventually bringing his Racing Bulls home in seventh.

Aston Martin finally showed some signs of life and Alonso made sure to capitalise. Reached Q2 on merit and converted 12th on the grid into an excellent eighth-place finish. Comfortably the team's best result for some time.

A frustrating weekend that ended with an avoidable mistake. Qualified ahead of Piastri and was right behind his team-mate before the final restart, only to lose control behind the safety car and ran through the gravel, dropping him to ninth.

A really impressive recovery considering he started at the very back because of his power unit penalty. Helped Lawson with a tow on Saturday and then charged through to score the final point on Sunday.

Andrew Benson Q&A: Send us your questions

Missing Q2 was disappointing but he responded with a strong recovery on Sunday. Climbed from 15th on the grid to finish just outside the points and comfortably ahead of Audi team-mate Bortoleto after the Brazilian's penalty.

A much more competitive weekend for Aston Martin generally. Stroll joined Alonso in Q2 and kept himself out of trouble through a chaotic race to finish 12th, even if his team-mate ultimately extracted more from the opportunity.

Started 21st due to grid penalties, so 13th represented a very respectable recovery. Kept things clean after his costly mistake last time out and made up plenty of ground in difficult conditions.

Another fairly anonymous weekend for Haas. Knocked out in Q1 and although he gained a couple of places during the race, 14th was about all there was to show for it.

Frustrated with Haas' qualifying run plan after going out in Q1 and never really recovered from there. Great start and was fighting well inside the top 10. Ultimately finished behind Bearman and was unable to make the changing conditions work sufficiently to threaten the points.

Qualifying ninth was an excellent start but Sunday unravelled almost immediately. Nearly lost the car on slicks during the formation procedure and ultimately fell all the way to 16th as Alpine's gamble failed to pay off.

Williams struggled for pace throughout the weekend but 13th represented a good qualifying. His race was then further compromised by contact with Bortoleto, for which the Audi driver was penalised, so 17th doesn't tell the whole story.

There was plenty to like about reaching Q3 in the Audi, but the race undid that good work. Contact with Sainz earned him a penalty and left him 18th after starting inside the top 10.

Qualified last and never looked likely to make meaningful progress even amid all the chaos. Reaching the chequered flag was at least something for Cadillac, but 19th completed another difficult weekend.

A far better race than his eighth place in qualifying suggested. Made an excellent start, ran inside the top three for virtually the entire afternoon and, even if he couldn't match Mercedes team-mate Antonelli, was heading for another podium before a power-unit failure stopped him with five laps remaining.

Williams lacked pace from the outset and qualifying 20th left him with an enormous amount of work to do. His eventual retirement was caused by a gearbox problem rather than a driving error, but there had been little sign of any kind of meaningful challenge before then.

A weekend to forget. Qualified ahead of Cadillac team-mate Perez but admitted his decision to run slicks was a risk before spinning into the gravel on lap nine and triggering the first safety car.

title: Will Wisconsin be ranked after blowout win vs. Michigan State?
description: The Wisconsin Badgers made another statement on Saturday, Oct. 3, defeating Michigan State 31-3 to extend their winning streak to four games.
fullText:
The Wisconsin Badgers made another statement on Saturday, Oct. 3, defeating Michigan State 31-3 to extend their winning streak to four games.

After an impressive comeback victory over then-No. 14 Penn State the week before, Wisconsin has continued to build momentum and put itself in the conversation for a spot in the AP Top 25.

However, will a dominant win over the Spartans be enough to finally get the Badgers ranked?

Wisconsin entered the weekend just outside the rankings, receiving the most AP votes of any unranked team. In addition, they received votes in the US LBM Coaches Poll as well.

With its latest victory, the Badgers have certainly strengthened their case, improving to 4-1 overall and 2-0 in Big Ten play.

Rolling the highlights from today’s win against Michigan State 👐 pic.twitter.com/6V6HT7cTHE

Quarterback Colton Joseph accounted for four touchdowns against the Spartans, while the defense held Michigan State to just three points and forced five fourth-down stops. Still, there is an argument to be made that Wisconsin will need another week before breaking into the Top 25.

While the 28-point victory was certainly convincing, Michigan State entered the matchup with a 2-2 record and has now lost three consecutive games. Beating a struggling Spartans team, even by a significant margin, may not be enough to move the Badgers past the teams currently occupying the final spots in the rankings.

A graphic featured on Saturday afternoon's game also put Wisconsin's lengthy absence from the AP Top 25 into perspective, stating that the team has been unranked in the last 53 AP polls, the 5th longest drought in program history.

Goodnight Badger Nation 😴 pic.twitter.com/VIJgtnq7tJ

That said, the Badgers have already proven they can compete with ranked opponents after taking down Penn State on the road. Four consecutive wins, including a victory over a previously ranked opponent, make a compelling argument for Wisconsin's inclusion.

Ultimately, Wisconsin may have done enough to earn consideration, but that doesn't necessarily mean it has done enough to earn a ranking. With a bye week ahead, the Badgers will have to wait and see whether voters believe their recent performances warrant a return to the Top 25. A ranking this week is possible, but it wouldn't be surprising to see Wisconsin remain just outside the cutoff for another week.

title: Mike Gansey discusses plan for Joel Embiid, health of Sixers star
description: Philadelphia 76ers President of Basketball Operations Mike Gansey discusses the plan for Joel Embiid and the health of his star big man.
fullText:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the Philadelphia 76ers head into another season and another chase for the Larry O'Brien trophy, one of the main focuses will be how they manage Joel Embiid and his health.

Obviously, Embiid has had a fantastic week of training camp. He has had a summer to just workout and focus on his body rather than having to rehab a nagging injury and the Sixers will benefit from that. His teammates have noticed a big difference with him and President of Basketball Operations Mike Gansey has been happy with what he's seen from his star big man, but obviously, there will be a plan for how they manage him.

"We got a plan together, and he's been in every single drill, every single practice," said Gansey before the team's Blue X White scrimmage on Saturday. "So there's been no restrictions. Obviously, worked super hard this summer. He told me he was motivated. He wanted to have a great year, and he's showing it out there. Looks a little bit lighter, obviously, but the skill level is still there. I mean, some of the stuff he does now seeing it in person, like it's incredible to watch some of the stuff he does on the floor. So we're excited about him, and he's been good this first week."

In terms of that "plan", Gansey didn't delve too much into it, but the Sixers have an idea of what they want to do with him in terms of his workload. Obviously, Philadelphia has a coach in Nick Nurse who dealt with load management of a star in the form of Kawhi Leonard during his time with the Toronto Raptors. It's all about taking it in chunks and seeing how Embiid handles the work he has put in.

"Simon (Rice), you know, from our medical team, me, myself, him, coach, we've been talking about it all summer, just trying to figure out a plan," Gansey added. "The best thing for him this summer to obviously play as many games as he can, but also be healthy and be consistent throughout the whole year. Because hopefully we're playing into May and June, and hopefully he's in those games and he's healthy and at his best."

One has to wonder if Embiid can stay healthy and continue to make strides in that area, that the plan could be tweaked a bit. Maybe he can play in back-to-backs or up his minutes or the number of his games played. It all depends, but Gansey at the moment just wants to focus on the team's plan.

"I think just for us, it's like, stick to the plan," Gansey finished. "Obviously, subject to change how things go, but it's been a good first week. The plan's been going well this first week, and obviously, have the scrimmage today (Saturday), day off tomorrow (Sunday). So get to Monday and then evaluate because I think with him, it's just kind of day to day and just seeing how he's feeling."

The Sixers will open the preseason on Monday against the New York Knicks.

title: Morning after: Final thoughts on Notre Dame’s rainy win over UNC
description: Notre Dame football defeated North Carolina, and here are some final thoughts wrapping up the Irish’s 37-26 victory.
fullText:
Notre Dame football got a solid win on Saturday afternoon, and while the 37-26 score won't inspire many, North Carolina is better than its 2-2 record.

The Irish are still undefeated at 5-0, and are squarely in the mix for a spot in the College Football Playoff. Games like these happen every weekend in college football, but it was still another double-digit victory for Notre Dame, as streak of now is at fourteen games, and the win streak is at fifteen.

There was plenty of good that we saw from the Irish on Saturday, and some bad as well. After getting a chance to digest the win, here are some thoughts wrapping up Notre Dame's win at North Carolina.

Got it done 👍#GoIrish☘️ pic.twitter.com/E2h90WS9w5

The end score was not, but it was helped by yet another garbage time touchdown by an opponent. Those still count, but it really doesn't tell the whole story of the game. There were flashes of a CFP title team, the response when it was 21-20 at the start of the third quarter, an improving run game along with CJ Carr being brilliant yet again. Notre Dame did not play a complete game, but the talent to get there is present.

Jonaz Walton has his first 100+ yard game.

That’s RB1.

Early on when the weather was dry, the Irish struggled to run the ball, especially in the middle of the line. That all changed as the game plan did with the rain, as the offensive line established itself and saw multiple solid runs through the interior. The way was paved by freshman Jonaz Walton, then Nolan James Jr. got through some tight windows as well. Overall, the Irish showed a much improved attack with the back accounting for 227 yards, as Walton has his first-career 100-yard rushing game with 120. There weren't many explosive runs, but the ground and pound worked well against the Tar Heels.

Billy Edwards Jr. throws his second pick of the day, and Luke Talich comes away with the interception for Notre Dame! pic.twitter.com/TJFDE4KxLz

After missing last week's game against Purdue with a hand injury, Talich's return showed he isn't fazed with having to wear a cast. He's pick off a pass, and block an extra point while having impact tackles in the run game. Talich wasn't expected to be this big of a contributor this season, but his emergence shows the top-end depth that Notre Dame has.

Absolute dot by CJ Carr pic.twitter.com/c5Fk4HUV0a

It cannot be understated how good Carr has been this season, even without putting up monster stats. He's super consistent, doesn't turn the ball over, and put the ball in spots where only his receivers can make a play. Carr's anticipation on throws is elite, as he lead more than a few to open spots on the field. I think there was just two or three throws that he'd like to have back out of 29 attempts, which is a pretty good day.

In the third quarter today against UNC @NDFootball rushed 20 times for 122 yards and possessed the ball for 13:18 of the quarter's 15 minutes.

It was the right move, as the rainy conditions made it hard for the ball to be gripped. Notre Dame made the choice to run the ball, and the whole team responded. As noted above, the backs took over and it was great to see. This is about the coaching staff, knowing that the players could play an old school-type game to carve out a win. It was a great strategical move by Notre Dame, and it paid off.

Jasper Scaife with a brutal afternoon . Dropped punt. Dropped hold. Surely it rains in Australia?

We are accustomed to the Irish being the better special teams unit in every game, but this one didn't go their way. The biggest play was a 97-yard kickoff touchdown return to start the second half, but Jasper Scaife has trouble holding onto the ball all game. His mishandled a snap early and it was almost blocked, then couldn't get another on an extra point. Spencer Porath was perfect on the day, making his lone field goal try and all four extra points. Talich had the block, but it wasn't perfect and could have cost the Irish. This will need to be shored up, but some it the problems can be attributed to the rain.

JADEN JEFFERSON OPENS THE SECOND HALF WITH A HOUSE CALL 💥

📺 @espn x @UNCFootball pic.twitter.com/DVA3nRIfUs

Freeman has long talked about winning the middle eight, the final four minutes of the first half and first four of the second, which the Irish did not accomplish yesterday. North Carolina scored with 0:21 seconds before the half, cutting the lead to 21-14. They'd return the opening kickoff of the second half for another score, but luckily missed the two-point try due to a bad snap. The Tar Heels were squarely in the game at this point, and against a better team, this could have been a major disaster.

This article originally appeared on Fighting Irish Wire: Morning after: Final thoughts on Notre Dame's rainy win over UNC

title: Christian McCaffrey Fantasy Week 4 Start or Sit: Do Not Get Greedy With a Healthy First-Rounder

fullText:
San Francisco hosts Denver with McCaffrey fifth among running backs in PFN's Week 4 rankings, and the first three weeks have brought cramps, zero explosive plays and workload that never approached elite. He has still cleared 7-plus PPR points as a pass catcher every week and found paydirt three times, which is a perfectly acceptable bottom to his production curve and far better experienced in September than December. Kaelon Black runs hard without convincing Kyle Shanahan to tilt toward a split, so the patience on a first-round pick should be rewarded right when the schedule matters most.

Through three weeks, CMC dealt with cramps, doesn't have an explosive play and hasn't been asked to assume elite volume.

And yet, he still has 7-plus PPR points as a pass catcher in all three games and has found paydirt three times. If this is the bottom of the McCaffrey production curve, this is perfectly acceptable, and I'd much rather experience it in September than December.

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Football Start/Sit Optimizer

Kaelon Black runs hard, but he hasn't done much to convince Kyle Shanahan to tilt the usage long-term closer to a split. The production of Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson may make the CMC numbers look ordinary, but he's healthy and still a key part of this passing game. If I told you that you'd have that into October, you'd be happy with the state of your first-round pick, so don't get greedy.

Your picking of McCaffrey was always one that you hoped would pay off over the long haul. If touches have been managed early this season in a way that they never were in 2025, and there's a chance that we are rewarded for our patience in this regard at the perfect time.

title: Will Titans' Tyjae Spears, Kevin Winston, or Garrett Dellinger play?
description: Tennessee faces injury concerns for Tyjae Spears and others ahead of their Week 4 matchup against the Ravens.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans will travel to Baltimore to take on the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in what should be an interesting Week 4 matchup.

The Titans head into the week with some injury concerns, some of which come at a position shrouded in mystery. Tennessee enters Sunday with three players- Tyjae Spears, Kevin Winston Jr., and Garrett Dellinger questionable for the contest, with Dellinger being a late addition on Saturday due to an illness.

Dellinger spent all week battling to help replace Fernando Carmons and Jackson Slater at right guard after both were placed on injured reserve during the week.

Tennessee made a few roster moves and used an elevation to insulate themselves if any of the three players can't go. Tennessee added Dellinger on Wednesday along with veteran running back Michael Carter, and on Saturday, they used a standard elevation on Drew Moss. These moves cover Dellinger and Spears, but they did not use an elevation on a safety, a good sign Winston should be able to play.

With Tennessee signing Carter to the 53-man roster and head coach Robert Saleh mentioning Spears having to clear some hurdles to be active this week, it is a distinct possibility Spears sets this one out. He was a full participant in practice Friday, which bodes well, but with weather a concern, it will likely be a game-time decision.

If Spears can't go, look for rookie Nick Singleton to get a few added carries, with Carter sprinkled in. Singleton made his NFL debut against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2 and looked good, though he left some yards on the field. Carter is a veteran and can play multiple roles if called upon.

With Winston a mid-week addition to the injury report after injuring his shoulder during practice on Thursday and then sitting out practice on Friday, it is hard to tell his status. Winston is a key contributor to the defense, and his absence will be felt. With Tennessee not elevating any defensive backs, that should be a positive sign he will be available this week, but there is still a chance his shoulder holds him out.

If Winston can't go, veteran Tony Adams would take over as the starter, and Terrell Burgess and Erick Hallett will likely move into the backup roles. Hallett was added to the 53-man roster ahead of the Giants game and has been active in all three games this season. He brings more experience in the system than Burgess, which could help.

This is the biggest question of the weekend, given the Titans' right-guard situation. As of Friday, no starter had been announced after Dellinger and Atonio Mafi battled all week to replace Fernando Carmona as the starter, with the loser of the battle placed as the primary backup along the interior to replace Jackson Slater.

Since no one except the coaching staff knows the plan at right guard, it's easy to point to Mafi as the starter if Dellinger can't go. Mafi is a veteran with exerience playing under offensive line coach Carmen Bricillo and could have already won the job, so this makes for an interesting development.

Tennessee used a standard elevation on Drew Moss, which could point to Dellinger sitting out and Moss taking over the swing interior position.

title: Jayden Daniels injury update: Latest on Commanders QB's status for today's game
description: Jayden Daniels is working his way back from a dislocated elbow. Will he play for the Commanders in Week 4 against the Colts in London?
fullText:
Jayden Daniels' season seemed in jeopardy. Until it wasn't.

The Washington Commanders quarterback dislocated his elbow for a second straight season in the team's Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Things looked bleak in the immediate aftermath, with surgery being on the table for one of the league's young stars.

After an injury-riddled second season, that was the last thing that the 25-year-old needed. Yet surgery is on the back burner for now, and the elbow brace has come to the front, in hopes of saving the season for Daniels and the Commanders.

With the team set to kick off the London slate of games this season in Week 4, everyone wants to know: will Jayden Daniels be suited up for the international contest?

Daniels will not play in Week 4.

The Commanders signal-caller traveled with the team to London and returned to practice in a limited capacity ahead of Week 4. It represented a positive turn of events for Daniels, who failed to participate ahead of Week 3.

Daniels told reporters on Thursday, Oct. 1 that he was just taking everything "day by day" and wasn't surprised to be back on the field so quickly.

While he doesn't have a full range of motion with the brace on, Daniels vowed that it won't change anything about his game.

Overall, his concern level about reinjuring the elbow is low.

"That's what the brace is for," Daniels said. "If I had that concern, I would have gotten surgery."

The 25-year-old explained that he chose to avoid surgery for now because he wants to keep playing.

"I love playing football, I get paid to play football," Daniels said. "Everybody is hurting. I just feel for me being a leader, go out there and give it my shot to go out and play and obviously protect myself. I just love football and have a passion for it."

More: Will Jayden Daniels need elbow surgery? Experts explain 'unusual' reinjury

Daniels suffered a left elbow dislocation in Week 2.

X-rays showed no fracture, which was a good sign for Daniels' availability going forward. While he might eventually need surgery, there seems to be a chance that he could avoid it during the season by playing with a brace on.

Of course, it's unclear how the quarterback's elbow will react outside of a controlled practice setting.

The Commanders' performance without him and Daniels' ability to take hits could go a long way in determining his future availability.

Daniels appears to be on the fast track to return relatively soon.

His return to practice suggests he could return as early as Week 5 against the New York Giants. If Washington wants to err on the side of caution, the team has just two games left before a Week 7 bye after returning home from London.

While the Commanders would probably love to live in a world where Daniels doesn't get hurt, it's comforting to have a veteran like Mariota available to step in when needed. He is a steadying force with plenty of experience, and the Commanders have been able to lean on him.

Kaliakmanis is a seventh-round rookie out of Rutgers and hasn't gotten into a game yet.

title: Chuba Hubbard Fantasy Week 4 Start or Sit: Four Straight Top 15 Finishes Is the Bet

fullText:
Detroit visits Carolina on Sunday, and Hubbard sits 12th among running backs in PFN's Week 4 rankings against a defense that ranks among the five worst in the league at stopping production on the ground by per-rush EPA. His glow-up deserves real credit after a 2025 season of 3.8 yards per carry and one touchdown on 134 rushes: he has gained yardage on 92.7% of his carries this year and cleared 6.5 PPR points as a pass catcher in all three games. For the season, he's gained yardage on 92.7% of his carries, a rate that only trails James Cook among the bellcows, and has cleared 6.5 PPR points as a pass catcher in all three contests to open this season.

title: Genoa’s De Rossi: ‘When you see me playing the clown to blame players, I’m finished’
description: Daniele De Rossi insists Genoa will pull clear again after a dismal start that has brought one point from five matches.Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the coach was adamant the solution is not th...
fullText:
Daniele De Rossi insists Genoa will pull clear again after a dismal start that has brought one point from five matches.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the coach was adamant the solution is not theatrics.

"We'll get ourselves out of this situation like last year. The important thing is that everyone wants to immerse themselves in it. I want to create new good moments. With Genoa."

GENOA, ITALY – AUGUST 22: Daniele De Rossi, Head Coach of Genoa, before the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on August 22, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

He revealed that someone close to him had sent a photograph of him celebrating on his knees in front of the Genoa support, with the suggestion that fans want to see him like that again. The response was blunt.

"What am I supposed to do, celebrate after a defeat? When I went to greet my former fans under the Curva Sud last year, did I have grit on my face? No. I was dejected.

"I could put on a show on the bench: shout, yell, insult the players, attack them in press conferences as many of my colleagues do. Bang my fists and say the players have to take responsibility and be men, show their attributes. But you won't see that from me. As long as my shoulders are broad enough to defend my players, I'll keep doing this job. When you see me playing the clown to offload blame, it'll mean I'm finished."

ROME, ITALY – AUGUST 30: Daniele De Rossi, Head Coach of Genoa, looks on before the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Genoa CFC at Stadio Olimpico on August 30, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

His approach from here is to treat it as a fresh start.

"I have very clear ideas. It makes no sense to look back now. With my staff we've decided to think we've just taken over. We're trying to eat the chicken with our hands. I have to work out how. We can't wait to start again after the break."

On Stephan El Shaarawy, De Rossi urged patience. "He's spent his whole career out wide and we took him to fill the gap there. We have to understand there's a fitness issue too, it's understandable that he's a bit behind."

He also gave an update on Lorenzo Colombo. "Watching the video, the injury looked frightening. I thought everything had gone with his leg planted in the ground." On teenager Robinho Junior, he was more upbeat: "He made an excellent impression on me."

title: Verstappen wins chaotic Sepang race but Antonelli still smiling
description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a turbulent Bahrain Grand Prix held in Malaysia on Sunday, withstanding bad weather, technical issues and being overtaken off the grid to record his first victory of the Formula One season. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes finished second and was boosted in the overall standings by team-mate George Russell having to retire from the race late on when sitting third.
fullText:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a turbulent Bahrain Grand Prix held in Malaysia on Sunday, withstanding bad weather, technical issues and being overtaken off the grid to record his first victory of the Formula One season.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes finished second and was boosted in the overall standings by team-mate George Russell having to retire from the race late on when sitting third. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton took third instead.

Antonelli now leads nearest rival Russell by 84 points. Seven scheduled races remain, although the season-ending Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix in November and December are under threat from the continuing situation in the Middle East and one of them could be dropped.

The Bahrain event, already postponed from April and then moved to Malaysia because of conflict in the Middle East, started over 90 minutes late due to heavy rain and software issues in Sepang.

Verstappen was on pole for the only time so far this season and his hopes of a first win since Abu Dhabi in December last year initially looked like they had evaporated - just like the rain on the drying track. But the Dutchman had other ideas.

"I'm incredibly proud of everyone. It was very hectic, with a lot of different things," Verstappen said after his 72nd career win in F1. "We kept it all under control."

The race began in the pits due to the weather and there were two laps behind the safety car before a standing start from the grid. Verstappen had a bad restart, allowing Antonelli and Russell to get past the four-time champion, who later retook second from the Briton.

The safety car came out again on lap 9 after an accident for Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas. The top cars pitted to remove intermediate tyres with the track no longer wet and Verstappen soon took the chance to overtake Antonelli and seize the lead again.

Russell - winner last time out in Baku - passed Antonelli too as the Italian, looking for a maiden championship aged 20, suddenly looked exposed. The Mercedes duo later switched places again though when Antonelli pounced halfway through the race.

There was a further twist 10 laps from the end when Verstappen pitted during a virtual safety car phase after Williams' Alex Albon went off. Antonelli was briefly in the lead, but Mercedes decided he had to pit too before the full safety car was brought out.

Russell's Mercedes came to a halt before full racing was again permitted. With the field bunched, Verstappen clung on with Antonelli just behind.

Antonelli said: "I think today was the maximum we could have done, massive congrats to Max and Red Bull for their incredible weekend. On our side, work to do but happy to come away with P2."

Red Bull have struggled all season, but the updates brought to Malaysia have done the trick. Verstappen's improvement comes too late for his world title hopes but adds another dynamic to the final months of the season.

The software problems which affected teams during the formation lap appeared to be linked to faulty wet weather settings given races this year in radically rebuilt cars have mainly been dry.

Ferrari seemed to be affected more than others and there was initial confusion about the starting places given cars were mixed up on the formation lap as some came to a crawl.

Officials agreed the original starting spots should count and Hamilton eventually profited, but only after recovering from a wrong tyre choice at the start.

He charged up the field to finish third ahead of team-mate Charles Leclerc, who also battled back from way down the field after early problems and a collision to place fourth.

Isack Hadjar was fifth in the second Red Bull and McLaren's Oscar Piastri sixth. Liam Lawson of Racing Bulls, Fernando Alonso in the Aston Martin, McLaren's world champion Lando Norris and Arvid Lindblad in the other Racing Bulls car rounded out the top 10.

Bahrain sent the trophy to Malaysia and its own marshals, one of whom entertained the crowd during the long rain delay by impersonating Harry Potter with his sweeping broom.

The Singapore Grand Prix is next weekend.

title: Arsenal 2027/28 third kit set for return to black
description: Arsenal’s third kit for the 2027/28 season is set to be black, meaning we now know the base colours of all three shirts for the next campaign.Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesFooty Headlines reports...
fullText:
Footy Headlines reports that Arsenal's 2027/28 third kit will be black, with a design aimed at lifestyle wear outside of football contexts.

The same source adds that we don't currently have official confirmation of the accent colours to combine with the black, but Footy Headlines expect the dark base to be paired with gold detailing.

Should that be the case, it may turn out looking relatively similar to the away kit in the 2022/23 campaign.

Details of Arsenal's home and away kits for 2027/28 had already leaked in recent weeks, as well as a planned change in sponsorship branding.

On the home kit, Arsenal are set to wear a pinstriped design in the usual red and white, with the kit also utilising navy details. There's also speculation that the Adidas stripes on the shoulders will be in navy blue, although that detail hasn't been confirmed.

On the away, reports suggests the shirt will be predominately white or off-white with an elegant green or mint green for logos and details.

The away kit is also set to use the classic Adidas Trefoil logo, the cannon crest instead of the Arsenal badge, green shorts, and white socks (with green as an alternative option), and it will incorporate a subtle tonal jacquard or debossed pattern woven into the shirt.

As for the branding, the front-of-shirt sponsorship logo will just read 'Emirates', rather than 'Fly Emirates' or 'Emirates – Fly Better'.

It will likely be a while before we get our first proper look at the new shirts, but the colour scheme of the three new kits is now becoming clear.

title: Arsenal get special Fabregas option under Como agreement
description: Cesc Fabregas has a special clause in his Como contract for his former clubs, including Arsenal according to reports.Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty ImagesPortuguese outlet A Bola report that former A...
fullText:
Portuguese outlet A Bola report that former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas has a special clause in his contract for three of the clubs he previously represented as a player.

According to the claims, Fabregas' deal with Como 1907 includes a release clause that would allow him to join Barcelona, Arsenal, or Chelsea for a fixed amount, without the need for any negotiations.

Barcelona are reportedly keeping an eye on the possibility, and you'd imagine it's only a matter of time before Chelsea are changing managers again. Arsenal are perhaps a tougher sell, considering recent reports of an extention for Mikel Arteta.

Gianluca Di Marzio (via Marca) confirms that Fabregas has a clause in his contract that allows him to leave under special 'very affordable' conditions, should Barcelona, Arsenal or Chelsea make a move.

Marca add that Fabregas is currently happy at Como, and there's no suggestion he's preparing to leave. The manager reportedly rejected several offers to do so over the summer, though none of them were from the three clubs in question.

Assuming none of the three clubs in question make a move for Fabregas, he has a contract with Como until 2028. The midfielder's only other former club as a senior professional were AS Monaco, but it seems they didn't make the list.

title: Liverpool will offload struggling forward: Three clubs want January deal
description: Liverpool strengthened their attack with a couple of new forwards in the summer transfer window. Victor Munoz was onboarded after the Reds triggered the FIFA World Cup winner’s £34m Osasuna release...
fullText:
Liverpool strengthened their attack with a couple of new forwards in the summer transfer window.

Victor Munoz was onboarded after the Reds triggered the FIFA World Cup winner's £34m Osasuna release clause.

And Andoni Iraola also reeled in Bradley Barcola in the closing stages of the window - with the France international arriving for a fee that could reach £123m.

Those signings will no doubt have an impact on forwards already on the books.

One such performer would be Federico Chiesa. The Italian, who turns 29 this month, finds himself well down the pecking order under Iraola this term.

Chiesa hasn't yet managed to make it into a single matchday squad under the Basque tactico having suffered an injury in a preseason friendly against Como.

Under contract until 2028 it has been speculated for a long time that the Euro 2020 winner would be heading back to Serie A. His wages - thought to be around £150k per week - are prohibitive for Italian sides while Liverpool are also insisting on a fee.

That has not stopped speculation ahead of the January transfer window however with three Italian top-flight sides now tracking Chiesa.

According to a report in Calciomercato Chiesa is wanted by champions Inter Milan as well as Lazio and Atalanta.

Describing Chiesa as a "struggling" Liverpool forward the report suggests that the versatile forward views a move back to Serie A as crucial to regaining his place in the national team.

"Federico Chiesa could return to Serie A during the winter transfer window, as the attacking winger continues to struggle to find a place at Liverpool," the report reads.

"Now in his third season in England, Federico Chiesa is ready to return to Serie A to try to find the consistency that could earn him a return to the national team in 2027.

"There are currently no concrete negotiations for the player, but Inter, Atalanta, and Lazio are closely monitoring the situation and could make an attempt for the former Juventus player during the winter transfer window."

Inter came close to landing Chiesa as an alternative to Luis Henrique during the summer window but ultimately the deal fell down.

Chiesa is currently miles off making it under Iraola - with younger players such as Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas now staking a claim for minutes on a more regular basis than the man signed in 2024 for £12.5m from Juventus.

title: Bhayshul Tuten Fantasy Week 4 Start or Sit: A Defined Hierarchy Makes Him an RB2
description: Jacksonville goes into Cincinnati with Tuten 18th among running backs in PFN’s Week 4 rankings, riding consecutive games with a score and three straight with a 15-plus-yard gain. This was labeled a committee entering the season, and while two players are getting work, the hierarchy is very defined, which keeps him in the RB2 conversation until proven otherwise.
fullText:
Jacksonville goes into Cincinnati with Tuten 18th among running backs in PFN's Week 4 rankings, riding consecutive games with a score and three straight with a 15-plus-yard gain. This was labeled a committee entering the season, and while two players are getting work, the hierarchy is very defined, which keeps him in the RB2 conversation until proven otherwise. The Jags ran 24 times for 126 yards in Cincinnati last season, and Jaylen Warren's 176 yards on 20 touches showed again last week how a team can control pace against the Bengals. I expect Jacksonville to dictate this one in a similar way, and I like getting a little creative with Tuten.

That's consecutive weeks with a score and three straight with a 15-plus-yard gain. Entering this season, the Jacksonville one was labeled as a committee, and while there are two players getting work, there is a very defined hierarchy here, and that puts Tuten firmly in the RB2 conversation week in and week out until proven otherwise.

Passing volume remains the biggest concern. Hurts has thrown exactly 25 passes in two of Philadelphia's three games, a relatively low number in the current NFL environment. His interception and sack rates are also higher than they were last season, creating a little more downside when the rushing production doesn't carry the fantasy line.

title: Real Madrid boss keeping a close tab on new signing amid strong performances for RM Castilla
description: Among all the signings Real Madrid made in the summer, Sergio Martinez’s name went under the radar the most.The youngster joined RM Castilla for a fee of €3 million following an excellent stint at...
fullText:
Among all the signings Real Madrid made in the summer, Sergio Martinez's name went under the radar the most.

The youngster joined RM Castilla for a fee of €3 million following an excellent stint at Racing Santander, which had made him one of the most sought-after young footballers in Spain.

Almost two months into the new season, Martinez has been performing well for RM Castilla and is starting to catch the eye of Jose Mourinho.

Jose Mourinho is constantly keeping an eye on Martinez. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

According to Diario AS, the Real Madrid manager has firmly kept his sights on Sergio Martinez, a midfielder with a tremendous amount of potential.

The ongoing international break has given Mourinho more time to keep an eye on the youngster, as he was present in RM Castilla's recent victory over Atletico Madrileno at the Alfredo Di Stefano Stadium on Friday.

Although it wasn't the best of performances from Martinez, it is firm reminder that Mourinho is very keen on observing the progress of the Spaniard.

Martinez had earlier impressed the former AS Roma manager in the Under-20 Intercontinental Cup at the Bernabeu, in front of 50,000 people.

Sergio Martinez has shown real promise so far. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

As far as the first-team is concerned, Martinez has yet to make his debut for Real Madrid, even though he was involved in two league matches at the start of the season when he was still at Racing.

Given that he had already scored in his debut La Liga game, one would expect Martinez to be frustrated at the lack of opportunities at Real Madrid.

However, the player must remain patient. He has already strong qualities at RM Castilla and has a playing style similar to Toni Kroos, something the club have been lacking for years now.

Real Madrid's current midfield is also far from perfect and Mourinho has been yearning for someone who can control the game in the middle of the park.

Sergio Martinez has the quality to become that solution in the Los Blancos midfield. But he must wait for his breakthrough, knowing that even a minor injury crisis could force Mourinho to try him out soon in the first-team.

fullText:
French national team coach Zinédine Zidane has singled out Bayern Munich's Michael Olise for praise during the international break.

"He's a bit reserved and shy off the pitch, but that's fine because on the pitch he's not shy at all," said Zidane, speaking to Téléfoot TF1.

"He's a natural leader with his game that he brings [to the French team]. He's also showing all his talent with the ball.

"He has established himself here for a while and is doing very well at his club," the 54-year-old head coach explained.

On Friday night, Olise produced a stunning goal from a freekick before France were pegged back and held to a 1-1 draw by Italy.

Later this evening, Les Bleus host Belgium at the Stade de France in Paris, with Olise likely to play a key role for Zidane's side yet again.

title: Elfyn Evans suffers puncture ahead of Power Stage WRC title decider
description: The drama sets up a thrilling final power stage of the season
fullText:
The battle for the 2026 World Rally Championship title will be decided on the final Rally Italy Sardinia Power Stage after Elfyn Evans suffered a puncture in the penultimate stage.

The championship leader was forced to stop on stage 16 to change a front-right wheel in what proved to be a late twist as the title battle seemed to swing further towards rally leader Oliver Solberg. It is the second rally in a row that Evans has suffered a puncture in the penultimate stage after suffering a similar fate in Chile.

"We could see it coming a long way back, it was a very fast corner with a lot of stones," said Evans. I eased the speed right off and went as clean as I could through it… yeah. Can always count on these [tyres]

"We'll try [on the Power Stage]."

Evans started Sunday with a six-point lead over rally leader Solberg but that was soon whittled down to three. Rally leader Solberg continued his impressive pace to top the Super Sunday standings, which offers a bonus five points, with Evans sitting in fourth that would earn two points.

However, the puncture in stage 16 wiped out any chance of Super Sunday points for Evans, reducing the gap between the title rivals to one point in Evans' favour heading into the final stage.

With Solberg on course to take a third win of the year and topping Super Sunday by 8.7s, he is set to win the title on countback if he ends the rally level on points.

It has created quite an incredible final-stage decider where, if Evans beats Solberg he is world champion and vice versa if Solberg is quicker than Evans on the 7.1km Sassari - Argentiera stage later this afternoon.

"Wow so easy," Solberg said sarcastically when he was told that he only needs to beat Evans in the Power Stage to be world champion.

"We'll do our very best to the end. On the first pass we had a clear disadvantage starting in the back, hopefully it's not the same in the Power Stage. Maybe I wish it was a more normal stage, but anyway I will fight. All in."
